avoir.tr: There will never be a day when I do not feel grief for you.

avoir.of: N'en avrai ja ki sustienget m'onur;
avoir.tr: I will never have anyone to uphold my honor;

avoir.of: Suz ciel ne quid aveir ami un sul!
avoir.tr: Under heaven I do not think I have a single friend!

avoir.of: Se jo ai parenz, n'en i ad nul si proz.»
avoir.tr: If I have kinsmen, there is not one so valiant.»

avoir.of: Cent milie Franc en unt si grant dulur
avoir.tr: A hundred thousand Franks feel such great grief over it

avoir.of: N'en i ad cel ki durement ne plurt. AOI.
avoir.tr: That there is not one of them who does not weep bitterly. AOI.

avoir.of: Si grant doel ai que jo ne vuldreie estre!»
avoir.tr: I have such great grief that I would not wish to be!»

avoir.of: «Ami Rollant, de tei ait Deus mercit!
avoir.tr: «Dear Roland, may God have mercy on you!

avoir.of: Ki tei ad mort France ad mis en exill.
avoir.tr: Whoever has killed you has put France into exile.

avoir.of: Si grant dol ai que ne voldreie vivre,
avoir.tr: I have such great grief that I would not wish to live,

avoir.of: E dist dux Naimes: «Or ad Carles grant ire.» AOI.
avoir.tr: And Duke Naimes says: «Now Charles has great grief.» AOI.

avoir.of: Que cil d'Espaigne en la bataille unt mort;
avoir.tr: Those whom the Spaniards killed in the battle;

avoir.of: Gefreid d'Anjou ad sun greisle sunet.
avoir.tr: Geoffrey of Anjou has sounded his trumpet.

avoir.of: Franceis descendent, Carles l'ad comandet.
avoir.tr: The Franks dismount, Charles has ordered it.

avoir.of: Tuz lur amis qu'il i unt morz truvet,
avoir.tr: All their friends whom they found dead there,

avoir.of: Ad un carne(l)[r] sempres les unt portet.
avoir.tr: At once they have carried them to a charnel house.

avoir.of: Asez i ad evesques e abez,
avoir.tr: There are many bishops and abbots there,

avoir.of: Gaillardement tuz les unt encensez;
avoir.tr: Vigorously they have censed them all;

avoir.of: A grant honor pois les unt enterrez.
avoir.tr: Then with great honor they have buried them.

avoir.of: Sis unt laisez: qu'en fereient il el? AOI.
avoir.tr: They left them: what else would they do? AOI.

avoir.of: Devant sei les ad fait tuz uvrir
avoir.tr: In front of himself he has had them all opened

avoir.of: E puis les cors des barons si unt pris,
avoir.tr: And then they took the bodies of the barons,

avoir.of: En quirs de cerf les seignurs unt mis:
avoir.tr: In stag hides they put the lords:

avoir.of: Encoi verrum se tu as vasselage.« AOI.
avoir.tr: Today we shall see whether you have valor.»

avoir.of: Carles li reis en ad prise sa barbe;
avoir.tr: Charles the king has taken hold of his beard;

avoir.of: Isnelement ad vestue sa brunie,
avoir.tr: Swiftly he has put on his hauberk,

avoir.of: Lacet sun helme, si ad ceinte Joiuse,
avoir.tr: He laces his helmet, and has girded on Joyeuse,

avoir.of: Guarnemenz unt ki ben lor atalente[n]t,
avoir.tr: They have equipment that pleases them well,

avoir.of: Puis sunt muntez e unt grant science.
avoir.tr: Then they have mounted and have great skill.

avoir.of: «En tels vassals deit hom aveir fiance!
avoir.tr: «In such vassals a man ought to have trust!

avoir.of: Apres icels en avrat altretant,
avoir.tr: After these there will be as many again,

avoir.of: Suz cel n'ad gent que Carles ait plus chere,
avoir.tr: Under heaven there is no people that Charles holds dearer,

avoir.of: Treis escheles ad l'emperere Carles.
avoir.tr: Emperor Charles has three divisions.

avoir.of: De tels barons qu'asez unt vasselage:
avoir.tr: From such barons that have plenty of valor:

avoir.of: La quinte eschele unt faite de Normans:
avoir.tr: Have made the fifth division of Normans:

avoir.of: Armes unt beles e bons cevals curanz;
avoir.tr: They have fine arms and good running horses;

avoir.of: Suz ciel n'ad gent ki plus poissent en camp.
avoir.tr: Under heaven there is no people who have more power in the field.

avoir.of: La siste eschele unt faite de Bretuns:
avoir.tr: The sixth division they have made of Bretons:

avoir.of: .XXX. milie chevalers od els unt.
avoir.tr: They have thirty thousand knights with them.

avoir.of: Li emperere ad .VI. escheles faites.
avoir.tr: The emperor has made six divisions.

avoir.of: Chevals unt bons e les armes mult beles.
avoir.tr: They have good horses and very fine arms.

avoir.of: E l'oidme eschele ad Naimes establie:
avoir.tr: And the eighth division Naimes has drawn up:

avoir.of: Chevalers unt plus de .XL. milie;
avoir.tr: They have more than forty thousand knights;

avoir.of: La noefme eschele unt faite de prozdomes
avoir.tr: They have made the ninth division of worthy men

avoir.of: .L. milie chevalers unt par cunte,
avoir.tr: They have fifty thousand knights by count,

avoir.of: Espiez unt forz e les hanstes sunt curtes.
avoir.tr: They have strong spears and the shafts are short;

avoir.of: Cors unt gaillarz e fieres cuntenances,
avoir.tr: They have sturdy bodies and fierce countenances,

avoir.of: Les chefs fluriz e les barbes unt blanches,
avoir.tr: Their heads hoary and their beards white,

avoir.of: Escuz unt genz, de multes cunoisances.
avoir.tr: They have fine shields, with many distinguishing marks.

avoir.of: Seint Piere fut (...), si aveit num Romaine;
avoir.tr: It was Saint Peter's (...), and it had the name Romaine;

avoir.of: Mais de Munjoie iloec out pris eschange. AOI.
avoir.tr: But there it took Munjoie in exchange. AOI.

avoir.of: De la baleine ki en sun cors l'aveit
avoir.tr: From the whale that had him in its body

avoir.of: Cum ad oret, si se drecet en estant,
avoir.tr: When he has prayed, he rises to his feet.

avoir.of: Gent ad le cors, gaillart e ben seant,
avoir.tr: He has a fine body, sturdy and comely,

avoir.of: Desur sa bronie fors ad mise sa barbe.
avoir.tr: Over his hauberk he has placed his beard outside.

avoir.of: En un emplein unt prise lur estage.
avoir.tr: On an open plain they have taken up their camp.

avoir.of: Uns Sulians ki ad dit sun message:
avoir.tr: A Syrian who has delivered his message:

avoir.of: «Veüd avum li orguillus reis Carles.
avoir.tr: «We have seen the proud King Charles.

avoir.of: Fiers sunt si hume, n'unt talent qu'il li faillent.
avoir.tr: His men are fierce, they have no desire to fail him.

avoir.of: Adubez vus, sempres avrez bataille!»
avoir.tr: Arm yourselves, you will soon have battle!»

avoir.of: Par sun orgoill li ad un num truvet:
avoir.tr: Out of his pride he has found a name for it:

avoir.of: Ses chevalers en ad fait escrier.
avoir.tr: He has had his knights cry it out.

avoir.of: La forcheüre ad asez grant li ber,
avoir.tr: The baron has a quite ample trunk,

avoir.of: Gros ad le piz, belement est mollet,
avoir.tr: He has a thick chest, it is finely molded;

avoir.of: Lees les espalles e le vis ad mult cler,
avoir.tr: Broad shoulders and a very bright face;

avoir.of: Deus! quel baron, s'oüst chrestientet!
avoir.tr: God! what a baron, if only he were a Christian!

avoir.of: N'i ad Franceis, si a lui vient juster,
avoir.tr: There is no Frank who, if he comes to joust with him,

avoir.of: Blanche ad la barbe ensement cume flur,
avoir.tr: His beard is white, just like a flower,

avoir.of: Il n'en at mie de Rollant sun nevold:
avoir.tr: He has nothing left of Roland, his nephew:

avoir.of: N'avrat vertut ques tienget cuntre nus.» AOI.
avoir.tr: He will not have the strength to stand against us.» AOI.

avoir.of: S'il m'at nunciet mes mes, li Sulians,
avoir.tr: If my messenger, the Syrian, has reported to me,

avoir.of: .X. escheles en unt faites mult granz.
avoir.tr: They have made ten very large divisions.

avoir.of: Apres icels en i ad ben altretanz:
avoir.tr: After those there are quite as many more:

avoir.of: - «Filz Malpramis,» Baligant li ad dit,
avoir.tr: «Son Malpramis,» Baligant said to him,

avoir.of: «Jo vos otri quanque m'avez ci quis.
avoir.tr: «I grant you whatever you have asked of me here.

avoir.of: Sis filz le siut, ki mult ad grant le cors.
avoir.tr: His son follows him, who has a very large body.

avoir.of: Chevalers unt a merveillus esforz;
avoir.tr: They have knights in marvelous strength;

avoir.of: En la menur .L. milie en out.
avoir.tr: In the smallest there were fifty thousand.

avoir.of: Sur les eschines qu'il unt en mi les dos
avoir.tr: Along the spines that they have in the middle of their backs

avoir.of: Jamais n'avrat el chef corone d'or.»
avoir.tr: Never again will he have a gold crown on his head.»

avoir.of: Durs unt les quirs ensement cume fer:
avoir.tr: They have hides as hard as iron:

avoir.of: Pur ço n'unt soign de elme ne d'osberc;
avoir.tr: For that reason they care nothing for helmet or hauberk;

avoir.of: Li amiralz .X. escheles ad justedes:
avoir.tr: The emir has assembled ten divisions:

avoir.of: «Ki par noz Deus voelt aveir guarison,
avoir.tr: «Whoever wants to have healing through our gods,

avoir.of: Trestut seit fiz, n'i avrat altre dreit.» AOI.
avoir.tr: Let it be wholly certain; there will be no other right.» AOI.

avoir.of: Entr'els nen at ne pui ne val ne tertre,
avoir.tr: Between them there is neither hill nor valley nor mound,

avoir.of: Bataille avrum e aduree e pesme.» AOI.
avoir.tr: We shall have a battle hard and bitter.» AOI.

avoir.of: Les escheles Charlun li ad mustrees:
avoir.tr: He has shown him Charles's battalions:

avoir.of: Desur lur bronies lur barbes unt getees,
avoir.tr: Over their hauberks they have thrown their beards,

avoir.of: Bataille avrum e forte e aduree:
avoir.tr: We shall have a battle strong and hard:

avoir.of: Baligant ad ses cumpaignes trespassees.
avoir.tr: Baligant has outdistanced his companies.

avoir.of: Une raisun lur ad dit e mustree:
avoir.tr: He has spoken a speech to them and set it out:

avoir.of: De sun espiet la hanste en ad branlee;
avoir.tr: He has brandished the shaft of his spear;

avoir.of: Envers Karlun la mure en ad turnee. AOI.
avoir.tr: He has turned its point toward Charles. AOI.

avoir.of: De cels d'Arabe si grant force i par (ar)ad,
avoir.tr: There is such a great force of those of Arabia there,

avoir.of: De la cuntree unt purprises les parz,
avoir.tr: They have occupied the parts of the country,

avoir.of: Ne mes que tant (scue)[cume] l'empereres en ad,
avoir.tr: Except for as much of it as the emperor holds,

avoir.of: Tantes batailles avez faites en camps!
avoir.tr: So many battles you have fought in the field!

avoir.of: S'il unt grant gent, d'iço, seignurs, qui calt?
avoir.tr: If they have a great host, what of it, lords? Who cares?

avoir.of: E Tencendor li (a)ad fait .IIII. salz.
avoir.tr: And Tencendor has made four leaps for him.

avoir.of: L'espiet a or li ad enz el cors mis,
avoir.tr: He has driven the gold-adorned spear into his body,

avoir.of: Carles ad dreit, ne li devom faillir.» AOI.
avoir.tr: Charles is in the right; we must not fail him.» AOI.

avoir.of: Apres li ad la bronie descunfite;
avoir.tr: After that he has undone his hauberk;

avoir.of: Tute l'enseigne li ad enz el cors mise,
avoir.tr: He has put the whole banner into his body,

avoir.of: Carles ad dreit vers la gent [pa]iesnie;
avoir.tr: Charles is in the right against the pagan people;

avoir.of: Deus nus ad mis al plus verai juïse.» AOI.
avoir.tr: God has set us on the truest judgment.» AOI.

avoir.of: «Li mien baron, nurrit vos ai lung tens.
avoir.tr: «My barons, I have nourished you a long time.

avoir.of: Deus! tantes hanstes i ad par mi brisees,
avoir.tr: God! so many spears broken there through the middle,

avoir.of: Plus de cent milie espees i unt traites.
avoir.tr: More than a hundred thousand swords they have drawn.

avoir.of: Tantes batailles avez faites pur mei,
avoir.tr: So many battles you have fought for me,

avoir.of: Ja savez vos cuntre paiens ai dreit.»
avoir.tr: You know well that I am in the right against the pagans.»

avoir.of: Itels .XX. miliers en ad od sei,
avoir.tr: He has with him twenty thousand such men,

avoir.of: N'en i ad cel sa lance n'i empleit;
avoir.tr: There is not one of them who does not drive his lance in there;

avoir.of: Trait ad l'espee, le punt est de cristal,
avoir.tr: He has drawn his sword, whose pommel is of crystal,

avoir.of: Mult ad grant doel Carlemagnes li reis,
avoir.tr: King Charlemagne feels very great grief,

avoir.of: Li empereres li ad dit a cunseill:
avoir.tr: The emperor has said to him in private:

avoir.of: Se jo vif alques, mult grant prod i avreiz.»
avoir.tr: If I live a while, you will gain great profit from it.»

avoir.of: N'i ad celoi que n'i fierge o n'i capleit. AOI.
avoir.tr: There is no one there who does not strike or hack. AOI.

avoir.of: Puis ad ocis Gebuin e Lorain,
avoir.tr: Then he has killed Gebuin and Lorain,

avoir.of: Ferez, baron, nus i avom guarant!» AOI.
avoir.tr: Strike, barons, we have a protector in her!» AOI.

avoir.of: E li Franceis n'unt talent que s'en algent;
avoir.tr: And the Franks have no wish to leave;

avoir.of: Des francs barons i ad mult gran damage.
avoir.tr: And among the noble barons there is great loss.

avoir.of: Doel i avrat, enceis qu'ele departed. AOI.
avoir.tr: There will be grief before it ends. AOI.

avoir.of: «Mi Damnedeu, jo vos ai mult servit!
avoir.tr: «My Lord Gods, I have served you greatly!

avoir.of: Perdut avez Malpramis vostre fils,
avoir.tr: You have lost Malpramis your son,

avoir.of: Granz ad le cors, ben resenblet marchis;
avoir.tr: He is big of body, and looks very much like a margrave;

avoir.of: Blanc[he] ad la barbe cume flur en avrill.»
avoir.tr: His beard is white as a flower in April.»

avoir.of: Li amiralz en ad le helme enclin,
avoir.tr: The emir has his helmet bowed,

avoir.of: Si grant doel ad sempres quiad murir.
avoir.tr: He has such grief that he thinks he will die at once.

avoir.of: Vostre conseill ai oc evud tuz tens.
avoir.tr: I have always had your counsel.

avoir.of: Avrum nos la victorie del champ?»
avoir.tr: Shall we have the victory of the field?»

avoir.of: Li amiraill ad sa barbe fors mise,
avoir.tr: The emir has let his beard show,

avoir.of: Li quens Oger cuardise n'out unkes;
avoir.tr: Count Oger never had cowardice;

avoir.of: N'i ad icel ki un sul mot respundet:
avoir.tr: There is not one of them who says a single word:

avoir.of: Que il ad tort e Carlemagnes dreit.
avoir.tr: That he is in the wrong and Charlemagne in the right.

avoir.of: Lor enseignes n'i unt mie ubliees:
avoir.tr: They have by no means forgotten their battle cries:

avoir.of: Li amira[l]z «Preciuse!» ad criee,
avoir.tr: The emir has cried «Precieuse!»,

avoir.of: Fraites les unt desuz cez bucles lees.
avoir.tr: They have broken them below the broad bosses.

avoir.of: Mult vassalment unt traites les espees.
avoir.tr: Very valiantly they have drawn their swords.

avoir.of: Mort as (...) mun filz, par le men esciente;
avoir.tr: You have killed (...) my son, to my certain knowledge;

avoir.of: Puis vunt ferir des espees qu'unt ceintes. AOI.
avoir.tr: Then they go to strike with the swords they have girded on. AOI.

avoir.of: Desur la teste li ad frait e fendut;
avoir.tr: Above, he has broken and split his head;

avoir.of: N'en ad poür ne de murir dutance;
avoir.tr: He has no fear and no dread of dying;

avoir.of: Ordres nen unt ne en lor chefs corones.
avoir.tr: They have no orders, nor tonsures on their heads.

avoir.of: E Carles ad sa bataille vencue.
avoir.tr: And Charles has won his battle.

avoir.of: De Sarraguce ad la porte abatue:
avoir.tr: He has broken down the gate of Saragossa:

avoir.of: E Bramidonie les turs li ad rendues:
avoir.tr: And Bramimonde has surrendered the towers to him:

avoir.of: Li emperere ad Sarraguce prise.
avoir.tr: The emperor has taken Saragossa.

avoir.of: S'or i ad cel qui Carles cuntredie voillet,
avoir.tr: If there is anyone there who wishes to oppose Charles,

avoir.of: Mais n'ad talent que li facet se bien nun.
avoir.tr: But he has no wish to do her anything but good.

avoir.of: Entresque a Blaive ad cunduit sun nevold
avoir.tr: As far as Blaye he has escorted his nephew

avoir.of: Carles en ad e dulor e pesance,
avoir.tr: Charles has both sorrow and grief over it,

avoir.of: Sempres est morte, Deus ait mercit de l'anme!
avoir.tr: At once she is dead; God have mercy on her soul!

avoir.of: Pited en ad, sin pluret l'emperere;
avoir.tr: He has pity for her, and the emperor weeps for it;

avoir.of: Prent la as mains, si l'en ad relevee.
avoir.tr: He takes her by the hands, and so has raised her up.

avoir.of: Desur l(es)[']espalles ad la teste clinee.
avoir.tr: Upon her shoulders she has her head bowed.

avoir.of: Quant Carles veit que morte l'ad truvee,
avoir.tr: When Charles sees that he has found her dead,

avoir.of: Quatre cuntesses sempres i ad mandees.
avoir.tr: He has summoned four countesses at once.

avoir.of: Mult grant honor i ad li reis dunee, AOI.
avoir.tr: The king has given her very great honor there. AOI.

avoir.of: A un estache l'unt atachet cil serf,
avoir.tr: To a stake those serfs have tied him,

avoir.of: N'ad deservit que altre ben i ait;
avoir.tr: He has not deserved to have any other good there;

avoir.of: De Guenelun, ki traïsun ad faite.
avoir.tr: Of Ganelon, who has committed treason.

avoir.of: Li emperere devant sei l'ad fait traire. AOI.
avoir.tr: The emperor has had him dragged before him. AOI.

avoir.of: Les .XII. pers ad traït por aveir.»
avoir.tr: The twelve peers he has betrayed for gain.»

avoir.of: Cors ad gaillard, el vis gente color;
avoir.tr: He has a sturdy body, a noble color in his face;

avoir.of: Venget m'en sui, mais n'i ad traïsun.»
avoir.tr: I have avenged myself, but there is no treason in it.»

avoir.of: De ses parenz ensemble [od li] i out trente.
avoir.tr: Of his kinsmen, together [with him], there were thirty.

avoir.of: Un en i ad a qui li altre entendent:
avoir.tr: There is one among them to whom the others listen:

avoir.of: N'i ad Frances ki vos juget a pendre,
avoir.tr: There is no Frank who will judge you to hang,

avoir.of: Asez i ad Alemans e tTiedeis.
avoir.tr: There are plenty of Germans and Teutons.

avoir.of: N'en i ad celoi nel graant e otreit,
avoir.tr: There is no one who does not grant and agree to it,

avoir.of: Al doel qu'il ad si se cleimet caitifs.
avoir.tr: In the grief he has, he calls himself wretched.

avoir.of: Heingre out le cors e graisle e eschewid,
avoir.tr: He had a lean body, slender and slim,

avoir.of: Curteisement a l'emperere ad dit:
avoir.tr: Courteously he said to the emperor:

avoir.of: Ja savez vos, que mult vos ai servit;
avoir.tr: You well know that I have served you greatly;

avoir.of: Se or ad parent ki m'en voeille desmentir,
avoir.tr: If now he has a kinsman who wishes to give me the lie on it,

avoir.of: A ceste espee, que jo ai ceinte ici,
avoir.tr: With this sword that I have girded here,

avoir.of: Respundent Franc: «Or avez vos ben dit.»
avoir.tr: The Franks answer: «Now you have spoken well.»

avoir.of: Qu'il fiert a colp, de sun tens n'i ad mais.
avoir.tr: For when he strikes a blow, there is none beyond him in his time.

avoir.of: Car cumandez, que tel noise n'i ait!
avoir.tr: So command that there be no such uproar here!

avoir.of: Ci vei Tierri, ki jugement ad fait.
avoir.tr: Here I see Thierry, who has pronounced judgment.

avoir.of: Sun destre guant en ad presentet Carle.
avoir.tr: His right glove he has presented to Charles.

avoir.of: Lur esperuns unt en lor piez calcez,
avoir.tr: Their spurs they have put on their feet,

avoir.of: Lur helmes clers unt fermez en lor chefs,
avoir.tr: Their bright helmets they have laced on their heads,

avoir.of: En lur puinz destres unt lur trenchanz espiez;
avoir.tr: In their right fists they have their sharp spears;

avoir.of: Qui pur Rollant de Tierri unt pitiet.
avoir.tr: Who for Roland's sake have pity on Thierry.

avoir.of: Li uns requiert l'altre, n'unt mie des destrers.
avoir.tr: Each goes at the other; they have no horses left.

avoir.of: Desur le frunt li ad faite descendre.
avoir.tr: He has made it come down on his forehead.

avoir.of: Parmi le vis (li ad faite descendre):
avoir.tr: Through the face (he has made it come down):

avoir.of: La destre joe en ad tute sanglente;
avoir.tr: He has his right cheek all bloody from it;

avoir.of: Jusqu'al nasel li ad frait e fendut,
avoir.tr: Down to the nose-guard he has broken and split it,

avoir.of: Del chef li ad le cervel espandut,
avoir.tr: From the head he has spilled the brain,

avoir.of: Brandit sun colp, si l'ad mort abatut.
avoir.tr: He brandishes his stroke and has struck him down dead.

avoir.of: Escrient Franc: «Deus i ad fait vertut!
avoir.tr: The Franks cry out: «God has wrought a miracle here!

avoir.of: E si parent, ki plaidet unt pur lui.» AOI.
avoir.tr: And his kinsmen, who have pleaded for him.» AOI.

avoir.of: Quant Tierris ad vencue sa bataille,
avoir.tr: When Thierry has won his battle,

avoir.of: Li reis ad pris Tierri entre sa brace,
avoir.tr: The king has taken Thierry in his arms,

avoir.of: [Munter l'unt] fait en une mule d'Arabe;
avoir.tr: They have made him mount an Arabian mule;

avoir.of: «Que me loez de cels qu'ai retenuz?
avoir.tr: «What do you advise me about those I have kept back?

avoir.of: .XXX. en i ad d'icels ki sunt pendut.
avoir.tr: Thirty of them there are who are hanged.

avoir.of: Sor tuit li altre l'unt otriet li Franc
avoir.tr: Above all the others, the Franks have agreed

avoir.of: Quant li empereres ad faite sa venjance,
avoir.tr: When the emperor has taken his vengeance,

avoir.of: «En ma maisun ad une caitive franche.
avoir.tr: «In my house there is a noble captive woman.

avoir.of: Tant ad oït e sermuns e essamples,
avoir.tr: She has heard so many sermons and examples,

avoir.of: Baptizez la, pur quei Deus en ait l'anme.»
avoir.tr: Baptize her, so that God may have her soul.»

avoir.of: Truvee li unt le num de Juliane.
avoir.tr: They have found for her the name of Juliana.

avoir.of: Quant l'emperere ad faite sa justise
avoir.tr: When the emperor has done his justice

avoir.of: En Bramidonie ad chrestientet mise,
avoir.tr: He has set Christianity in Bramimonde,

avoir.of: A la citet que paien unt asise:
avoir.tr: In the city that the pagans have besieged:

avouer.of: La vos sivrat, ço dit mis avoez.»
avouer.tr: there he will follow you, so says my lord.»

bailler.tr: The caliph said: «You have served us ill,

bailler.of: «Carle me mandet, ki France ad en baillie,
bailler.tr: «Charles, who has France in his keeping, commands me,

bailler.of: Il nen est dreiz que paiens te baillisent;
bailler.tr: It is not right that pagans should hold you;

bailler.of: Carles li dist: «Culvert, mar le baillastes!»
bailler.tr: Charles says to him: «Villain, you handled him badly!»
«Baligant, sire, you have been badly treated today.

baiser.of: Quan l'ot Marsilie, si l'ad baiset el col,
baiser.tr: When Marsile heard this, he kissed him on the neck,

baiser.of: Puis se baiserent es vis e es mentuns.
baiser.tr: Then they kissed each other on the faces and on the chins.

baiser.of: Puis se baiserent es buches e es vis. AOI.
baiser.tr: Then they kissed each other on the mouths and on the faces. AOI.

baiser.of: Par amistiet l'en baisat en la buche,
baiser.tr: In friendship kissed him on the mouth,

baisser.of: Baisset sun chef, si cumencet a penser. AOI.
baisser.tr: he bows his head, and begins to think. AOI.

baisser.of: Paien i baissent lur chefs e lur mentun;
baisser.tr: The pagans lower their heads and their chins;

balayer.of: Jusqu'a la tere si chevoel li balient;
balayer.tr: His hair sweeps down to the ground;

baptiser.of: Baptizet sunt asez plus de .C. milie
baptiser.tr: More than a hundred thousand are baptized,

baptiser.of: Baptizez la, pur quei Deus en ait l'anme.»
baptiser.tr: Baptize her, so that God may have her soul.»
There they baptize the queen of Spain:

battre.of: Les renges li batent josqu'as mains.
battre.tr: The streamers beat down to his hands.

battre.of: Si guarnement sunt tut a or batud;
battre.tr: His trappings are all beaten with gold;

battre.of: Ben le batirent a fuz e a bastuns;
battre.tr: They beat him soundly with rods and with sticks;

battre.of: A l'une main si ad sun piz batud:
battre.tr: With one hand he has beaten his breast:

battre.of: A granz bastuns le batent e defruisent.
battre.tr: With big sticks they beat him and smash him.

battre.of: Tres ben le batent a fuz e a jamelz:
battre.tr: They beat him very well with sticks and with staves:

blesser.of: La gent de France iert blecee e blesmie;
blesser.tr: The host of France will be wounded and bruised;

blesser.of: Si est blecet, ne quit que anme i remaigne.
blesser.tr: He is so wounded, I do not think a soul remains in him.

blâmer.of: De l'algalifes nel devez pas blasmer,
blâmer.tr: Concerning the caliph you must not blame him,

blâmer.of: Que mi parent pur mei seient blasmet
blâmer.tr: That my kinsmen be blamed because of me

blâmer.of: Cil ki la sunt ne funt mie a blasmer.
blâmer.tr: Those who are there are not at all to be blamed.

blâmer.of: Ambure ocit, ki quel blasme ne quil lot.
blâmer.tr: He kills them both, let who will blame or praise it.

blêmir.of: La gent de France iert blecee e blesmie;
blêmir.tr: The host of France will be wounded and bruised;

boire.of: Li miez guariz en unt boüd itant,
boire.tr: Those best protected have swallowed just as much,

bondir.of: Sur tuz les altres bundist li olifant.
bondir.tr: Above all the others the oliphant resounds.

bouillir.of: Desuz le frunt li buillit la cervele.
bouillir.tr: Beneath the forehead his brain boils.

bouter.of: Il les ad prises, en sa hoese les butet, AOI.
bouter.tr: He took them, into his boot he stuffed them, AOI.

bouter.of: En ses granz plaies les pans li ad butet;
bouter.tr: He has pressed the pieces of it into his great wounds;

bouter.of: E Mahumet enz en un fosset butent,
bouter.tr: And Mahumet they throw into a ditch,

braire.of: E humes braire, contre tere murir,
braire.tr: And men cry out and die against the ground,

braire.of: Cil d'Ociant i braient e henissent,
braire.tr: Those of Occiant bray and neigh there,

brandir.of: Quant l'oït Guenes, l'espee en ad branlie;
brandir.tr: When Ganelon heard this, he brandished his sword;

brandir.of: Par tel air l'at estrussee e brandie,
brandir.tr: With such force he wrenched and brandished it,

brandir.of: Enpeint le ben, fait li brandir le cors,
brandir.tr: Drives it home well, makes the body sway,

brandir.of: Empeint le ben, que mort le fait brandir,
brandir.tr: Drives it well in, so that he makes him reel dead,

brandir.of: Brandist sun colp e li Sarrazins chiet;
brandir.tr: He brandishes his blow and the Saracen falls;

brandir.of: Brandist sun colp, si l'ad mort abatut,
brandir.tr: He brandishes his blow, and has struck him dead,

brandir.of: Tient sun espiet, sin fait brandir la hanste,
brandir.tr: He holds his spear, and makes its shaft quiver,

brandir.of: De sun espiet la hanste en ad branlee;
brandir.tr: He has brandished the shaft of his spear;

brandir.of: Brandit sun colp, si l'ad mort abatut.
brandir.tr: He brandishes his stroke and has struck him down dead.

briser.of: Trenchet le piz, si li briset les os,
briser.tr: Slashes his chest, and breaks his bones,

briser.of: En dous meitiez li ad briset le col;
briser.tr: In two halves he has broken his neck;

briser.of: La hanste briset e esclicet josqu'as poinz.
briser.tr: His lance breaks and splinters all the way to his fists.

briser.of: Cruist li acers, ne briset ne n'esgrunie.
briser.tr: The steel grates; it neither breaks nor chips.

briser.of: L'espee cruist, ne fruisset, ne ne brise,
briser.tr: The sword grates; it neither shatters nor breaks,

briser.of: Deus! tantes hanstes i ad par mi brisees,
briser.tr: God! so many spears broken there through the middle,

brocher.of: Sun cheval broche e muntet un lariz,
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse and climbs a hillock,

brocher.of: Brochent ad ait pur le plus tost aler,
brocher.tr: They spur hard to go all the faster,

brocher.of: Sun cheval brochet, laiset curre a esforz,
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse, lets it run at full force,

brocher.of: Le cheval brochet des oriez esperuns,
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse with his golden spurs,

brocher.of: Sun cheval brochet des esperuns d'or fin,
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse with the spurs of fine gold,

brocher.of: Sun cheval (...) brochet, si li laschet la resne,
brocher.tr: Spurs his horse, lets loose the rein,

brocher.of: Le cheval brochet, vait ferir Oliver:
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse, goes to strike Oliver:

brocher.of: Sun cheval brochet, si vait ferir Chernuble:
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse, and goes to strike Chernuble:

brocher.of: Laschent lor reisnes, brochent amdui a ait,
brocher.tr: They slacken their reins, both spur eagerly,

brocher.of: Li arcevesque brochet par tant grant vasselage:
brocher.tr: The archbishop spurs with such great valor:

brocher.of: Brochet le bien, le frein li abandunet,
brocher.tr: He spurs it hard, gives it free rein,

brocher.of: Sun cheval brochet des esperuns d'or mier,
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse with spurs of pure gold,

brocher.of: Brochet le bien des aguz esperuns,
brocher.tr: He spurs it well with sharp spurs,

brocher.of: Sun ceval brochet, si li curt ad esforz;
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse, and rushes at him with all his might;

brocher.of: Laschet la resne, des esperuns le brochet,
brocher.tr: He slackens the rein, spurs it with his spurs,

brocher.of: Sun ceval brochet, ki oït del cuntence.
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse, which heard the dispute.

brocher.of: Le cheval brochet des esperuns d'or mer,
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse with the spurs of pure gold,

brocher.of: Brochent ad ait tant cum durent li port.
brocher.tr: They spur eagerly as far as the passes extend.

brocher.of: Brochet le ben, si vait ferir Bevon,
brocher.tr: spurs it well, and goes to strike Beuve,

brocher.of: Brochet le ben des esperuns a or,
brocher.tr: He spurs it hard with his spurs of gold,

brocher.of: Le cheval brochet, si vient poignant vers lui. AOI.
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse and comes riding toward him. AOI.

brocher.of: Brochet le bien des esperuns d'or fin,
brocher.tr: Spurs it hard with his spurs of fine gold,

brocher.of: Le cheval brochet, li sancs en ist tuz clers,
brocher.tr: He spurs the horse, the clear blood pours out of it,

brocher.of: Des esperons puis brochet le cheval,
brocher.tr: Then with his spurs he spurs his horse,

brocher.of: Brochent a eit; dunc laisent curre Francs:
brocher.tr: Spur at full speed; then the Franks let them run:

brocher.of: Le cheval brochet des esperuns d'or fin,
brocher.tr: He spurs his horse with spurs of fine gold,

brocher.of: Des esporuns ben brochot sun cheval;
brocher.tr: Was spurring his horse hard with his spurs;

brocher.of: Brochent ad eit, lor cevals laissent cure,
brocher.tr: They spur eagerly, let their horses run,

brocher.of: Brochent les bien, tutes les resnes lasquent;
brocher.tr: They spur them well, they slacken all the reins;

bénir.of: E l'arcevesque de Deu les beneïst:
bénir.tr: And the archbishop blessed them in God's name:

bénir.of: Ne lesserat que nos ne beneïsse.» AOI.
bénir.tr: He will not fail to bless us.» AOI.

bénir.of: E beneïst Karlun e France dulce,
bénir.tr: And to bless Charles and sweet France,

bénir.of: Sis beneïst Carles de sa main destre.
bénir.tr: Charles blessed them with his right hand.

bénir.of: E si evesque les eves beneïssent,
bénir.tr: And his bishops bless the waters,

casser.of: Quasset sun elme, si l'unt nasfret el chef,
casser.tr: His helm shattered, and they have wounded him in the head,

casser.of: L'escut li freint, cuntre le coer li quasset,
casser.tr: He breaks his shield, and shatters it against his heart,

casser.of: Tuz lur escuz i fruissent e esquassent,
casser.tr: All their shields they shatter and break there,

ceindre.of: Ceint Murglies, s'espee, a sun costed;
ceindre.tr: He girds Murgleis, his sword, at his side;

ceindre.of: Ceintes espees as punz d'or neielez,
ceindre.tr: Girt with swords with pommels of nielloed gold,

ceindre.of: Healmes lacez e ceintes lur espees,
ceindre.tr: helmets laced and their swords girded,

ceindre.of: Ce dist Chernubles: «Ma bone espee ai ceinte;
ceindre.tr: Chernuble says: «My good sword I have girded on;
They gird on swords of Viennese steel;

ceindre.of: Ma bone espee que ai ceint al costet:
ceindre.tr: My good sword that I have girded at my side:

ceindre.of: Dunc la me ceinst li gentilz reis, li magnes.
ceindre.tr: Then the noble king, the great one, girded me with you.

ceindre.of: Ceinte Joiuse, unches ne fut sa per,
ceindre.tr: Girded Joyeuse, whose equal never was,

ceindre.of: Lacet sun helme, si ad ceinte Joiuse,
ceindre.tr: He laces his helmet, and has girded on Joyeuse,
Swords girded, French ones and Spanish ones;

ceindre.of: Puis ceint s'espee al senestre costet.
ceindre.tr: Then girds his sword at his left side.

ceindre.of: Puis vunt ferir des espees qu'unt ceintes. AOI.
ceindre.tr: Then they go to strike with the swords they have girded on. AOI.

ceindre.of: A ceste espee, que jo ai ceinte ici,
ceindre.tr: With this sword that I have girded here,
They gird swords with hilts of pure gold,

celer.of: La traïsun ne poet estre celee;
Cument qu'il seit, ne s'i voelt celer mie.
celer.tr: Whatever may happen, he does not wish to hide at all.

celer.of: Dist Guenelon: «Fel seie se jol ceil!
celer.tr: Ganelon said: «May I be a villain if I conceal it!

cesser.of: Gent paienor ne voelent cesser unkes:
cesser.tr: The pagan people never wish to rest:

chaloir.of: Ne li chalt, sire, de quel mort nus muriuns.
chaloir.tr: Cares not, sire, by what death we may die.

chaloir.of: De ço qui calt? N'en avrunt sucurance.
chaloir.tr: What does it matter? They will have no help from it.

chaloir.of: De ço qui calt? car demuret i unt trop.
chaloir.tr: What does it matter? For they have tarried too long.

chaloir.of: De ço qui calt? car ne lur valt nient.
chaloir.tr: But what use is it? It avails them nothing.

chaloir.of: De ço qui calt? Se fuit s'en est Marsilies,
chaloir.tr: What does it matter? Marsile has fled,

chaloir.of: De ço qui chelt, quant nul n'en respundiet?
chaloir.tr: What does it matter, since no one answers?

chaloir.of: S'il unt grant gent, d'iço, seignurs, qui calt?
chaloir.tr: If they have a great host, what of it, lords? Who cares?

chanceler.of: Sun petit pas s'en turnet cancelant.
chanceler.tr: He sets off at a little pace, staggering.

chanceler.of: Carles cancelet, por poi qu'il n'est caüt;
chanceler.tr: Charles staggers; he has all but fallen;

chanter.of: Que malvaise cançun de nus chantet ne seit!
chanter.tr: So that no evil song be sung about us!

chanter.of: Male chançun n'en deit estre cantee.» AOI.
chanter.tr: Let no evil song be sung about it.» AOI.

chanter.of: Que nuls prozdom malvaisement n'en chant.
chanter.tr: So that no worthy man may sing ill of it.

chanter.of: Tel coronet ne chantat unches messe
chanter.tr: Never did such a tonsured man chant a mass

charger.tr: Four hundred mules laden with gold and silver,

charger.of: Quatre cenz mulz cargez del ór d'Arabe,
charger.tr: Four hundred mules laden with the gold of Arabia,
seven hundred camels, laden with gold and silver,

charger.of: .X. muls cargez del plus fin or d'Arabe;
charger.tr: Ten mules laden with the finest gold of Arabia;

charrier.tr: Fifty carts, that he will have carried away:

charrier.of: Cinquante care, que carier en ferez;
charrier.tr: fifty carts, which you will have carted away;

chausser.of: El destre poign si li faites chalcer.
chausser.tr: And have him put it on his right hand.

chausser.of: Lur esperuns unt en lor piez calcez,
chausser.tr: Their spurs they have put on their feet,

chercher.of: Cercet les vals e si cercet les munz:
chercher.tr: He searches the valleys and he searches the hills:

chercher.of: A mil Franceis funt ben cercer la vile,
chercher.tr: They have the city thoroughly searched by a thousand Franks,

chevaucher.of: Guenes chevalchet suz une olive halte,
chevaucher.tr: Ganelon rides beneath a tall olive tree,

chevaucher.of: Tant chevalcherent Guenes e Blancandrins,
chevaucher.tr: So long did Ganelon and Blancandrin ride together,

chevaucher.of: Tant chevalcherent e veies e chemins,
chevaucher.tr: So long did they ride, both byways and roads,

chevaucher.of: Ne mul ne mule que puissez chevalcher;
chevaucher.tr: Nor mule nor she-mule that you may ride;

chevaucher.of: Vers dulce France chevalchet l'emperere.
chevaucher.tr: Toward sweet France the emperor rides.

chevaucher.of: Paien chevalchent par cez greignurs valees,
chevaucher.tr: The pagans ride through these larger valleys,

chevaucher.of: Li empereres mult fierement chevalchet.
chevaucher.tr: The emperor rides very proudly.

chevaucher.of: Ne mul ne mule que deiet chevalcher,
chevaucher.tr: Nor mule nor she-mule that one ought to ride,

chevaucher.of: Dejuste lui li dux Neimes chevalchet
chevaucher.tr: Beside him Duke Naimes rides

chevaucher.of: Puis si chevalchent, par mult grant cuntençun,
chevaucher.tr: Then they ride forth, with very great striving,

chevaucher.of: Es destrers muntent, si chevalchent estreiz.
chevaucher.tr: They mount their war-horses and ride in close ranks.

chevaucher.of: Felun paien par grant irur chevalchent.
chevaucher.tr: The wicked pagans ride with great fury.

chevaucher.of: Kar chevalchez a quanque vos puez!
chevaucher.tr: So ride on with all the speed you can!

chevaucher.of: Puis si chevalchent, Deus! par si grant fiertet!
chevaucher.tr: Then they ride on, God! with such great fierceness!

chevaucher.of: Tut premereins chevalchet devant l'ost.
chevaucher.tr: First of all he rides out before the host.

chevaucher.of: Li quens Rollant par mi le champ chevalchet,
chevaucher.tr: Count Roland rides through the middle of the field,

chevaucher.of: E Oliver chevalchet par l'estor,
chevaucher.tr: And Oliver rides through the fray,

chevaucher.of: Puis si chevalchet od sa grant ost banie.
chevaucher.tr: Then he rides forth with his great mustered host.

chevaucher.of: Devant chevalchet un Sarrasin, Abisme:
chevaucher.tr: Out in front rides a Saracen, Abisme:

chevaucher.of: Cevalche, rei! Bosuign avum d'aïe!»
chevaucher.tr: Ride, king! We have need of aid!»

chevaucher.of: Car chevalcez! Pur qu'alez arestant?
chevaucher.tr: So ride on! Why do you keep stopping?

chevaucher.of: Li empereres cevalchet par irur
chevaucher.tr: The emperor rides on in wrath

chevaucher.of: Li empereres chevalchet ireement,
chevaucher.tr: The emperor rides on in wrath,

chevaucher.of: Par grant irur chevalchet li reis Charles;
chevaucher.tr: In great wrath rides King Charles;

chevaucher.of: Icil chevalchent fierement e a íre,
chevaucher.tr: These men ride fiercely and with wrath,

chevaucher.of: Ki estre i voelt isnelement chevalzt!
chevaucher.tr: Whoever wants to be there, ride swiftly!

chevaucher.of: Car chevalchez! Vengez ceste dulor!»
chevaucher.tr: So ride! Avenge this grief!»

chevaucher.of: Puis si chevalchet od sa grant ost li ber.
chevaucher.tr: Then the baron rides on with his great host.

chevaucher.of: «Charle, chevalche, car tei ne faudrad clartet!
chevaucher.tr: «Charles, ride, for light will not fail you!

chevaucher.of: Dist Baligant: «Car chevalchez, barun!
chevaucher.tr: Baligant said: «Ride now, barons!

chevaucher.of: Tant chevalcherent que en Sarraguce sunt.
chevaucher.tr: They rode until they are in Saragossa.

chevaucher.of: Eissez des nefs, muntez, si cevalciez!
chevaucher.tr: Come out of the ships, mount, and ride!

chevaucher.of: Si chevalcherent, que fereient il plus?
chevaucher.tr: And they rode on; what more would they do?

chevaucher.of: Tant chevalchat qu'en Sarraguce fut.
chevaucher.tr: He rode so far that he was in Saragossa.

chevaucher.of: Tant chevalchat, qu'il est premers devant,
chevaucher.tr: He rode so far that he is first in front,

chevaucher.of: Puis sunt muntet, par grant vertut chevalchent
chevaucher.tr: Then they are mounted, with great force they ride

chevaucher.of: Veiz Baligant, ki apres tei chevalchet:
chevaucher.tr: See Baligant, who rides after you:

chevaucher.of: Si chevalcez el premer chef devant,
chevaucher.tr: And ride in the first rank, at the head, ahead,

chevaucher.of: Icil chevalchent en guise de baron,
chevaucher.tr: These ride in the manner of barons,

chevaucher.of: Puis si chevalchet mult aficheement.
chevaucher.tr: Then he rides on most eagerly.

chevaucher.of: Mult gentement li emperere chevalchet:
chevaucher.tr: Most nobly the emperor rides:

chevaucher.of: Dist a sun perre: «Sire, car cevalchum!
chevaucher.tr: He says to his father: «Sire, let us ride on!

chevaucher.of: E si cevalcent el premer chef devant,
chevaucher.tr: And they ride in the first van ahead,

chevaucher.of: Li amiraill chevalchet par cez oz.
chevaucher.tr: The emir rides through these hosts.

chevaucher.of: «Karles de France chevalchet cume fols.
chevaucher.tr: «Charles of France rides like a madman.

chevaucher.of: Paien chevalchent en guise de produme. AOI.
chevaucher.tr: The pagans ride in the manner of worthy men. AOI.

chevaucher.of: Des Canelius chevalchent envirun.
chevaucher.tr: They ride around among the Canelius.

chevaucher.of: «Seignurs barons, devant chevalchereiz,
chevaucher.tr: «Lords barons, you will ride in front,

chevaucher.of: Car chevalchez pur la bataille quere!»
chevaucher.tr: Ride on, to seek the battle!»

chevaucher.of: Mult fierement chevalchet li emperere;
chevaucher.tr: Very proudly the emperor rides;

chevaucher.of: Chevalchez, bers! Nul de nus ne vus falt.»
chevaucher.tr: Ride, brave men! Not one of us will fail you.»

chevaucher.of: E Malpramis parmi le camp chevalchet;
chevaucher.tr: And Malpramis rides across the field;

chevaucher.of: «Bel sire Naimes, kar chevalcez od mei!
chevaucher.tr: «Fair lord Naimes, come, ride with me!

chevaucher.of: Li amiralz chevalchet par le camp,
chevaucher.tr: The emir rides across the field,

chevaucher.of: Carles cevalchet e les vals e les munz;
chevaucher.tr: Charles rides over the valleys and the mountains;

chevaucher.of: Tant chevalchat qu'il descent al perrun.
chevaucher.tr: He rode until he dismounts at the mounting-block.

choir.of: Quant le dut prendre, si li caït a tere.
choir.tr: When he had to take it, it fell from him to the ground.

choir.of: Carlles verrat sun grant orguill cadeir;
choir.tr: Charles will see his great pride fall;

choir.of: Qui[d]ás, le guant me caïst en la place,
choir.tr: Did you think the glove would fall to me on the spot,

choir.of: Que il me chedet, cum fist a Guenelun
choir.tr: that it should fall from me, as it happened to Ganelon

choir.of: Pluie n'i chet, rusee n'i adeiset,
choir.tr: No rain falls there, no dew settles there,

choir.of: Ne France dulce ja cheet en viltet!
choir.tr: Nor sweet France ever fall into disgrace!

choir.of: Li paiens chet cuntreval a un quat;
choir.tr: The pagan falls down dead at one blow;

choir.of: E la cervele li chet as piez desuz;
choir.tr: And his brains fall down at his feet;

choir.of: Chiedent i fuildres e menut e suvent,
choir.tr: Thunderbolts fall there, both small and frequent,

choir.of: Brandist sun colp e li Sarrazins chiet;
choir.tr: He brandishes his blow and the Saracen falls;

choir.of: Encuntre tere en cheent les esclaces.
choir.tr: The clots of it fall to the ground.

choir.of: Quel part qu'il alt, ne poet mie chaïr.
choir.tr: Wherever he may go, he cannot fall.

choir.of: Or est grant doel quant l'arcevesque chiet. AOI.
choir.tr: Now there is great sorrow when the archbishop falls. AOI.

choir.of: Voeillet o nun, a tere chet pasmet.
choir.tr: Whether he will or no, he falls to the ground in a swoon.

choir.of: Falt li le coer, si est chaeit avant.
choir.tr: His heart fails him, and he has fallen forward.

choir.of: Sur l'erbe verte si est caeit envers:
choir.tr: On the green grass he has fallen on his back:

choir.of: Caiuz en est li cristals e li ors.»
choir.tr: The crystal and the gold have fallen from it.»

choir.of: Isnelement sur tute sa gent chet.
choir.tr: Swiftly it falls upon all his people.

choir.of: Mais ço ne set liquels abat ne quels chiet.
choir.tr: But he cannot tell which one fells nor which one falls.

choir.of: Chet li as piez, li amiralz la reçut;
choir.tr: She falls at his feet, the emir received her;

choir.of: Sempres caïst, se Deus ne li aidast.
choir.tr: He would at once have fallen, had God not helped him.

choir.of: Sur l'erbe verte le sanc tut cler caeir.
choir.tr: And the bright blood fall on the green grass.

choir.of: Cez chevalers ki dunc veïst caïr
choir.tr: Whoever then might see those knights fall,

choir.of: Baligant veit sun gunfanun cadeir
choir.tr: Baligant sees his gonfalon fall

choir.of: Cheent li rei, a tere se turbecherent,
choir.tr: The kings fall, tumble to the ground,

choir.of: Cheent li clou, si pecerent les bucles;
choir.tr: The nails fall, and they shatter the bosses;

choir.of: Carles cancelet, por poi qu'il n'est caüt;
choir.tr: Charles staggers; he has all but fallen;

choir.of: Pert la culor, chet as piez Carlemagne,
choir.tr: She loses her color, falls at Charlemagne's feet,

choir.of: Les alves turnent, les seles cheent a tere.
choir.tr: The saddle-bows turn, the saddles fall to the ground.

choir.of: Li sancs tuz clers en chiet el pred herbus
choir.tr: The bright blood falls from it onto the grassy meadow.

châtier.of: Vint tresqu'a els, sis prist a castier:
châtier.tr: Came right up to them, and began to rebuke them:

cingler.tr: Before they had sailed four leagues,

cingler.of: Siglent a fort e nagent e guvernent.
cingler.tr: They sail hard, and row, and steer.

clamer.of: Noble vassal vos i solt hom clamer.
clamer.tr: A noble vassal one was wont to call you there.

clamer.of: Clamez vos culpes, si preiez Deu mercit!
clamer.tr: Confess your sins, and pray to God for mercy!

clamer.of: E cil de France le cleiment a guarant.
clamer.tr: And those of France acclaim him as their protector.

clamer.of: Siet el ceval qu'il cleimet Barbamusche,
clamer.tr: He sits on the horse he calls Barbamusche,

clamer.of: N'i ad eschipre quis cleim se par loi nun.
clamer.tr: There is no sailor who does not claim him as his rightful master.

clamer.of: Siet el cheval qu'il cleimet Gramimund,
clamer.tr: He sits on the horse he calls Gramimund,

clamer.of: Siet el ceval qu'il cleimet Salt Perdut:
clamer.tr: He sits on the horse that he calls Salt Perdut:

clamer.of: Siet el cheval que il cleimet Marmorie,
clamer.tr: He sits on the horse that he calls Marmorie,

clamer.of: E cil d'Espaigne s'en cleiment tuit dolent.
clamer.tr: And those of Spain lament over it, all grieving.

clamer.of: Sur sun ceval que cleimet Veillantif.
clamer.tr: Upon his horse that is called Veillantif.

clamer.of: Siet el cheval qu'om cleimet Veillantif,
clamer.tr: He sits on the horse that men call Veillantif,

clamer.of: Cleimet sa culpe, si reguardet amunt,
clamer.tr: He confesses his guilt, and looks up again,

clamer.of: Cleimet sa culpe e menut e suvent;
clamer.tr: He proclaims his guilt, in detail and often;

clamer.of: Cleimet sa culpe, si priet Deu mercit:
clamer.tr: He proclaims his guilt and begs God for mercy:

clamer.of: Trait ses chevels, si se cleimet caitive,
clamer.tr: Tears at her hair and declares herself wretched,

clamer.of: Quite li cleim, se il la voelt aveir,
clamer.tr: I declare it free to him, if he wishes to have it,

clamer.of: Quite vus cleimet d'Espaigne le regnet.»
clamer.tr: He declares the kingdom of Spain quit to you.»

clamer.of: De bachelers que Carles cleimet enfanz.
clamer.tr: Of young men whom Charles calls "children."

clamer.of: Que Guenelun cleimt quite ceste feiz,
clamer.tr: To declare Ganelon free this once,

clamer.of: Que clamez quite le cunte Guenelun,
clamer.tr: To declare Count Ganelon free,

clamer.of: Al doel qu'il ad si se cleimet caitifs.
clamer.tr: In the grief he has, he calls himself wretched.

combattre.of: Puis m'en cumbatre a Carlles e a Franceis?»
combattre.tr: Can I then fight against Charles and the Franks?»

combattre.of: Cumbatrat sei a trestute sa gent,
combattre.tr: He will fight him with all his people,
Furiously it fights with the leopard.
And I will fight the twelve companions.»

combattre.of: Asez est mielz que moerium cumbatant.
combattre.tr: It is much better that we die fighting.
And mighty and a battling vassal.

combattre.of: Unc nel sunast se ne fust (cu)cumbatant.»
combattre.tr: He would never sound it unless he were fighting.»

combattre.of: Sis cumbatirent al bon vassal Rollant;
combattre.tr: And they fought the good vassal Roland;

combattre.of: Ki se cumbat as Sarrazins d'Espaigne;
combattre.tr: Who fights against the Saracens of Spain;

combattre.of: A cels d'Espaigne mult s'i est cumbatuz;
combattre.tr: He fought hard there against those of Spain;

combattre.of: Li quens Rollant genteme[n]t se cumbat,
S'il ne cumbat a cele gent hardie,
combattre.tr: If he does not fight that bold people,

combattre.of: Li reis Marsilie s'i cumbatit, li bers.
combattre.tr: King Marsile fought there, the brave man.

combattre.of: Li emperere, s'il se cumbat od mei,
combattre.tr: The emperor, if he fights with me,

combattre.of: Unc ne vi gent ki si fust cumbatant.
combattre.tr: I never saw a people so warlike.

combattre.of: Mult sereit fols ki [l]a(a) se cumbatreit.»
combattre.tr: He would be very foolish who would fight over it.»

combattre.of: Jo si li fals, od lui m'en cumbatrai.»
combattre.tr: I declare it false, and with him I shall fight over it.»

combattre.of: La vunt sedeir cil kis deivent cumbatre.
combattre.tr: There go to sit those who must fight.

commander.of: N'en parlez mais, se jo nel vos cumant!» AOI.
commander.tr: Speak of it no more, unless I command you to!» AOI.

commander.of: Carles comandet que face sun servise:
commander.tr: Charles commands that I perform his service:

commander.of: Puisquel comant, aler vus en estoet.»
commander.tr: Since I command it, you must go.»

commander.of: Or irez vos certes, quant jol cumant.»
commander.tr: Now you will go indeed, since I command it.»

commander.of: Jointes ses mains iert vostre comandet;
commander.tr: With joined hands he will be at your command;

commander.of: Par penitence les cumandet a ferir.
commander.tr: As penance he commands them to strike.

commander.of: Sil cumandat as cous de sa maisun.
commander.tr: And handed him over to the cooks of his household.

commander.of: Hoi te cumant al Glorius celeste!
commander.tr: Today I commend you to the Glorious One in heaven!

commander.of: Li reis cumandet Gebuin e Otun,
commander.tr: The king commands Gebuin and Otun,

commander.of: Isnelement si li ad comandet:
commander.tr: Swiftly he has commanded him thus:

commander.of: L'empereür li cumandet a guarder.
commander.tr: He commits the emperor to him to guard.

commander.of: Ne deit manger, se jo ne li cumant.
commander.tr: Must not eat unless I command it.

commander.of: Jo vos cumant qu'en Sarraguce algez;
commander.tr: I command you to go to Saragossa;

commander.of: «Jo te cumant de tutes mes oz l'aunde.»
commander.tr: «I entrust to you the command of all my hosts.»

commander.of: En un carne(l)[r] cumandez que hom les port.»
commander.tr: Order that they be carried to a charnel house.»

commander.of: Franceis descendent, Carles l'ad comandet.
commander.tr: The Franks dismount, Charles has ordered it.

commander.of: Li reis cumandet Tedbalt e Gebuin,
commander.tr: The king commands Thibaut and Gebuin,

commander.of: Ço dist li reis: «Seignurs, jo vos cumant,
commander.tr: The king said: «Lords, I command you,

commander.of: Icil cumandet le cunte Nevelun,
commander.tr: He commands Count Nevelon,

commander.of: Francs les cumandent a Deu e a ses nuns.
commander.tr: The Franks commend them to God and to his names.

commander.of: Car cumandez, que tel noise n'i ait!
commander.tr: So command that there be no such uproar here!

commander.of: Li reis cumandet un soen veier, Basbrun:
commander.tr: The king gives orders to one of his bailiffs, Basbrun:

commencer.of: Baisset sun chef, si cumencet a penser. AOI.
commencer.tr: he bows his head, and begins to think. AOI.

commencer.of: Des ore cumencet le cunseill que mal prist. AOI.
commencer.tr: From now begins the counsel that came to ill. AOI.

commencer.of: Mult fierement cumencet sa raisun,
commencer.tr: Very fiercely he begins his speech,

commencer.of: Quant l'ot Rollant, si cumençat a rire. AOI.
commencer.tr: When Roland heard it, he began to laugh. AOI.

commencer.of: Par grant saver cumencet a parler
commencer.tr: With great wisdom he begins to speak,

commencer.of: Puis si cumencet a venir ses tresors. AOI.
commencer.tr: Then he begins to bring forth his treasures. AOI.

commencer.of: Par grant veisdie cumencet a parler,
commencer.tr: With great cunning he begins to speak,

commencer.of: Li arcevesque cumencet la bataille.
commencer.tr: The archbishop begins the battle.

commencer.of: En la grant presse cumencet a ferir.
commencer.tr: In the great press he begins to strike.

commencer.of: Tendrur en out, cumencet a plurer.
commencer.tr: Felt tenderness for it, begins to weep.

commencer.of: Par sun orgoill cumencet mortel rage;
commencer.tr: Through his pride he begins a mortal madness;

commencer.of: A sei meïsme la cumencet a pleindre:
commencer.tr: He begins to lament over it to himself:

commencer.of: Que jo ne fui a l'estur cumencer!»
commencer.tr: That I was not at the beginning of the battle!»

commencer.of: E Baligant cumencet a penser;
commencer.tr: And Baligant begins to ponder;

commencer.of: Des morz qu'il troevet cumencet a plurer.
commencer.tr: At the dead he finds there he begins to weep.

commencer.of: Sa barbe blanche cumencet a detraire,
commencer.tr: He begins to tear his white beard,

commencer.of: Dist Baligant: «Malvais sermun cumences!»
commencer.tr: Baligant said: «You begin an evil sermon!»

commencer.of: Des ore cumencet le plait de Guenelun.
commencer.tr: From now begins the trial of Ganelon.

commencer.of: Des ore cumencet le plait e les noveles
commencer.tr: From now on begin the trial and the news

commencer.of: Quant Guenes veit que ses granz plaiz cumencet,
commencer.tr: When Ganelon sees that his great trial begins,

commencer.of: De lur espees cumencent a capler
commencer.tr: With their swords they begin to hack

commencer.of: Des ore cumencet l'ocisiun des altres.
commencer.tr: From this hour begins the execution of the others.

communier.of: Oent lur messes e sunt acuminiez;
communier.tr: They hear their masses and receive communion;

comparer.of: Einz vos avrunt li meillor comperee.»
comparer.tr: Before the best men shall have paid dearly for you.»

comparer.of: Ki quel cumpert, venuz en sunt ensemble.
comparer.tr: Whoever pays for it, they have come together.

compter.of: Jo ai cunte n'i ad mais que .VII. liwes.
compter.tr: I reckon there are no more than seven leagues.

conduire.of: Ne nus seiuns cunduiz a mendeier.» AOI.
conduire.tr: And that we be reduced to begging.» AOI.

conduire.of: Tanz riches reis cunduit a mendisted:
conduire.tr: So many rich kings has he led to beggary:

conduire.of: Tanz riches reis cunduiz a mendistiet:
conduire.tr: so many rich kings he has brought to beggary:

conduire.of: Ki l'en cunduistrent tresqu'en la mer:
conduire.tr: Who escorted him all the way to the sea:
«I will lead my body into Roncevaux;

conduire.of: Si aiderez a cunduire ma gent.»
conduire.tr: And you will help to conduct my people.»

conduire.of: Lez le costet li conduist sun espiet.
conduire.tr: Along his side his spear passes.
By magic Jupiter led him there.

conduire.of: Cunduit sun cors en la presse des Francs.
conduire.tr: He guides his body into the press of the Franks.

conduire.of: Entresque a Blaive ad cunduit sun nevold
conduire.tr: As far as Blaye he has escorted his nephew

conduire.of: Od .C. serjanz par force les cunduit.
conduire.tr: With a hundred sergeants he leads them by force.

confesser.of: Ben sunt cunfes e asols e seignez:
confesser.tr: They are well confessed and absolved and blessed:

confondre.of: En cest païs nos est venuz cunfundre.
confondre.tr: Has come into this land to destroy us.

confondre.of: Lui e altrui travaillent, e cunfundent.»
confondre.tr: They torment him and others, and bring ruin.»

confondre.of: Li soens orgoilz le devreit ben cunfundre,
confondre.tr: His own pride ought well to bring him to ruin,

confondre.of: Deus me cunfunde, se la geste en desment!
confondre.tr: May God confound me, if I belie my lineage!
Then he cries out: «These are good to destroy!

confondre.of: Cest nostre rei por quei lessas cunfundre?
confondre.tr: Why did you let this king of ours be confounded?

confondre.of: Quant ele vit Arrabiz si cunfundre,
confondre.tr: When she saw the Arabs so confounded,
The pagans are dead, some overwhelmed,

confondre.of: Se uns escapet, morz ies e cunfunduz.»
confondre.tr: If one escapes, you are dead and ruined.»

connaître.of: N'est hom kil veit e conuistre le set
connaître.tr: There is no man who sees him and comes to know him

connaître.of: Mult ad apris ki bien conuist ahan.
connaître.tr: He has learned much who knows hardship well.

connaître.of: Les colps Rollant conut en treis per(r)uns,
connaître.tr: He recognizes Roland's blows on three boulders,

connaître.of: Ben le conuis que gueredun vos en dei
connaître.tr: I know well that I owe you a reward for it,

connaître.of: L'un conuist l'altre as haltes voiz e as cleres;
connaître.tr: Each recognizes the other by their loud and clear voices;

connaître.of: De vasselage te conoissent ti per;
connaître.tr: Your peers know you for valor;

conquérir.of: Tresqu'en la mer cunquist la tere altaigne.
conquérir.tr: he conquered the high land all the way to the sea.

conquérir.of: Jo vos cunquis e Noples e Commibles,
conquérir.tr: I conquered for you both Noples and Commibles,

conquérir.of: Ki cunquist Puille e trestute Calabre;
conquérir.tr: Who conquered Apulia and all of Calabria;

conquérir.of: Ad oes seint Perre en cunquist le chevage:
conquérir.tr: For Saint Peter's use he won from it the tribute:

conquérir.of: Cunquerrat li les teres d'ici qu'en Orient.» AOI.
conquérir.tr: He will conquer lands for them from here to the Orient.» AOI.

conquérir.of: Par tantes teres est alet cunquerant,
conquérir.tr: Through so many lands has he gone conquering,

conquérir.of: Si cunquerrai Durendal od la meie.
conquérir.tr: And I shall conquer Durendal with my own blade.

conquérir.of: A oes Carlon si granz païs cunquis!
conquérir.tr: and for Charles's use conquered such great lands!

conquérir.of: Ço est Gualter, ki cunquist Maelgut,
conquérir.tr: It is Walter, who conquered Maelgut,

conquérir.of: Jo l'en cunquis Namon e Bretaigne,
conquérir.tr: With you I conquered for him Namon and Brittany,

conquérir.of: Si l'en cunquis e Peitou e le Maine;
conquérir.tr: And with you I conquered for him Poitou and Maine too;

conquérir.of: Jo l'en cunquis Normendie la franche,
conquérir.tr: With you I conquered for him Normandy the free,

conquérir.of: Si l'en cunquis Provence e Equitaigne
conquérir.tr: And with you I conquered for him Provence and Aquitaine

conquérir.of: Jo l'en cunquis Baiver e tute Flandres,
conquérir.tr: With you I conquered for him Bavaria and all of Flanders,

conquérir.of: Jo l'en cunquis e Escoce e Vales Islonde,
conquérir.tr: With you I conquered for him Scotland, Wales, and Iceland,

conquérir.of: Cunquis l'en ai païs e teres tantes,
conquérir.tr: I have conquered for him so many lands and countries,

conquérir.of: Mult larges teres de vus avrai cunquises,
conquérir.tr: With you I shall have conquered very broad lands,

conquérir.of: Li gentilz quens, qu'il fut mort cunquerant.
conquérir.tr: Of the noble count, that he died a conqueror.

conquérir.of: De tantes teres cum li bers conquist,
conquérir.tr: The many lands that the baron conquered,

conquérir.of: Cunquis l'avrat d'oi cest jur en un meis.
conquérir.tr: Within a month from this day he will have conquered him.

conquérir.of: «Morz est mis nies, ki tant me fist cunquere.»
conquérir.tr: «Dead is my nephew, who made me conquer so much.»

conquérir.of: Il le cunquist es guez desuz Marsune,
conquérir.tr: He had conquered it at the fords below Marsonne,

conquérir.of: Fors cels de France, ki les regnes cunquerent.
conquérir.tr: Except those of France, who conquered the kingdoms.

conquérir.of: Regnes cunquis e desordenet reis!
conquérir.tr: Kingdoms conquered and kings overthrown!

conseiller.of: Cunseilez mei cume mi savie hume,
conseiller.tr: Counsel me, as my wise men,

conseiller.of: E pur prozdomes tenir e cunseiller,
conseiller.tr: And for upholding worthy men and counselling them,

conseiller.of: Cunse[i]l[l]ez mei e dreit[ure] e honur;
conseiller.tr: Counsel me, and (grant) justice and honor;

conseiller.of: Si hume li lo[d]ent, si li unt cunseillet.
conseiller.tr: His men advise him to it, and have counseled him so.

consentir.of: Dist al paien: «Deus tut mal te consente!
consentir.tr: He said to the pagan: «May God grant you every evil!

consentir.of: Respunt dux Neimes: «E Deus le nos cunsente!» AOI.
consentir.tr: Duke Naimes replies: «May God grant it to us!» AOI.

consentir.of: Par ta mercit, se tei plaist, me cunsent
consentir.tr: By your mercy, if it please you, grant me

conter.of: E Blancandrins, por la raisun cunter.
conter.tr: And Blancandrin, to set forth the matter.

contrarier.of: Pur Deu vos pri, ne vos cuntraliez!
contrarier.tr: For God's sake I pray you, do not quarrel!

contredire.of: En piez se drecet, si li vint cuntredire.
contredire.tr: Rises to his feet, and came to contradict him.

contredire.of: S'or i ad cel qui Carles cuntredie voillet,
contredire.tr: If there is anyone there who wishes to oppose Charles,

convenir.of: Dient Franceis: «Il nus i cuvent guarde!» AOI.
convenir.tr: The Franks say: «We must be on our guard in this!» AOI.

convertir.of: Ço voelt li reis par amur cunvertisset.
convertir.tr: That is the king's wish, that she be converted through love.

corner.of: Ne pur paien, que ja seie cornant!
corner.tr: Nor for any pagan, that I should ever sound the horn!
Roland said: «I will sound the olifant,

corner.of: Se vos cornez, n'ert mie hardement.
corner.tr: If you sound the horn, it will be no act of valor.

corner.of: Jo cornerai, si l'orrat li reis Karles.»
corner.tr: I will sound the horn, and King Charles will hear it.»

corner.of: Pur un sul levre vat tute jur cornant,
corner.tr: For a single hare he goes blowing his horn all day,

corner.of: Rumput est li temples, por ço que il cornat.
corner.tr: His temple is broken, because he blew the horn.

corner.of: Jo oi al corner que guaires ne vivrat.
corner.tr: I hear by the blowing that he will not live long.

corner.of: Seisante milie en i cornent si halt,
corner.tr: Sixty thousand blow them there so loud,

corroyer.tr: Twelve sergeants have well equipped them.

corroyer.of: De guarnemenz se prent a cunreer,
corroyer.tr: He sets about equipping himself with gear,

coucher.of: Sur un perrun de marbre bloi se culchet,
coucher.tr: Upon a block of blue-grey marble he lies down,

coucher.of: Descent a piet, a l[a] tere se culchet,
coucher.tr: He dismounts on foot, lies down on the ground,

coucher.of: Sur l'erbe verte puis l'at suef culchet,
coucher.tr: On the green grass then he has laid him gently,

coucher.of: Sur un escut l'ad as altres culchet,
coucher.tr: Has laid him upon a shield beside the others,

coucher.of: Sur l'erbe verte s'i est culcet adenz,
coucher.tr: On the green grass he has lain down face down,

coucher.of: Culchet sei a tere, si priet Damnedeu
coucher.tr: He lies down on the ground and prays the Lord God

coucher.of: Culchet sei a tere, sin ad Deu graciet.
coucher.tr: Lays himself down on the earth and thanks God for it.

coucher.of: Quant il se drecet, li soleilz est culchet.
coucher.tr: When he rises, the sun has set.

coucher.of: Li emperere s'est culcet en un pret:
coucher.tr: The emperor has lain down in a meadow:

coucher.of: Sur la verte herbe mult laidement se culcet;
coucher.tr: On the green grass he lays himself down most wretchedly;

coucher.of: S'en ma mercit ne se culzt a mes piez
coucher.tr: If he does not throw himself at my feet, at my mercy,

coucher.of: Sur l'erbe verte se est culchet adenz,
coucher.tr: On the green grass he has lain down face first,

coucher.of: Culcez s'est li reis en sa cambre voltice.
coucher.tr: The king has lain down in his vaulted chamber.

courir.of: Plus curt a piet que ne fait un cheval.
courir.tr: He runs faster on foot than a horse does.

courir.of: Curant i vint Margariz de Sibilie;
courir.tr: Margariz of Seville came running there;

courir.of: Sur Veillantif, sun bun cheval curant.
courir.tr: On Veillantif, his good swift horse.

courir.of: Sun cheval brochet, laiset curre a esforz,
courir.tr: He spurs his horse, lets it run at full force,

courir.of: E Anseïs laiset le cheval curre,
courir.tr: And Anseïs lets his horse run,

courir.of: Sun ceval brochet, si li curt ad esforz;
courir.tr: He spurs his horse, and rushes at him with all his might;

courir.of: Beste nen est ki poisset curre a lui.
courir.tr: There is no beast that can run as fast as it.

courir.of: Li val parfunt e les ewes curant.
courir.tr: The valleys deep and the rivers swift-running.

courir.of: Rollant reguardet, puis si li est curut,
courir.tr: He looks at Roland, then runs to him,

courir.of: En Rencesvals ad un ewe curant;
courir.tr: At Roncesvals there is a running stream;

courir.of: Met sei en piez e de curre s'astet.
courir.tr: He gets to his feet and hastens to run.

courir.of: Desuz un pin i est alet curant,
courir.tr: Beneath a pine he has gone running,

courir.of: Ad Apolin (en) curent en une crute,
courir.tr: They run to Apollin, into a crypt,

courir.of: Eschiez e barges e galees curant;
courir.tr: Skiffs and barges and galleys under way;

courir.of: E Bramidonie vient curant cuntre lui;
courir.tr: And Bramimonde comes running toward him;

courir.of: Lascent les resnes a lor cevals curanz,
courir.tr: Loosen the reins to their running horses,

courir.of: Brochent a eit; dunc laisent curre Francs:
courir.tr: Spur at full speed; then the Franks let them run:

courir.of: Brochent ad eit, lor cevals laissent cure,
courir.tr: They spur eagerly, let their horses run,

courir.of: Puint le ceval, laisset curre ad espleit,
courir.tr: He spurs the horse, lets it run at full speed,

courir.of: Li cheval sunt orgoillus e curant;
courir.tr: The horses are proud and running;

courroucer.of: Si li ad dit: «A tort vos curuciez,
courroucer.tr: And said to him: «Wrongly do you grow angry,

couvrir.of: Ki fut cuvert d'une palie alexandrin.
couvrir.tr: Which was covered with an Alexandrian silk.

couvrir.of: Cuverz en sunt li val e les muntaignes
couvrir.tr: The valleys and the mountains are covered with them,

couvrir.of: De tutes parz en sunt cuvert li camp;
couvrir.tr: On all sides the fields are covered with them;

couvrir.of: Bien sunt cuverz d'un palie galazin. AOI.
couvrir.tr: They are well covered with a Galatian silk cloth. AOI.

craindre.of: Jo me crendreie, que vos vos meslisez.
craindre.tr: I would fear that you would come to blows.

craindre.of: Soürs est Carles, que nuls home ne crent.» AOI.
craindre.tr: Charles is secure, for he fears no man.» AOI.

craindre.of: Soürs est Carlles, ne (cre) crent hume vivant.» AOI.
craindre.tr: Charles is secure, he fears no living man.» AOI.

craindre.of: Ja mar crendrez nul hume a mun vivant!» AOI.
craindre.tr: Never, while I live, need you fear any man!» AOI.

craindre.of: Carles ne creint nuls hom ki seit vivant.»
craindre.tr: Charles fears no man who is living.»

craindre.of: Li amiralt, il nel crent ne ne dutet.
craindre.tr: The emir, he neither fears him nor dreads him.

crier.of: Cel nen i ad ki ne criet: «Marsilie!
crier.tr: There is not one who does not cry out: «Marsile!

crier.of: Adubez vos, si criez vostre enseigne,
crier.tr: Arm yourselves, cry out your war-cry,
From it they have their rallying cry, to shout «Munjoie!»;

crier.of: Pluret e criet, mult forment se doluset;
crier.tr: Weeps and cries out, loudly laments;

crier.of: Plurent e crient, demeinent grant dolor,
crier.tr: Weeping and crying out, showing great grief,

crier.of: Li chrestien te recleiment e crient.»
crier.tr: The Christians call on you and cry out.»

croire.of: Il dist al rei: «Ja mar crerez Marsilie.
croire.tr: He said to the king: «It would be folly to trust Marsile.

croire.of: E dist al rei: «Ja mar crerez bricun,
croire.tr: And said to the king: «Never to your harm will you believe a knave,

croire.of: Iert i sis nies, li quens Rollant, (...) ço crei,
croire.tr: There will be his nephew, Count Roland, (...) so I believe,

croire.of: Mort sunt li cunte, se est ki mei en creit.
croire.tr: The counts are dead, if there is anyone who believes me in this.

croire.of: Del rei paien, sire, par veir creez,
croire.tr: Concerning the pagan king, lord, believe in truth,

croire.of: Ne creit en Deu, le filz sainte Marie;
croire.tr: He does not believe in God, the son of holy Mary;

croire.of: Sem(e) creïsez, venuz i fust mi sire;
croire.tr: Had you trusted me, my lord would have come here;

croire.of: Pui li dites, il n'en irat, s'il me creit.»
croire.tr: Then tell him he will not go away, if he believes me.»

croire.of: «Seignors barons, jo vos aim, si vos crei.
croire.tr: «Lord barons, I love you and I trust you.

croire.of: Respunt li dux: «Sire, jo vos en crei.
croire.tr: The duke answers: «Sire, I believe you in this.

croire.of: Puis serf e crei le rei omnipotente!»
croire.tr: Then serve and believe in the all-powerful King!»

croire.of: Li reis creit en Deu, faire voelt sun servise;
croire.tr: The king believes in God, wishes to do his service;
She wishes to believe in God, she asks for Christianity.

croiser.of: Cruisiedes ad ses blanches [mains], les beles.
croiser.tr: He has crossed his white hands, the beautiful ones.

crouler.of: De sun algeir ad la hanste crollee.
crouler.tr: With his javelin he has shaken the shaft.

croître.of: Soleill n'i luist, ne blet n'i poet pas creistre,
croître.tr: The sun does not shine there, nor can grain grow there,

cueillir.of: Rollant sis nies me coillit en haür,
cueillir.tr: Roland, his nephew, took me into hatred,

daigner.of: Vostre olifan, suner vos nel deignastes;
daigner.tr: Your olifant, you did not deign to sound it;
You did not deign to sound your oliphant,

daigner.of: Quant jel vos dis, cumpainz, vos ne deignastes.
daigner.tr: When I told you of it, comrade, you did not deign to.

demander.of: S'est, kil demandet, ne l estoet enseigner.
demander.tr: He is so, whoever seeks him, that there is no need to point him out.

demander.of: Carles respunt: «Tort fait kil me demandet!
demander.tr: Charles replies: «He who asks me does wrong!
Whoever then had heard them call «Munjoie»

demander.of: Que ses cumpainz Rollant li ad tant demandee,
demander.tr: Which his companion Roland had so much asked of him,

demander.of: Cel nen i ad «Munjoie!» ne demant. AOI.
demander.tr: There is not one who does not cry «Munjoie!» AOI.

demander.of: Si li demandet dulcement e suef:
demander.tr: And asks him gently and softly:

demander.of: E en Saisonie fait il ço, qu'il demandet;
demander.tr: And in Saxony he does what he demands;
They will ask: «Where is the captain count?»
The men will come and will ask for news;

demander.of: Puis sunt muntez, la bataille demandent;
demander.tr: Then they are mounted, they demand battle;

demander.of: Dist Malpramis: «Le colp vos en demant.» AOI.
demander.tr: Malpramis says: «I ask the first blow of you for it.» AOI.

demander.of: Meillor vassal de lui ja ne demant.
demander.tr: A better vassal than he I never ask for.
The Franks answer: «You need not ask.

demander.of: Si li demande: «Reis magnes, que fais tu?»
demander.tr: And asks him: «Great king, what are you doing?»

demander.of: Or sunt Franceis a icels qu'il demandent.
demander.tr: Now the Franks are upon those they were seeking.

demander.of: «Soer, cher'amie, de hume mort me demandes.
demander.tr: «Sister, dear friend, you ask me for a dead man.

demander.of: Dist li emper[er]es: «Bons pleges en demant.»
demander.tr: The emperor says: «I ask for good pledges for it.»

demander.of: E puis demandent lur chevals e lur armes.
demander.tr: And then they ask for their horses and their arms.
She wishes to believe in God, she asks for Christianity.

demeurer.of: La noit demurent tresque vint al jur cler.
demeurer.tr: The night they remain until the bright day came.

demeurer.of: De ço qui calt? car demuret i unt trop.
demeurer.tr: What does it matter? For they have tarried too long.

demeurer.of: Demurent trop, n'i poedent estre a tens. AOI.
demeurer.tr: They tarry too long, they cannot be there in time. AOI.

demeurer.of: Morz est li quens, que plus ne se demuret.
demeurer.tr: The count is dead, he lingers no longer.

demeurer.of: La nuit targer e le jur demurer.
demeurer.tr: The night to delay and the day to stay.

demeurer.of: E cil est loinz, si ad mult demuret;
demeurer.tr: And Baligant is far away, and has delayed greatly;

demeurer.of: Si Arrabiz de venir ne demurent,
demeurer.tr: If the Arabs do not delay in coming,

demeurer.of: Li amiralz ne se voelt demurer:
demeurer.tr: The emir does not wish to delay:

demeurer.of: Ço que estre en deit, ne l'alez demurant.»
demeurer.tr: Whatever is to come of it, do not delay it.»

descendre.of: E li message descendirent a pied,
descendre.tr: And the messengers dismounted on foot,

descendre.of: Que en Sarraguce descendent suz un if.
descendre.tr: That in Saragossa they dismount beneath a yew.

descendre.of: N'en descendrat pur malvaises nuveles,
descendre.tr: He will not come down from them for any bad news,

descendre.of: Franceis de[s]cendent, a tere se sunt mis,
descendre.tr: The Franks dismount, they prostrated themselves on the ground,

descendre.of: Nostre Franceis i descendrunt a pied,
descendre.tr: Our Frenchmen will dismount here on foot,

descendre.of: Franceis descendent, si adubent lor cors
descendre.tr: The French dismount, and they equip their bodies

descendre.of: Descent a piet, a l[a] tere se culchet,
descendre.tr: He dismounts on foot, lies down on the ground,

descendre.of: Mil Sarrazins i descendent a piet,
descendre.tr: A thousand Saracens dismount and stand on foot,

descendre.of: Devers la teste sur le quer li descent.
descendre.tr: From his head it descends toward his heart.

descendre.of: Angles del ciel i descendent a lui. AOI.
descendre.tr: Angels from heaven descend to him. AOI.

descendre.of: Sur l'erbe verte descent li reis en un pred,
descendre.tr: The king dismounts onto the green grass in a meadow,

descendre.of: Li gentilz reis descendut est a piet,
descendre.tr: The noble king has dismounted, on foot,

descendre.of: Franceis descendent en la tere deserte,
descendre.tr: The Franks dismount on the deserted land,

descendre.of: Suz un olive est descendut en l'umbre,
descendre.tr: Under an olive tree he has dismounted, in the shade,

descendre.of: Li dui message descendent al perrun.
descendre.tr: The two messengers dismount at the mounting block.

descendre.of: A un perron de marbre est descenduz,
descendre.tr: He dismounted at a marble block,

descendre.of: Par les degrez jus del paleis descent,
descendre.tr: Down the steps, down from the palace he goes,

descendre.of: Li reis descent, si ad rendut ses armes,
descendre.tr: The king dismounts, and has handed over his arms,

descendre.of: Descent a pied, aled i est pleins curs,
descendre.tr: He dismounts, has gone there at full speed,

descendre.of: Franceis descendent, Carles l'ad comandet.
descendre.tr: The Franks dismount, Charles has ordered it.

descendre.of: Par tut le champ cil de France descendent,
descendre.tr: Across the whole field those of France dismount,

descendre.of: Li emperere de sun cheval descent;
descendre.tr: The emperor dismounts from his horse;

descendre.of: Paien descendent pur lur cors aduber.
descendre.tr: The pagans dismount to arm themselves.

descendre.of: Tant chevalchat qu'il descent al perrun.
descendre.tr: He rode until he dismounts at the mounting-block.

descendre.of: Desur le frunt li ad faite descendre.
descendre.tr: He has made it come down on his forehead.

descendre.of: Parmi le vis (li ad faite descendre):
descendre.tr: Through the face (he has made it come down):

descendre.of: Vienent ad Ais, descendent en la place.
descendre.tr: They come to Aix, they dismount in the square.

desservir.of: N'ad deservit que altre ben i ait;
desservir.tr: He has not deserved to have any other good there;

devenir.of: Ne seit ocis, u devient chrestien.
devenir.tr: Who is not slain, or becomes a Christian.
There he will wish to become a Christian.»

devenir.of: Qu'il devendrat jointes ses mains tis hom,
devenir.tr: That he will become, his hands joined, your vassal,

devenir.of: Que est devenuz li Guascuinz Engeler?
devenir.tr: What has become of the Gascon Engelier?

devenir.of: Dist cascun a l'altre: «Caitifs, que devendrum?
devenir.tr: Each says to the other: «Wretches, what will become of us?
What will become of me, sorrowful, wretched?

devenir.of: Deven mes hom, en fedeltet voeill rendre;
devenir.tr: Become my man, I wish you to pay homage;

devoir.of: En France, ad Ais, s'en deit ben repairer.
devoir.tr: To France, to Aix, he ought well to return.

devoir.of: Le glorius, que de[v]u[n]s aürer!
devoir.tr: the glorious, whom we must adore!

devoir.of: En France, ad Ais, devez bien repairer;
devoir.tr: to France, to Aix, you ought rightly to return;

devoir.of: Ceste grant guerre ne deit munter a plus.»
devoir.tr: This great war ought not to mount up to more.»

devoir.of: Mai[s] saives hom, il deit faire message:
devoir.tr: But a wise man, he ought to carry a message:

devoir.of: Quant le dut prendre, si li caït a tere.
devoir.tr: When he had to take it, it fell from him to the ground.

devoir.of: Quant aler dei, n'i ai plus que targer.»
devoir.tr: Since I must depart, there is no more reason for me to tarry.»

devoir.of: Ki ço jugat, que doüsez aler
devoir.tr: He who decreed that you should go

devoir.of: Li quens Rollant nel se doüst penser,
devoir.tr: Count Roland ought not to have thought of it,

devoir.of: Li soens orgoilz le devreit ben cunfundre,
devoir.tr: His own pride ought well to bring him to ruin,

devoir.of: Li Glorius, qui devum aürer!
devoir.tr: The Glorious One, whom we must adore!

devoir.of: Vos le doüssez esculter e oïr.»
devoir.tr: You ought to have listened to him and heard him out.»

devoir.of: De l'algalifes nel devez pas blasmer,
devoir.tr: Concerning the caliph you must not blame him,

devoir.of: «Sire parastre, mult vos dei aveir cher:
devoir.tr: «Lord stepfather, I must hold you dear:

devoir.of: Ne mul ne mule que deiet chevalcher,
devoir.tr: Nor mule nor she-mule that one ought to ride,

devoir.of: «Hom sui Rollant, jo ne li dei faillir.»
devoir.tr: «I am Roland's man, I must not fail him.»

devoir.of: Respunt gualter: «Pur vos le dei ben faire.»
devoir.tr: Gautier replies: «For you I must do it well.»

devoir.of: Ben devuns ci estre pur nostre rei:
devoir.tr: We must indeed stand here for our king:

devoir.of: Pur sun seignor deit hom susfrir destreiz
devoir.tr: For his lord a man should suffer hardships

devoir.of: Sin deit hom perdre e del quir e del peil.
devoir.tr: And a man should lose both hide and hair for it.

devoir.of: Pur sun seignur deit hom susfrir granz mals
devoir.tr: For his lord a man must suffer great hardships

devoir.of: Sin deit hom perdre del sanc e de la char.
devoir.tr: And a man must lose of his blood and of his flesh.

devoir.of: Pur nostre rei devum nus ben murir.
devoir.tr: For our king we must surely die.

devoir.of: Li emperere nos devreit ben venger.
devoir.tr: The emperor ought well to avenge us.

devoir.of: L'enseigne Carle n'i devum ublier.»
devoir.tr: We must not forget Charles's war-cry here.»

devoir.of: Cels ki ci sunt devum aveir mult vil;
devoir.tr: Those who are here we should hold very cheap;
