férir.tr: And the pagan presses hard upon him to strike.

férir.of: Vait le ferir par sun grant vasselage:
férir.tr: He goes to strike him with his great valor:

férir.of: N'i ad celoi que n'i fierge o n'i capleit. AOI.
férir.tr: There is no one there who does not strike or hack. AOI.

férir.of: Si vait ferir le cunte Guneman,
férir.tr: And goes to strike Count Guneman,

férir.of: Ferez, baron, nus i avom guarant!» AOI.
férir.tr: Strike, barons, we have a protector in her!» AOI.

férir.of: De lur espiez ben i fierent e caplent;
férir.tr: With their spears they strike and hack well there;

férir.of: Mult ben i fierent Franceis e Arrabit;
férir.tr: Very well the Franks and the Arabs strike there;

férir.of: S'or n'i ferez pur venger vostre hunte.»
férir.tr: If you do not strike now to avenge your shame.»

férir.of: Vunt les ferir la o il les encuntrent.
férir.tr: They go to strike them wherever they meet them.

férir.of: Mult ben i fiert Carlemagnes li reis, AOI.
férir.tr: Very well King Charlemagne strikes there, AOI.

férir.of: Si vait ferir celui ki le dragun teneit,
férir.tr: And goes to strike the one who held the dragon,

férir.of: Trestut seit fel ki n'i fierget a espleit!» AOI.
férir.tr: Let him be utterly a villain who does not strike hard here!» AOI.

férir.of: Franc e paien i fierent des espees.
férir.tr: Franks and pagans strike there with their swords.

férir.of: Si se vunt ferir, granz colps s'entredunerent
férir.tr: They go to strike one another, they dealt each other great blows

férir.of: Puis fierent il nud a nud sur les bronies;
férir.tr: Then they strike on the hauberks, bare to bare;

férir.of: Puis vunt ferir des espees qu'unt ceintes. AOI.
férir.tr: Then they go to strike with the swords they have girded on. AOI.

férir.of: Fier Carlemagne sur l'elme d'acer brun,
férir.tr: He strikes Charlemagne on the helmet of brown steel,

férir.of: Fiert l'amiraill de l'espee de France,
férir.tr: He strikes the emir with the sword of France,

férir.of: Cascuns i fiert tanz granz colps cum il poet.
férir.tr: Each one strikes there as many great blows as he can.

férir.of: Qu'il fiert a colp, de sun tens n'i ad mais.
férir.tr: For when he strikes a blow, there is none beyond him in his time.

férir.of: Par grant vertut vait ferir l'uns li altre;
férir.tr: With great force each goes to strike the other;

férir.of: Fierent e caplent sur cez helmes d'acer;
férir.tr: They strike and hack at their steel helmets;

férir.of: Si fiert Tierri sur l'elme de Provence:
férir.tr: He strikes Thierry on the helmet of Provence:

férir.of: Ço veit Tierris, que el vis est ferut:
férir.tr: Thierry sees this, that he is struck in the face:

férir.of: Fiert Pinabel sur l'elme d'acer brun,
férir.tr: He strikes Pinabel on the helmet of dark steel,

gager.of: Guaz vos en dreit par cez pels sabelines;
gager.tr: I pledge you amends by these sable furs;

garantir.of: Jo ne vos pois tenser ne guarantir.
garantir.tr: I cannot protect you nor save you.
I will at once warrant my judgment.»

garder.of: Nes poet guarder que mals ne l'i ateignet. AOI.
garder.tr: he cannot keep harm from reaching him there. AOI.

garder.of: Nes poet guarder que alques ne l'engignent. AOI.
garder.tr: He cannot guard against their deceiving him in some way. AOI.

garder.of: Gua[r]dez le ben, ja nel verrai des oilz.»
garder.tr: Guard him well, for I shall never see him again with my eyes.»

garder.of: Guardet al bref, vit la raisun escrite:
garder.tr: He looks at the letter, saw the writing set down there:

garder.of: Guardez de nos ne turnez le curage.
garder.tr: Take care that you do not turn your heart away from us.

garder.of: E .XX. hostages; faites les ben guarder!
garder.tr: And twenty hostages; have them well guarded!

garder.of: Que il ne voelent ne tenir ne guarder.
garder.tr: Which they wish neither to hold nor to keep.

garder.of: Or guart chascuns que granz colps (l')[i] empleit,
garder.tr: Now let each man take care to strike great blows there,

garder.of: Guardet su destre par mi un val herbus,
garder.tr: He looks to his right across a grassy valley,

garder.of: Guardez amunt devers les porz d'Espaigne:
garder.tr: Look up toward the passes of Spain:

garder.of: Traït vos ad ki a guarder vos out.
garder.tr: He who should have guarded you has betrayed you.

garder.of: Guardet a tere, veit gesir le glutun,
garder.tr: He looks to the ground, sees the wretch lying there,

garder.of: Guardet arere, veit le glutun gesir,
garder.tr: He looks behind, sees the wretch lying there,

garder.of: «Ben le me guarde, si cume tel felon!
garder.tr: «Guard him well for me, as befits such a felon!

garder.of: Tant le guardent quel rendent a Charlun.
garder.tr: They guard him until they hand him back to Charles.

garder.of: Guardez, seignurs, qu'il n'en algent vif!
garder.tr: Take care, lords, that they do not get away alive!

garder.of: Guardet aval e si guardet amunt:
garder.tr: He looks down and he looks up:

garder.of: «Guardez le champ e les vals e les munz.
garder.tr: «Guard the field and the valleys and the mountains.

garder.of: L'empereür li cumandet a guarder.
garder.tr: He commits the emperor to him to guard.

garder.of: Carles guardat amunt envers le ciel,
garder.tr: Charles looked up toward the sky,

garder.of: Sálvent le rei e guardent la reïne!»
garder.tr: Save the king and guard the queen!»

garder.of: Sein Gabriel, ki de part Deu le guarde,
garder.tr: Saint Gabriel, who guards him on God's behalf,

garder.of: Guardet a la tere, veit sun nevold gesir.
garder.tr: He looks at the ground, sees his nephew lying there.

garder.of: Guardet a tere, veit gesir sun nev[u]ld:
garder.tr: He looks at the ground, sees his nephew lying there:

garder.of: Guardent la vile a oes l'empereor.
garder.tr: They guard the city for the emperor's use.

garder.of: Fait cels guarder tresque li dreiz en serat. AOI.
garder.tr: He has them kept under guard until justice is done of it. AOI.

garnir.of: Ben sunt guarniz e de chevals e d'armes;
garnir.tr: They are well equipped both with horses and with arms;

garnir.of: De Sarraguce Carles guarnist les turs;
garnir.tr: Charles garrisons the towers of Saragossa;

gemmer.of: Luisent cil elme, ki ad or sunt gemmez,
gemmer.tr: The helmets gleam, which are gemmed with gold,

gemmer.of: La bone sele, ki a ór est gemmee,
gemmer.tr: The good saddle, which is jeweled with gold,

gemmer.of: Sil fiert en l'elme, ki gemmet fut a or:
gemmer.tr: And strikes him on the helmet, which was set with gems in gold:

gemmer.of: Laciet sun elme, ki est a or gemmet,
gemmer.tr: Laced his helmet, which is set with gold and gems,

gemmer.of: Lacet sun elme, ki ad or est gemmet,
gemmer.tr: Laces his helmet, which is set with gems in gold,

gemmer.of: Luisent cil elme as perres d'or gemmees,
gemmer.tr: Those helmets gleam, set with gold gems,

gemmer.of: Desur cez helmes, ki sunt a or gemez;
gemmer.tr: On their helmets, which are gemmed with gold;

glatir.of: Arguille si cume chen i glatissent;
glatir.tr: Those of Arguille yelp there like dogs;

gouverner.of: Siglent a fort e nagent e guvernent.
gouverner.tr: They sail hard, and row, and steer.

gracier.of: Ço dist li reis: «Graciet en seit Deus!
gracier.tr: Thus said the king: «May God be thanked for it!

gracier.of: Culchet sei a tere, sin ad Deu graciet.
gracier.tr: Lays himself down on the earth and thanks God for it.

guerroyer.of: N'avrat talent, que ja mais vus guerreit.» AOI.
guerroyer.tr: He will have no desire ever again to make war on you.» AOI.

guerroyer.of: Cil ne sunt proz ja mais pur guerreier.
guerroyer.tr: They will never again be of use for waging war.

guerroyer.of: En France irai pur Carles guerreier;
guerroyer.tr: I will go to France to wage war on Charles;

guetter.of: La noit la guaitent entresqu'a l 'ajurnee.
guetter.tr: All night they keep watch over her until daybreak.

guider.tr: «At Roncevaux I will lead my company,

guider.of: Ki guierat mes oz a tel poeste,
guider.tr: Who will lead my armies with such power,
«In three carts guide them [...] very well.»
And Gibuin and Guinemant will lead them.»

guider.of: Les guierat, kar la cumpaigne est fiere. AOI.
guider.tr: Will lead them, for the company is fierce. AOI.

guider.of: Sis guierat Hermans li dux de Trace.
guider.tr: Hermann, duke of Thrace, will lead them.

guider.of: Richard li velz les guierat el camp:
guider.tr: Richard the Old will lead them in the field:

guider.of: «Guiez ma gent, jo vos en faz le dun!» AOI.
guider.tr: «Lead my people, I make you a gift of it!» AOI.

guider.of: Els guierat Jozerans e Godselmes. AOI.
guider.tr: Joceran and Godselme will lead them. AOI.

guider.of: Les guierunt tut par chevalerie. AOI.
guider.tr: They will lead them, all in knightly fashion. AOI.

guider.of: Sis guierat Tierris, li dux d'Argone. AOI.
guider.tr: Thierry, duke of Argonne, will lead them. AOI.
And you will lead all my divisions;

guérir.of: Si m(e) guarisez e de mort et de hunte.»
guérir.tr: And save me from death and from shame.»
Charles answers: «He may yet be saved.» AOI.

guérir.of: Par Charlemagne n'er(cs) guariz ne tensez.
guérir.tr: Will not be protected nor defended by Charlemagne.

guérir.of: Asoldrai vos pur voz anmes guarir.
guérir.tr: I shall absolve you to save your souls.

guérir.of: Ja pur Charles n'i ert un sul guarit:
guérir.tr: Never, for all of Charles, shall a single one be saved:

guérir.of: Deus le guarit, qu'el(l) cors ne l'ad tuchet.
guérir.tr: God protects him, for it did not touch his body.

guérir.of: De cent millers n'en poent guarir dous.
guérir.tr: Of a hundred thousand not two of them can escape.

guérir.of: Nel poet guarir sun escut ne sa bronie:
guérir.tr: Neither his shield nor his hauberk can protect him:

guérir.of: E p[ri]ent Deu qu'il guarisset Rollant
guérir.tr: And they pray to God that He keep Roland safe
Recovered and returned from his swoons,

guérir.of: E recreant ki les lerrat guar[ir]!»
guérir.tr: And a coward whoever lets them escape!»
And saved Daniel from the lions,

guérir.of: Guaris de mei l'anme de tuz perilz
guérir.tr: Save my soul from all perils
Pinabel said: «You will be safe soon.

guérir.of: Vostre servise l'en doüst bien guarir!
guérir.tr: Your service ought to have protected him well!

guérir.of: Deus le guarit, que mort ne l'acraventet. AOI.
guérir.tr: God protects him, so that Pinabel does not fell him dead. AOI.

gâter.of: Carles li magnes ad Espaigne guastede
gâter.tr: Charles the Great has laid waste to Spain,

gâter.of: Mort m'ad mes homes, ma tere deguastee,
gâter.tr: Has killed my men, laid my land waste,

gésir.of: Gesir porrum el burc de seint Denise.»
gésir.tr: We shall be able to lie in the town of Saint Denis.»

gésir.of: Guardet a tere, veit gesir le glutun,
gésir.tr: He looks to the ground, sees the wretch lying there,

gésir.of: Guardet arere, veit le glutun gesir,
gésir.tr: He looks behind, sees the wretch lying there,

gésir.of: Li sanc tuz clers gesir par cele place!
gésir.tr: The bright blood lying all over that place!

gésir.of: L'un gist sur l'altre e envers e adenz.
gésir.tr: One lies upon another, both on his back and face down.

gésir.of: Tanz bons vassals veez gesir par tere!
gésir.tr: So many good vassals you see lying upon the ground!

gésir.of: Ne jerrei(e)z ja mais entre sa brace!» AOI.
gésir.tr: You shall never lie in her arms!» AOI.

gésir.of: Desur (...) sa brunie li gist sa blanche barbe.
gésir.tr: Over his hauberk hangs his white beard.

gésir.of: De cels de France i veit tanz morz gesir!
gésir.tr: of those of France he sees so many lying dead!

gésir.of: En seintes flurs il les facet gesir!
gésir.tr: May he make them lie among holy flowers!

gésir.of: Gesir adenz, a la tere sun vis,
gésir.tr: Lying face down, his face to the earth,

gésir.of: La veit gesir le nobilie barun,
gésir.tr: There he sees lying the noble baron,

gésir.of: Defors sun cors veit gesir la buele;
gésir.tr: Outside his body he sees the bowels lie;

gésir.of: Si se feinst mort, si gist entre les altres;
gésir.tr: He feigned himself dead, he lies among the others;

gésir.of: Li quens Rollant se jut desuz un pin;
gésir.tr: Count Roland lay beneath a pine;

gésir.of: Lessez gesir les morz tut issi cun il sunt,
gésir.tr: Let the dead lie just as they are,

gésir.of: Carles se gist, mais doel ad de Rollant
gésir.tr: Charles lies down, but he grieves for Roland

gésir.of: Ki herbe voelt, il la prent en gisant.
gésir.tr: Whoever wants grass takes it lying down.

gésir.of: Il jut anuit sur cel ewe de Sebre:
gésir.tr: He lay tonight on the bank of the Ebro:

gésir.of: Sur l'erbe verte veit gesir sun nevuld;
gésir.tr: He sees his nephew lying on the green grass;

gésir.of: Guardet a la tere, veit sun nevold gesir.
gésir.tr: He looks at the ground, sees his nephew lying there.

gésir.of: Guardet a tere, veit gesir sun nev[u]ld:
gésir.tr: He looks at the ground, sees his nephew lying there:

gésir.of: Par poestet icele noit i jurent.
gésir.tr: By might they lay there that night.

gésir.of: A Seint Romain; la gisent li baron.
gésir.tr: At Saint Romain; there the barons lie.

haïr.of: Suz ciel n'at hume que [tant] voeillet haïr;
haïr.tr: Under heaven there is no man he would so wish to hate;

hennir.of: Cil d'Ociant i braient e henissent,
hennir.tr: Those of Occiant bray and neigh there,

honnir.of: Par quel mesure le poüssum hunir.»
honnir.tr: As to by what means we might dishonor him.»

honnir.of: Franceis murrunt e France en ert hunie;
honnir.tr: The French will die and France will be shamed by it;

honnir.of: Que dulce France par nus ne seit hunie!
honnir.tr: Let sweet France not be dishonored through us!

honnir.of: Deus! Perre, n'en laise(i)t hunir France!»
honnir.tr: God! Father, do not let France be shamed by it!»

hâter.tr: Who urge themselves on to battle, and make haste:

hâter.of: Met sei en piez e de curre s'astet.
hâter.tr: He gets to his feet and hastens to run.

hâter.of: E li paiens de ferir mult le hastet.
hâter.tr: And the pagan presses hard upon him to strike.

héberger.of: Franc se herbergent par tute la cuntree.
héberger.tr: The Franks make camp throughout the countryside.
The emperor says: «It is time to make camp;

héberger.of: Desur la rive sunt Frances herbergiez:
héberger.tr: The French are camped on the riverbank:

incliner.of: Li reis paiens parfundement l 'enclinet. AOI.
incliner.tr: The pagan king bows deeply to him. AOI.

incliner.of: A icel mot l'un a l'altre ad clinet.
incliner.tr: At that word the one bowed to the other.
The two messengers both bowed to him,

incliner.of: Desur l(es)[']espalles ad la teste clinee.
incliner.tr: Upon her shoulders she has her head bowed.

issir.of: Ist de la prese, si se met en bandun,
issir.tr: He springs out of the press and flings himself forward,

issir.of: Fors s'en eissirent li Sarrazins dedenz,
Par les oreilles fors se ist la cervel.
issir.tr: Through the ears his brain comes out.

issir.of: Del sanc qu'en ist se pasmet e angoiset.
issir.tr: From the blood that flows from it he faints and is in anguish.

issir.of: Issent de mer, venent as ewes dulces,
issir.tr: They leave the sea, they come to the fresh waters,

issir.of: Li amiralz est issut del calan:
issir.tr: The emir has come out of the barge:

issir.of: Eissez des nefs, muntez, si cevalciez!
issir.tr: Come out of the ships, mount, and ride!

issir.of: Paien d'Arabe des nefs se sunt eissut,
issir.tr: The pagans of Arabia have come out of the ships,

issir.of: Issent des porz e de la tere guaste,
issir.tr: They come out of the passes and out of the wasted land,

issir.of: Le cheval brochet, li sancs en ist tuz clers,
issir.tr: He spurs the horse, the clear blood pours out of it,

jeter.of: De sun col getet ses grandes pels de martre,
jeter.tr: From his neck he throws his great pelts of marten,

jeter.of: Cuntre dous deie l'ad del furrer getee,
jeter.tr: He drew it two fingers' width out of the scabbard,

jeter.of: Getet le a tere, sil receit Blancandrin;
jeter.tr: He throws it to the ground, and Blancandrin catches it;

jeter.of: Getet serez sur un malvais sumer.
jeter.tr: You will be thrown upon a wretched pack-horse.

jeter.of: Freint le seel, getet en ad la cire,
jeter.tr: He breaks the seal, has cast away the wax,

jeter.of: Od sun espiet l'anme li getet fors,
jeter.tr: With his spear casts out his soul,

jeter.of: Ki lui veïst l'un geter mort su[r] l'altre,
jeter.tr: Whoever had seen him throw one dead upon another,

jeter.of: Osbercs e helmes i getent grant flambur,
jeter.tr: Hauberks and helmets cast forth a great blaze of light,
Throw one dead man upon another,

jeter.of: De cels d'Espaigne en ad get[et] mort .XX.,
jeter.tr: Of those of Spain he has thrown twenty dead,

jeter.of: La sus amunt pargetent tel luiserne
jeter.tr: Up there on high they cast such a light

jeter.of: Sur l'erbe verte getent un palie blanc:
jeter.tr: On the green grass they spread a white silk cloth;

jeter.of: Plus qu'en ne poet un bastuncel jeter,
jeter.tr: Farther than one can throw a stick,

jeter.of: Sin getat mort Malpalin de Nerbone;
jeter.tr: And there he threw Malpalin of Narbonne down dead;

jeter.of: Desur lur bronies lur barbes unt getees,
jeter.tr: Over their hauberks they have thrown their beards,

jeter.of: A icest colp en jetent mort .VII. milie.
jeter.tr: At this one blow they cast down dead seven thousand.

jeter.of: Getez mei hoi de mort e de calunje!»
jeter.tr: Free me today from death and from accusation!»

joindre.of: Qu'il devendrat jointes ses mains tis hom,
joindre.tr: That he will become, his hands joined, your vassal,

joindre.of: En Rencesvals a Rollant irai juindre,
joindre.tr: At Roncevaux I will go to join Roland,

joindre.of: Cuntre le ciel ambesdous ses mains juintes,
joindre.tr: Toward heaven both his hands joined,

joindre.of: Cuntre le ciel amsdous ses mains ad juinz,
joindre.tr: Toward heaven he has joined both his hands,

joindre.of: Juntes ses mains est alet a sa fin.
joindre.tr: With his hands joined he has gone to his end.

joncher.of: La veïsez la tere si junchee:
joncher.tr: There you would see the earth so strewn:

jouer.of: As tables juent pur els esbaneier
jouer.tr: At backgammon they play to amuse themselves
«To Roncevaux I will go to disport my body!

jouer.of: Unches nuls hom nel vit juer ne rire.
jouer.tr: Never did any man see him play or laugh.

jouir.of: En sun curage en est joüs e liet.
jouir.tr: In his heart he is glad and joyful about it.

jouter.tr: «Felon French, today you shall joust with ours,

jouter.of: «Sire cumpaign, a mei car vus justez!
jouter.tr: «Lord companion, come now, join me here!

jouter.of: Trestut le cors a la tere li justet.
jouter.tr: His whole body sinks down to the ground.
Set them side by side and arrange them in rows before you.»

jouter.of: Par vos li mand bataille i seit justee.»
jouter.tr: Through you I send word that battle is to be joined there.»

jouter.of: Por granz batailles juster e defenir.
jouter.tr: For fighting in great battles and bringing them to an end.

jouter.of: N'i ad Franceis, si a lui vient juster,
jouter.tr: There is no Frank who, if he comes to joust with him,

jouter.of: Si justerunt a Charles e a Franceis.
jouter.tr: And they will fight against Charles and the Franks.
The foremost battalions have come together.

jouter.of: E Guineman justet a un rei leutice.
jouter.tr: And Guineman jousts with a Lutician king.

jouter.of: Puis sunt justez par amur e par feid,
jouter.tr: Then they join together, in love and in faith,

jouter.of: Des dous baruns justee est la bataille.
jouter.tr: By the two barons the battle is fought.

juger.of: Li duze per mar i serunt jugez!»
juger.tr: The twelve peers would be ill-judged [for it]!»

juger.of: Si as juget qu'a Marsiliun en alge!
juger.tr: So you have decided that I should go to Marsile!

juger.of: Oït l'avez, sur vos le jugent Franc.»
juger.tr: You have heard it, the Franks judge it against you.»

juger.of: Ki ço jugat, que doüsez aler
juger.tr: He who decreed that you should go

juger.of: Pois me jugez Rollant a rereguarde.
juger.tr: Then assign Roland to me for the rearguard.

juger.of: Kar me jugez, ki ert en la rereguarde.»
juger.tr: Now judge for me, who shall be in the rearguard.»

juger.of: Li quens Rollant quant il s'oït juger,
juger.tr: Count Roland, when he hears himself thus assigned,

juger.of: La rereguarde avez sur mei jugiet.
juger.tr: You have assigned the rearguard to me.

juger.of: La rereguarde est jugee (...) sur lui:
juger.tr: The rearguard has been assigned (...) to him:

juger.of: Chi ad juget mis nes a (la) rereguarde.
juger.tr: He who has assigned my nephew to the rearguard.

juger.of: Il est juget que nus les ocirum.» AOI.
juger.tr: It is judged that we shall kill them.» AOI.

juger.of: Li .XII. per tuit sunt jugez a perdre;
juger.tr: The Twelve Peers are all condemned to perish;

juger.of: Ki nus jugat devant l'empereür.»
juger.tr: Who judged us before the emperor.»

juger.of: Jo vos plevis, tuz sunt jugez a mort.» AOI.
juger.tr: I pledge you, all are condemned to death.» AOI.

juger.of: El plait ad Ais en fut juget a prendre,
juger.tr: At the trial at Aix he was condemned to be seized,

juger.of: Ceste bataille seit ju(ic)get en sun num!» AOI.
juger.tr: May this battle be judged in his name!» AOI.

juger.of: «De Guenelun car me jugez le dreit!
juger.tr: «Judge me the right of Ganelon!

juger.of: Si me jugat a mort e a dulur.
juger.tr: And judged me to death and to suffering.

juger.of: N'i ad Frances ki vos juget a pendre,
juger.tr: There is no Frank who will judge you to hang,

juger.of: Pur ço le juz jo a prendre e a murir
juger.tr: For that I judge him to be seized and to die

juger.of: Puis que il sunt a bataille jugez, AOI.
juger.tr: Since they have been judged to battle, AOI.

jurer.of: La traïsun me jurrez de Rollant si illi est.»
jurer.tr: You will swear to me the betrayal of Roland, if it is so.»

jurer.of: La traïsun jurat, e si s'en est forsfait. AOI.
jurer.tr: He swore the betrayal, and thus made himself guilty of it. AOI.

jurer.of: Ço ad juret li Sarrazins espans:
jurer.tr: The Spanish Saracen has sworn this:

jurer.of: Guenes li fels ad nostre mort juree;
jurer.tr: Ganelon the traitor has sworn our death;

jurer.of: Li amiralz en juret quanqu'il poet
jurer.tr: The emir swears with all his might

jurer.of: Ki me jurat cume sa per a prendre?»
jurer.tr: Who swore to me to take me as his peer?»

lacer.of: Healmes lacez e ceintes lur espees,
lacer.tr: helmets laced and their swords girded,

lacer.of: Lacent lor elmes mult bons sarraguzeis,
lacer.tr: They lace on their fine Saragossan helmets,

lacer.of: Helmes laciez e blancs osbercs vestuz
lacer.tr: helmets laced on and white hauberks donned.

lacer.of: Laciet en su un gunfanun tut blanc;
lacer.tr: A pure white gonfalon laced upon it;

lacer.of: Lacent cil'elme as perres d'or gemmees,
lacer.tr: They lace on those helmets gemmed with gold,

lacer.of: Laciet sun elme, ki est a or gemmet,
lacer.tr: Laced his helmet, which is set with gold and gems,

lacer.of: Lacet sun helme, si ad ceinte Joiuse,
lacer.tr: He laces his helmet, and has girded on Joyeuse,

lacer.of: Helmes laciez e vestues lor bronies;
lacer.tr: Helmets laced and their hauberks put on;

lacer.of: Lacet sun elme, ki ad or est gemmet,
lacer.tr: Laces his helmet, which is set with gems in gold,

laisser.of: Laissun les fols, as sages nus tenuns.» AOI.
laisser.tr: Let us leave the fools, let us hold to the wise.» AOI.

laisser.of: E dist al rei: «Laisez ester voz Francs!
laisser.tr: And said to the king: «Let your Franks be!

laisser.of: Se lui lessez, n'i trametrez plus saive.»
laisser.tr: If you leave him aside, you will not send a wiser one.»

laisser.of: A lui lais jo mes honurs e mes fieus.
laisser.tr: To him I leave my lands and my fiefs.

laisser.of: Jo ne lerreie, por l'or que Deus fist
laisser.tr: I would not refrain, for all the gold that God made

laisser.of: Lessez (la) folie, tenez vos al saveir.
laisser.tr: Leave aside folly, hold to wisdom.

laisser.of: Sa rereguarde lerrat derere sei:
laisser.tr: His rearguard he will leave behind him:

laisser.of: Demi mun host vos lerrai en present.
laisser.tr: Half my host I will leave to you here and now.

laisser.of: As porz d'Espaigne ad lesset sun nevold.
laisser.tr: At the passes of Spain he has left his nephew.

laisser.of: Jo l'ai lesset en une estrange marche!
laisser.tr: I have left him in a strange land!

laisser.of: Ne lesserat bataille ne lur dunt.
laisser.tr: Will not fail to give them battle.

laisser.of: Se truis Rollant, ne lerrai que nel mat!»
laisser.tr: If I find Roland, I will not fail to bring him down!»

laisser.of: Laissent les mulz e tuz les palefreiz,
laisser.tr: They leave behind the mules and all the palfreys,

laisser.of: Li emperere, ki Franceis nos laisat,
laisser.tr: The emperor, who left the French to us,

laisser.of: «Seignurs baruns, Carles nus laissat ci;
laisser.tr: «Lord barons, Charles left us here;

laisser.of: Fols est li reis ki vos laissat as porz.
laisser.tr: Foolish is the king who left you at the passes.

laisser.of: Sun cheval brochet, laiset curre a esforz,
laisser.tr: He spurs his horse, lets it run at full force,

laisser.of: Ne leserat, ço dit, que n'i parolt:
laisser.tr: He will not refrain, he says, from speaking there:

laisser.of: Il fist que proz qu'il nus laisad as porz:
laisser.tr: He acted as a brave man when he left us at the passes:

laisser.of: Ne laisserat que n'i parolt, ço dit:
laisser.tr: He will not refrain from speaking to him, he says this:

laisser.of: E Anseïs laiset le cheval curre,
laisser.tr: And Anseïs lets his horse run,

laisser.of: Voillet o nun, tut i laisset sun tens.
laisser.tr: Willing or not, each leaves his life there.

laisser.of: Ne laisserat qu'Abisme nen asaillet;
laisser.tr: He will not fail to assail Abisme;

laisser.of: Ne lesserat que nos ne beneïsse.» AOI.
laisser.tr: He will not fail to bless us.» AOI.

laisser.of: Carles li magnes mar vos laissat as porz!
laisser.tr: Charlemagne left you at the passes to your sorrow!

laisser.of: E recreant ki les lerrat guar[ir]!»
laisser.tr: And a coward whoever lets them escape!»

laisser.of: Li uns ne volt l'altre nient laisser.
laisser.tr: Not one of them is willing to abandon the other.

laisser.of: Ne lur lerat tant cum il serat vif.
laisser.tr: He will not leave them as long as he is alive.

laisser.of: Ne vos lerrai pur nul hume de car.
laisser.tr: I will not leave you for any man of flesh.

laisser.of: Lancuns a lui, puis sil laissums ester.»
laisser.tr: Let us hurl at him, then let him be.»

laisser.of: Desuz le cunte, si l'i unt mort laisset.
laisser.tr: Beneath the count, and have left him dead there.

laisser.of: Paien s'en fuient, puis sil laisent ester.
laisser.tr: The pagans flee, then they leave him be.

laisser.of: Or sunt il morz: nes i devuns laiser.
laisser.tr: Now they are dead: we must not leave them.

laisser.of: Deus! Perre, n'en laise(i)t hunir France!»
laisser.tr: God! Father, do not let France be shamed by it!»

laisser.of: Li .XII. per, que jo aveie laiset?»
laisser.tr: The twelve peers, whom I had left behind?»

laisser.of: Lessez gesir les morz tut issi cun il sunt,
laisser.tr: Let the dead lie just as they are,

laisser.of: E par cez prez les laisez refreider.»
laisser.tr: And let them cool off in these meadows.»

laisser.of: [Qu']en Rencesvals ad laiset morz sang[l]enz.
laisser.tr: Whom he has left dead and bloody in Roncevaux.

laisser.of: Cest nostre rei por quei lessas cunfundre?
laisser.tr: Why did you let this king of ours be confounded?

laisser.of: Laisent Marbrose e si laisent Marbrise,
laisser.tr: They leave Marbrose and they leave Marbrise,

laisser.of: Que ne lairat pur tut l'or desuz ciel,
laisser.tr: That he will not desist, for all the gold beneath heaven,

laisser.of: Lur chevals laisent dedesuz un olive:
laisser.tr: They leave their horses beneath an olive tree:

laisser.of: Noz chevalers i unt lesset ocire;
laisser.tr: They have let our knights be killed there;

laisser.of: - «Laissez ço ester!« dist Marsilies li reis.
laisser.tr: «Let that be!» said King Marsile.

laisser.of: Sis unt laisez: qu'en fereient il el? AOI.
laisser.tr: They left them: what else would they do? AOI.

laisser.of: Ja devers els bataille n'ert lessee.
laisser.tr: Never on their side will the battle be left.

laisser.of: Brochent a eit; dunc laisent curre Francs:
laisser.tr: Spur at full speed; then the Franks let them run:

laisser.of: Brochent ad eit, lor cevals laissent cure,
laisser.tr: They spur eagerly, let their horses run,

laisser.of: Puint le ceval, laisset curre ad espleit,
laisser.tr: He spurs the horse, lets it run at full speed,

laisser.of: Mil chevalers i laissat puigneürs;
laisser.tr: He left there a thousand fighting knights;

laisser.of: Laisum le plait e si preium le rei
laisser.tr: Let us drop the trial and let us pray the king

laisser.of: Vivre le laisez, car mult est gentilz hoem.
laisser.tr: Let him live, for he is a very noble man.

laisser.of: Ceste bataille, car la laisses ester!
laisser.tr: This battle, pray leave it be!

lancer.of: Il lor lancent e lances e espiez,
lancer.tr: They hurl at them both lances and spears,

lancer.of: Lancuns a lui, puis sil laissums ester.»
lancer.tr: Let us hurl at him, then let him be.»

lancer.of: Plus qu'om ne lancet une verge pelee,
lancer.tr: Farther than one throws a peeled rod,

laver.of: Puis od les ewes lavat les prez del sanc,
laver.tr: Then with the waters he washed the meadows of the blood,

laver.of: Ben sunt lavez de piment e de vin.
laver.tr: They are well washed with spiced wine and with wine.

lever.of: Li empereres est par matin levet;
lever.tr: The emperor is risen at morning;

lever.of: Turpins de Reins en est levet del renc,
lever.tr: Turpin of Reims has risen from the ranks,

lever.of: Ambes ses mains en levat cuntre munt,
lever.tr: He raised both his hands toward the heavens,

lever.of: Li empereres est par matin levet;
lever.tr: The emperor has risen at morning;

lever.of: En sur un tertre cuntre le ciel levee.
lever.tr: raised it up on a hilltop against the sky.

lever.of: Mahumet levent en la plus halte tur.
lever.tr: They raise up Mohammed on the highest tower.
He stood godfather to King Marsile,

lever.of: Leverunt nos en bieres sur sumers,
lever.tr: They will lift us onto biers on pack-horses,

lever.of: Lievet sa main, fait sa b[en]eïçun,
lever.tr: He raises his hand, gives his blessing,

lever.of: Levet sa main, sur lui fait sun signacle.
lever.tr: Raises his hand, makes his sign over him.

lever.of: Granz est li calz, si se levet la puldre.
lever.tr: Great is the heat, and the dust rises.

lier.of: Pris e liez serez par poested;
lier.tr: You will be seized and bound by force,

lier.of: Par poestet serez pris e liez;
lier.tr: By force you will be taken and bound;

lier.of: Les mains li lient a curreies de cerf;
lier.tr: They bind his hands with straps of deerskin;

lier.of: Puis si li lient e les piez e les mains.
lier.tr: Then they bind both his feet and his hands.

livrer.of: Livrez m'en ore le guant e le bastun.»
livrer.tr: Hand me now the glove and the staff.»

livrer.of: Puis li livrat le bastun e le bref.
livrer.tr: Then he handed over to him the staff and the letter.

livrer.of: El destre poign al paien l'ad liv(e)ret.
livrer.tr: Into the right fist of the pagan he handed it over.

livrer.of: Livrez le mei, jo en ferai la justise.»
livrer.tr: Hand him over to me, I will do justice on him for it.»

livrer.of: Altre bataille lur livrez de meïsme:

livrer.tr: I will give him a mortal battle.»

livrer.of: Une bataille lur livrat le jur pesme. AOI.
livrer.tr: Gave them a fierce battle that grievous day. AOI.

livrer.of: Jo vos plevis, tuz sunt a mort livrez.» AOI.
livrer.tr: I pledge you, they are all delivered up to death.» AOI.

livrer.of: Livrent lur prez, asez i ad fresche herbe;
livrer.tr: They give them the meadows; there is plenty of fresh grass there;

livrer.of: De Sarraguce les clefs li ad livrees.
livrer.tr: He has handed over to him the keys of Saragossa.

livrer.of: Pur sun poign destre l'en liverai le che(s)[f].»
livrer.tr: For his right hand I will deliver him the head.»

louer.of: Ben en purrat luer ses soldeiers.
louer.tr: Well will he be able to pay his soldiers with it.

louer.of: Dunt bien purrez voz soldeiers luer.
louer.tr: that you will well be able to pay your soldiers.

louer.of: Ki ço vos lodet que cest plait degetuns,
louer.tr: Whoever advises you that we reject this agreement,

louer.of: Loat sun Deu, ne fist altre respuns.
louer.tr: Praised his God, made no other reply.

louer.of: Tant nel vos sai ne preiser ne loer
louer.tr: I cannot so praise him to you nor extol him

louer.of: Ambure ocit, ki quel blasme ne quil lot.
louer.tr: He kills them both, let who will blame or praise it.

louer.of: Tort nos ad fait: nen est dreiz qu'il s'en lot,
louer.tr: He has wronged us: it is not right that he should boast of it,

louer.of: Si hume li lo[d]ent, si li unt cunseillet.
louer.tr: His men advise him to it, and have counseled him so.
«Look at the pride of France the praised!

louer.of: «Que me loez de cels qu'ai retenuz?
louer.tr: «What do you advise me about those I have kept back?

luire.of: Soleill n'i luist, ne blet n'i poet pas creistre,
luire.tr: The sun does not shine there, nor can grain grow there,

luire.of: Luisent cil elme, ki ad or sunt gemmez,
luire.tr: The helmets gleam, which are gemmed with gold,

luire.of: Dreites cez hanstes, luisent cil espiet brun.
luire.tr: Upright are those lances, those burnished spearheads gleam.

luire.of: L'elme li freint u li carbuncle luisent,
luire.tr: He breaks his helm where the carbuncles gleam,

luire.of: Cuntre le ciel sur tuz les altres luist.
luire.tr: Against the sky he shines above all the others.

luire.of: Quatre perruns i ad luisant de marbre.
luire.tr: Four blocks of marble are there, gleaming.

luire.of: Cuntre soleill si luises e reflambes!
luire.tr: How you shine and flash against the sun!

luire.of: Clers est li jurz et li soleilz luisant.
luire.tr: Bright is the day and the sun shining.

luire.of: Luisent cil elme as perres d'or gemmees,
luire.tr: Those helmets gleam, set with gold gems,

luire.of: Clers fut li jurz e li soleilz luisanz.
luire.tr: Bright was the day and the sun shining.

lutter.of: E prenent sei a braz ambesdous por loiter;
lutter.tr: And they seize each other in their arms, both of them, to wrestle;

lâcher.of: Sun cheval (...) brochet, si li laschet la resne,
lâcher.tr: Spurs his horse, lets loose the rein,

lâcher.of: Laschent lor reisnes, brochent amdui a ait,
lâcher.tr: They slacken their reins, both spur eagerly,

lâcher.of: Laschet la resne, des esperuns le brochet,
lâcher.tr: He slackens the rein, spurs it with his spurs,

lâcher.of: Laschet la resne, mult suvent l'esperonet,
lâcher.tr: He loosens the rein, very often he spurs it,

lâcher.of: Lascent les resnes a lor cevals curanz,
lâcher.tr: Loosen the reins to their running horses,

lâcher.of: Brochent les bien, tutes les resnes lasquent;
lâcher.tr: They spur them well, they slacken all the reins;

mander.of: Mandez Carlun a l'orguillus, (e) al fier,
mander.tr: Send word to Charles, to the proud, to the fierce,

mander.of: Iço vus mandet reis Marsilies, li bers:
mander.tr: This is what King Marsile, the baron, sends word to you:

mander.of: Ses baruns mandet pur sun cunseill finer:
mander.tr: His barons he summons to settle his counsel:

mander.of: Ses baruns mandet pur sun cunseill fenir:
mander.tr: He summons his barons to settle his counsel:

mander.of: Mais il me mandet que en France m'en alge:
mander.tr: But he commands me that I depart from France:

mander.of: Quant ço vos mandet li reis Marsiliun,
mander.tr: When the king Marsile sends you word of this,

mander.of: Quant il vos mandet, qu'aiez mercit de lui,
mander.tr: When he sends word to you, that you have mercy on him,

mander.of: Iço vus mandet Carlemagnes, li ber,
mander.tr: This is what Charlemagne the baron commands you:

mander.of: Que Charles li mandet, li reis poesteïfs,
mander.tr: What Charles commands him, the mighty king,

mander.of: Par mei li mandet, sun mortel enemi.»
mander.tr: Commands him through me, his mortal enemy.»

mander.of: Quar ço vos mandet Carles, ki France tient,
mander.tr: For thus Charles, who rules France, commands you:

mander.of: «Carle me mandet, ki France ad en baillie,
mander.tr: «Charles, who has France in his keeping, commands me,

mander.of: E si vos mandet reis Marsilies li ber,
mander.tr: And so King Marsile the brave sends word to you,

mander.of: Marsilies mandet d'Espaigne les baruns,
mander.tr: Marsile summons the barons of Spain,

mander.of: Cum faitement li manderum nuveles?»
mander.tr: In what way shall we send him news?»

mander.of: Quant Deus del cel li mandat par sun a[n]gle,
mander.tr: When God from heaven sent word to him by his angel

mander.of: En Babilonie Baligant ad mandet,
mander.tr: He has sent to Babylon for Baligant,

mander.of: Mandet sa gent de .XL. regnez,
mander.tr: He summons his people from forty kingdoms,

mander.of: Par vos li mand bataille i seit justee.»
mander.tr: Through you I send word that battle is to be joined there.»

mander.of: U est Marsilie, que jo aveie mandet?«
mander.tr: Where is Marsile, whom I had summoned?»

mander.of: Li reis mandet que vos le sucurez.
mander.tr: The king sends word that you are to help him.

mander.of: Mandet li reis e si hume trestuz
mander.tr: The king summons, and all his men,

mander.of: Par ses messages mandet ses jugeors:
mander.tr: He summons his judges by his messengers:

mander.of: Alemans mandet, si mandet Borguignuns,
mander.tr: He summons Alemanni, and he summons Burgundians,

mander.of: Quatre cuntesses sempres i ad mandees.
mander.tr: He has summoned four countesses at once.

mander.of: Que Carles mandet humes de plusurs teres.
mander.tr: That Charles summons men from many lands.

manger.of: N'en mangerunt ne lu ne porc ne chen.»
manger.tr: Neither wolf nor pig nor dog shall eat of us.»

manger.of: Urs e leuparz les voelent puis manger,
manger.tr: Bears and leopards then want to devour them,

manger.of: Ne deit manger, se jo ne li cumant.
manger.tr: Must not eat unless I command it.

manœuvrer.of: en l'oret punt l'ad faite manuvrer.
manœuvrer.tr: And has had it fashioned into the golden pommel.

mater.of: Se truis Rollant, ne lerrai que nel mat!»
mater.tr: If I find Roland, I will not fail to bring him down!»

mater.of: Le grant orgoill se ja puez matir,
mater.tr: If you can ever crush their great pride,

maudire.of: Si maldient Carlun e France dulce.
maudire.tr: Who curse Charles and sweet France.

mendier.of: Ne nus seiuns cunduiz a mendeier.» AOI.
mendier.tr: And that we be reduced to begging.» AOI.

mener.of: En Sarraguce menez vostre ost banie,
mener.tr: To Saragossa lead your summoned host,

mener.of: Enpres li dient: «Sire, car nos menez!»
mener.tr: Then they say to him: «Lord, do lead us along!»

mener.of: Menet serez . . . [tut] dreit ad Ais le siet:
mener.tr: You will be led straight to the seat of Aix:

mener.of: Enz el verger l'en meinet josqu'al rei.
mener.tr: Into the orchard he leads him as far as the king.

mener.of: Recreanz ert de sa guerre mener,
mener.tr: He will be weary of waging his war,

mener.of: Itels .C. milie Sarrazins od els meinent,
mener.tr: Such a hundred thousand Saracens they lead with them,

mener.of: Si i merrez Torleu, le rei persis,
mener.tr: And you will lead there Torleu, the Persian king,
They lead the pagans to the baptistery:

mener.of: En France dulce iert menee caitive:
mener.tr: She will be led captive to sweet France:

mener.of: E Bramidonie, qu'il meinet en sa prisun;
mener.tr: And Bramimonde, whom he leads in his custody;

mentir.tr: «Vile pagan, you have lied in this!

mentir.of: Aït vos Deus, ki unkes ne mentit!
mentir.tr: May God aid you, who never lied!

mesurer.of: Grant demi pied mesurer i pout hom.
mesurer.tr: A good half-foot one could measure there.

mesurer.of: Cinquante pez i poet hom mesurer.
mesurer.tr: Fifty feet one can measure there.

mettre.of: Li frein sunt d'or, les seles d'argent mises.
mettre.tr: The bridles are of gold, the saddles set with silver.

mettre.of: Pa[r] num de ocire i metrai un mien filz,
mettre.tr: At risk of being slain, I will put there a son of mine,

mettre.of: Metez le sege a tute vostre vie,
mettre.tr: Lay the siege for the whole of your life,

mettre.of: E tutes teres met en chalengement!
mettre.tr: And puts all lands into contention!

mettre.of: Or e argent lur met tant en present,
mettre.tr: He puts so much gold and silver before them as gifts,

mettre.of: Quant le vit Guenes, mist la main a l'espee,
mettre.tr: When Ganelon saw it, he put his hand to his sword,

mettre.of: Sa rereguarde avrat detres sei mise;
mettre.tr: He will have placed his rearguard behind him;

mettre.of: A Durendal jo la metrai encuntre;
mettre.tr: Against Durendal I will set it;

mettre.of: Tere Majur vos metrum en present.
mettre.tr: We will deliver the Great Land to you.

mettre.of: L'empereor vos metrum en present.»
mettre.tr: We will hand over the emperor to you.»

mettre.of: Jo vos plevis qu'en vermeill sanc ert mise.
mettre.tr: I pledge to you that it will be set in crimson blood.

mettre.of: Itels .XX. milie en mist a une part
mettre.tr: Set apart such twenty thousand men

mettre.of: Franceis de[s]cendent, a tere se sunt mis,
mettre.tr: The Franks dismount, they prostrated themselves on the ground,

mettre.of: Franceis se drecent, si se metent sur piez.
mettre.tr: The French rise up and get to their feet.

mettre.of: Ist de la prese, si se met en bandun,
mettre.tr: He springs out of the press and flings himself forward,

mettre.of: El cors li met les pans del gunfanun,
mettre.tr: Drives into his body the folds of the gonfanon,

mettre.of: Sun grant espiet par mi le cors li mist,
mettre.tr: He thrust his great spear through the middle of his body,

mettre.of: Sun bon espiet li me(n)t en la curaille,
mettre.tr: He thrusts his good spear into his belly,

mettre.of: Del bon espiet el cors li met la mure,
mettre.tr: Drives the point of his good spear into his body,

mettre.of: Empeinst le ben, tut le fer li mist ultre,
mettre.tr: Thrusts it well, sends the iron clean through him,

mettre.of: El cors li met sun bon espiet tre[n]chant,
mettre.tr: Into his body he drives his good sharp spear,

mettre.of: Sun fort escut par mi le cors li mist,
mettre.tr: His strong spear he thrust through the middle of his body,

mettre.of: Fors de la teste li met les oilz ansdous,
mettre.tr: From his head he drives out both his eyes,

mettre.of: Tere Major ço dit, metrat a hunte,
mettre.tr: The Great Land, he says, he will put to shame,

mettre.of: De sun espiet el cors li met la mure,
mettre.tr: He thrusts the point of his spear into his body,

mettre.of: Empeint le ben, tut le fer li mist ultre,
mettre.tr: Drives it in hard, sends all the iron through,

mettre.of: El cors li met les pans del gunfanun,
mettre.tr: Into his body he drives the folds of the gonfanon,

mettre.of: El cors li met e le fer e le fust;
mettre.tr: He thrusts into his body both the iron and the shaft;

mettre.of: El cors li met tute l'enseingne bloie,
mettre.tr: Drives into his body all the blue ensign,

mettre.of: Rollant ad mis l'olifan a sa buche,
mettre.tr: Roland has put the oliphant to his mouth,

mettre.of: Cil le receit, si met .C. cumpaignons
mettre.tr: The cook receives him, and sets a hundred companions

mettre.of: E si li metent el col un caeignun,
mettre.tr: And they put a chain around his neck,

mettre.of: Sur un sumer l'unt mis a deshonor.
mettre.tr: On a pack-horse they have set him in dishonor.

mettre.of: En ceste tere nus ad mis tels feluns!
mettre.tr: He has set such villains in this land!

mettre.of: Par mi le piz sun espiet li mist fors,
mettre.tr: He thrust his spear out through the middle of his breast,

mettre.of: Sis mist en reng dedevant ses genuilz.
mettre.tr: And sets them in a row before his knees.

mettre.of: En pareïs les metet en se[i]ntes flurs!
mettre.tr: May he set them in paradise among holy flowers!

mettre.of: Ço est l'arcevesque, que Deus mist en sun num.
mettre.tr: That is the archbishop, whom God placed in his name.

mettre.of: Met sei en piez e de curre s'astet.
mettre.tr: He gets to his feet and hastens to run.

mettre.of: Amsdous les oilz del chef li ad mis fors;
mettre.tr: Has driven both eyes out of his head,

mettre.of: Met sei sur piez, quanqu'il poet, s'esvertuet;
mettre.tr: He gets to his feet, as best he can, he exerts himself;

mettre.of: Desuz lui met s'espee e l'olifan (en sumet);
mettre.tr: Beneath himself he puts his sword and the oliphant (on top);

mettre.of: Mais lui meïsme ne volt mettre en ubli,
mettre.tr: But he will not put himself into oblivion either,

mettre.of: Les freins a or e metent jus des testes,
mettre.tr: They take the golden bridles down from their heads,

mettre.of: Sun grant espiet met a sun chef li ber;
mettre.tr: The valiant man puts his great spear at his head;

mettre.of: U[n] faldestoed i unt mis d'olifan.
mettre.tr: They have set a throne of ivory there.

mettre.of: «Ami Rollant, Deus metet t'anme en flors,
mettre.tr: «Dear Roland, may God set your soul among flowers,

mettre.of: L'anme de tei seit mise en pareïs!
mettre.tr: May your soul be placed in paradise!

mettre.of: Ki tei ad mort France ad mis en exill.
mettre.tr: Whoever has killed you has put France into exile.

mettre.of: Entre les lur aluee e mise,
mettre.tr: Allotted and placed among theirs,

mettre.of: Un blanc sarcou de marbre sunt enz mis;
mettre.tr: A white marble sarcophagus, they are put inside;

mettre.of: En quirs de cerf les seignurs unt mis:
mettre.tr: In stag hides they put the lords:

mettre.of: Desur sa bronie fors ad mise sa barbe.
mettre.tr: Over his hauberk he has placed his beard outside.

mettre.of: L'espiet a or li ad enz el cors mis,
mettre.tr: He has driven the gold-adorned spear into his body,

mettre.of: Tute l'enseigne li ad enz el cors mise,
mettre.tr: He has put the whole banner into his body,

mettre.of: Deus nus ad mis al plus verai juïse.» AOI.
mettre.tr: God has set us on the truest judgment.» AOI.

mettre.of: El cors li met tute l'enseigne jalne,
mettre.tr: He puts the whole yellow banner into his body,

mettre.of: El cors li mis mun espiet une feiz.»
mettre.tr: I drove my spear into his body once.»

mettre.of: Li amiraill ad sa barbe fors mise,
mettre.tr: The emir has let his beard show,

mettre.of: Met a sa buche une clere buisine,
mettre.tr: He puts a clear trumpet to his mouth,

mettre.of: Met li l'espee sur les chevels menuz,
mettre.tr: He sets the sword on his thin hair,

mettre.of: Met l'oliphan plein d'or e de manguns:
mettre.tr: He sets the oliphant full of gold and mangons:

mettre.of: En blancs sarcous fait metre les seignurs
mettre.tr: In white sarcophagi he has the lords placed

mettre.of: E sun cors metre...
mettre.tr: And his body put...

mettre.of: Met li el poign de cerf le destre guant.
mettre.tr: He places in his hand the right glove of deerskin.

mettre.of: Mult granz offrendes metent par cez musters.
mettre.tr: They place very great offerings in these minsters.

mettre.of: Celes met jus, puis li afublent altres;
mettre.tr: Sets those aside, then others are put on him;

mettre.of: En Bramidonie ad chrestientet mise,
mettre.tr: He has set Christianity in Bramimonde,

monter.of: Cil sunt muntez ki le message firent,
monter.tr: Those who carried the message have mounted,

monter.of: Cunseill d orguill n'est dreiz que a plus munt,
monter.tr: Counsel of pride, it is not right that it rise further,

monter.of: Ceste grant guerre ne deit munter a plus.»
monter.tr: This great war ought not to mount up to more.»

monter.of: En Tachebrun, sun destrer est munted;
monter.tr: He has mounted Tachebrun, his warhorse;

monter.of: Pois est munted, entret en sun veiage. AOI.
monter.tr: Then he mounted, and set out on his journey. AOI.

monter.of: Li quens Rollant est muntet el destrer.
monter.tr: Count Roland has mounted his warhorse.

monter.of: Puis que il est sur un cheval muntet,
monter.tr: Once he is mounted upon a horse,

monter.tr: They mount their war-horses and ride in close ranks.

monter.of: Oliver est desur un pui haut muntez,
monter.tr: Oliver has climbed up onto a high hill,

monter.tr: Olivier has climbed up onto a hill;

monter.of: Sun cheval broche e muntet un lariz,
monter.tr: He spurs his horse and climbs a hillock,

monter.of: Puis sunt muntez sur lur curanz destrers.
monter.tr: Then they have mounted their swift war-horses.

monter.of: Es destrers muntent tuit li barun de l'ost,
monter.tr: Onto their war-horses mount all the barons of the host,

monter.tr: He climbs onto a hillock; beneath a fair tree

monter.tr: At that word the emperor has mounted. AOI.

monter.of: Puis sunt muntez sus el paleis altisme.
monter.tr: Then they went up into the very lofty palace.

monter.of: Li dui message es chevals sunt muntet.
monter.tr: The two messengers are mounted on horses.

monter.of: Eissez des nefs, muntez, si cevalciez!
monter.tr: Come out of the ships, mount, and ride!

monter.of: Puis sunt muntez es chevals e es muls;
monter.tr: Then have mounted on horses and on mules;

monter.of: Puis en un sun destrer brun est munte;
monter.tr: Then he mounts a brown war-horse of his own;

monter.of: Par les degrez el paleis muntet sus,
monter.tr: Up the steps into the palace he goes,

monter.of: Muntet el ceval, vient a sa gent puignant.
monter.tr: Mounts the horse, comes to his people at a gallop.

monter.of: Puis sunt muntet, par grant vertut chevalchent
monter.tr: Then they are mounted, with great force they ride

monter.of: Devant les altres est en un pui muntet.
monter.tr: In front of the others he has climbed onto a hill.

monter.of: En Tencendur, sun bon cheval, puis muntet:
monter.tr: Then he mounts Tencendur, his good horse:

monter.of: Puis sunt muntez e unt grant science.
monter.tr: Then they have mounted and have great skill.

monter.of: Puis sunt muntez, la bataille demandent;
monter.tr: Then they are mounted, they demand battle;

monter.of: Muntet li reis en sun cheval curant;
monter.tr: The king mounts his running horse;

monter.of: En sun destrer Baligant est muntet;
monter.tr: Baligant has mounted his warhorse;

monter.of: Prent Tencendur, muntet i est li reis magnes.
monter.tr: He takes Tencendur, and the great king has mounted.

monter.of: En sum sa tur muntee est Bramidonie,
monter.tr: At the top of her tower Bramimonde has climbed,

monter.of: Muntet el palais, est venut en la sale.
monter.tr: He goes up into the palace, has come into the hall.

monter.of: Puis sunt muntez en lur curanz destrers.
monter.tr: Then they are mounted on their swift destriers.

monter.of: [Munter l'unt] fait en une mule d'Arabe;
monter.tr: They have made him mount an Arabian mule;

montrer.of: E il li ad cum chevaler mustree.
montrer.tr: And he has shown it to him in knightly fashion.

montrer.tr: The angel of God has shown this to the baron.

montrer.of: Les escheles Charlun li ad mustrees:

montrer.tr: He has spoken a speech to them and set it out:

montrer.of: Cez lor espees tutes nues i mustrent,
montrer.tr: They show those swords of theirs, all bare, there,

mordre.of: El destre braz li morst uns vers si mals.
mordre.tr: In his right arm a fierce boar bit him.

mordre.of: E porc e chen le mordent e defulent.
mordre.tr: And pigs and dogs bite him and trample him.

mouler.of: Gros ad le piz, belement est mollet,
mouler.tr: He has a thick chest, it is finely molded;

mouler.of: Granz ies e forz e tis cors ben mollez;
mouler.tr: Big and strong, and your body well shaped;

mourir.of: Ne li chalt, sire, de quel mort nus muriuns.
mourir.tr: Cares not, sire, by what death we may die.

mourir.of: Mielz est que sul moerge que tant bon chevaler.
mourir.tr: Better that I alone die than so many good knights.

mourir.of: La murrez vus a hunte e a viltet.»
mourir.tr: There you will die in shame and in disgrace.»

mourir.of: Que suls i moerge en l'estrange cuntree,
mourir.tr: That I died alone in the foreign land,

mourir.of: Meilz voelt murir que guerpir sun barnet.»
mourir.tr: He would rather die than abandon his noble company.»

mourir.tr: So many rich kings dead and vanquished in the field:

mourir.tr: The counts are dead, if there is anyone who believes me in this.

mourir.tr: - «Whoever could bring it about that Roland be killed there,

mourir.of: E, se il poet, murrat i veirement.
mourir.tr: And, if he can, he will truly die there.

mourir.tr: They have no fear nor dread of dying.

mourir.tr: The French will die in grief and in shame.

mourir.of: Franceis murrunt, si a nus s'abandunent;
mourir.tr: The French will die, if they engage with us;

mourir.of: Franceis murrunt e France en ert deserte,
mourir.tr: The French shall die and France will be left desolate,

mourir.of: Franceis murrunt, Carles en ert dolent.
mourir.tr: The French will die, Charles will be grieved by it.

mourir.of: Franceis murrunt e France en ert hunie;
mourir.tr: The French will die and France will be shamed by it;

mourir.of: Franceis murrunt e France en ert deserte.»
mourir.tr: The French shall die and France shall be left desolate.»

mourir.of: Ja pur murir ne vus en faldrat uns.» AOI.
mourir.tr: Never, even to escape death, will a single one of us fail you.» AOI.

mourir.of: Melz voeill murir que huntage me venget.
mourir.tr: I would rather die than that shame befall me.

mourir.of: Ja pur murir n'eschiverunt bataille.
mourir.tr: Never, even on pain of death, will they shun battle.

mourir.of: Se jo i moert, dire poet ki l'avrat
mourir.tr: If I die here, whoever has it may say

mourir.tr: For our king we must surely die.

mourir.of: Se vos murez, esterez seinz martirs,
mourir.tr: If you die, you will be holy martyrs,

mourir.of: Or est le jur qu'els estuvrat murir.»
mourir.tr: Now is the day when they must die.»

mourir.of: Moerent paien e alquanz en i pasment.
mourir.tr: The pagans die and several of them faint there.

mourir.of: Ki de murir nen ourent esperance. AOI.
mourir.tr: Who had no hope of escaping death. AOI.

mourir.of: Moerent paien a miller(e)[s] e a cent;
mourir.tr: Pagans die there by thousands and by hundreds;

mourir.of: Paien sunt morz a millers e a fuls:
mourir.tr: The pagans are dead by the thousands and in droves:

mourir.of: Asez est mielz que moerium cumbatant.
mourir.tr: It is much better that we die fighting.

mourir.of: «Sire cumpainz, ja est morz Engeler;
mourir.tr: «Sir companion, Engelier is now dead;

mourir.of: Li quens Rollant, quant il veit Sansun mort,
mourir.tr: Count Roland, when he sees Samson dead,

mourir.of: Morz est li quens, de sun tens n'i ad plus.
mourir.tr: The count is dead, of his time there is no more.

mourir.of: Cels qu'il unt mort, ben les poet hom preiser;
mourir.tr: those whom they have slain, one can well count them;

mourir.of: Einz que il moergent, se vendrunt mult cher.
mourir.tr: Before they die, they will sell themselves very dear.

mourir.of: Mielz voeill murir que hunte nus seit retraite.» AOI.
mourir.tr: I would rather die than that shame be reported of us.» AOI.

mourir.of: Franceis sunt morz par vostre legerie.
mourir.tr: The French are dead through your rashness.

mourir.of: U pris ú mort i fust li reis Marsilie.
mourir.tr: Captured or killed would have been King Marsile.

mourir.of: Vos i murrez e France en ert (...) huníe.
mourir.tr: You will die here and France will be shamed by it.

mourir.of: «Se veïssum Rollant einz qu'il fust mortz,
mourir.tr: «If only we might see Roland before he is dead,

mourir.of: Barons Franceis, pur mei vos vei murir:
mourir.tr: French barons, for my sake I see you die:

mourir.of: De doel murra, se altre ne m'i ocit.
mourir.tr: I shall die of grief, if nothing else slays me.

mourir.of: Que hoi murrum par le mien escient.
mourir.tr: That today we shall die, to my knowledge.

mourir.of: Morz est li quens, que plus ne se demuret.
mourir.tr: The count is dead, he lingers no longer.

mourir.of: Or veit Rollant que mort est sun ami,
mourir.tr: Now Roland sees that his friend is dead,

mourir.of: Quant tu es mor[t], dulur est que jo vif!»
mourir.tr: Since you are dead, it is grief that I live!»

mourir.of: Morz sunt Franceis, tuz les i ad perdut,
mourir.tr: The Franks are dead; he has lost them all,

mourir.of: Mort sunt si hume, sis unt paiens (...) vencut;
mourir.tr: His men are dead, and the pagans have defeated them;

mourir.of: Sempres murrai, mais cher me sui vendut!»
mourir.tr: Soon I shall die, but I have sold myself dear!»

mourir.of: Or sunt il morz: nes i devuns laiser.
mourir.tr: Now they are dead: we must not leave them.

mourir.of: [Morz est Turpin, le guerreier Charlun.]
mourir.tr: [Dead is Turpin, Charles's warrior.]

mourir.of: Mielz voeill murir qu'entre paiens remaigne.
mourir.tr: I would rather die than have it remain among pagans.

mourir.of: Li gentilz quens, qu'il fut mort cunquerant.
mourir.tr: Of the noble count, that he died a conqueror.

mourir.of: Morz est Rollant, Deus en ad l'anme es cels.
mourir.tr: Roland is dead; God has his soul in the heavens.

mourir.of: Quant Carles veit que tuit sunt mort paiens,
mourir.tr: When Charles sees that all the pagans are dead,

mourir.of: Josqu'il seit mort u tut vif recreant.»
mourir.tr: Until he is dead or, quite alive, a craven.»

mourir.of: Meilz voel murir que ja fuiet de camp;
mourir.tr: He would rather die than ever flee from the field;

mourir.of: Mort m'ad mes homes, ma tere deguastee,
mourir.tr: Has killed my men, laid my land waste,

mourir.of: Sun filz ad mort, qu'il tant suleit amer,
mourir.tr: His son is dead, whom he so loved,

mourir.of: Morz est Rollant e li quens Oliver,
mourir.tr: Roland is dead, and Count Oliver,

mourir.of: De lur Franceis i ad mort .XX. millers.
mourir.tr: Of their Franks twenty thousand lie dead.

mourir.of: Ja ne (ne) murreit en estrange regnet
mourir.tr: He would never die in a foreign realm

mourir.of: Jo lur dirrai qu'il est morz en Espaigne.
mourir.tr: I will tell them that he is dead in Spain.

mourir.of: «Morz est mis nies, ki tant me fist cunquere.»
mourir.tr: «Dead is my nephew, who made me conquer so much.»

mourir.of: Quant cil est [morz] ki tuz jurz nos cadelet?
mourir.tr: When he is dead who always commands us?

mourir.of: Ki tei ad mort France ad mis en exill.
mourir.tr: Whoever has killed you has put France into exile.

mourir.of: Que cil d'Espaigne en la bataille unt mort;
mourir.tr: Those whom the Spaniards killed in the battle;

mourir.of: Ja por murir ne guerpirunt bataille.
mourir.tr: Never, even to die, will they abandon battle.

mourir.of: Einz i murat que cuardise i facet. AOI.
mourir.tr: He will die there sooner than commit cowardice there. AOI.

mourir.of: Ja pur murir cil n'erent recreanz.
mourir.tr: Never, even to die, will they be recreant.

mourir.tr: The Franks say: «You will soon die, villains!

mourir.of: Qu'en Rencesvals furent morz l'altre seir!
mourir.tr: Who were dead at Roncevaux the other evening!

mourir.of: Sempres fust mort li nobilies vassal.
mourir.tr: The noble vassal would at once be dead.

mourir.of: Morz est li gluz ki en destreit vus teneit;
mourir.tr: Dead is the wretch who held you in distress;

mourir.of: Asez i moerent e des uns e des altres.
mourir.tr: Many die there, both of the one side and of the other;

mourir.of: E humes braire, contre tere murir,
mourir.tr: And men cry out and die against the ground,

mourir.of: Si grant doel ad sempres quiad murir.
mourir.tr: He has such grief that he thinks he will die at once.

mourir.of: E cil respunt: «Morz estes, Baligant!

mourir.of: Mais Deus ne volt qu'il seit mort ne vencut.
mourir.tr: But God does not wish him to be dead or conquered.

mourir.of: N'en ad poür ne de murir dutance;
mourir.tr: He has no fear and no dread of dying;

mourir.of: Morz est de doel. Si cum pecchet l'encumbret,
mourir.tr: He is dead of grief. As sin weighs upon him,

mourir.tr: The pagans are dead, some overwhelmed,

mourir.tr: At once she is dead; God have mercy on her soul!

mourir.of: Morz est Rollant, ja mais nel revereiz;
mourir.tr: Roland is dead, you will never see him again;

mourir.tr: Not by his dying will any gain of him be seen,

mourir.of: Pur ço le juz jo a prendre e a murir
mourir.tr: For that I judge him to be seized and to die

mourir.of: Mielz voeill murir que il me seit reprovet.»
