servir.tr: Then serve and believe in the all-powerful King!»

servir.of: Serveie le par feid e par amur.
servir.tr: I served him in faith and in love.

servir.of: Puis si li servet par amur e par feid.
servir.tr: Then he will serve him in love and in faith.

servir.of: Puis si vos servet par feid e par amor.
servir.tr: Then he will serve you in faith and in love.

servir.of: Ja savez vos, que mult vos ai servit;
servir.tr: You well know that I have served you greatly;

sevrer.of: Tute la teste li ad par mi sevree,
sevrer.tr: He has cut his whole head clean in two,

sevrer.of: Le destre poign li ad del cors sevret;
sevrer.tr: That he has severed his right hand from his body;

signer.of: De sa main destre l'ad asols e seignet,
signer.tr: With his right hand he absolved and blessed him,

signer.of: E l'arcevesque de Deu les ad seignez;
signer.tr: And the archbishop has blessed them in God's name;
And the archbishop has absolved and blessed them.

signer.of: Si sunt asols e seignez de part Deu.
signer.tr: They are absolved and blessed in God's name.

signer.of: Seignat sun chef de la vertut poisant.
signer.tr: He signed his head with the cross of powerful virtue.

signer.of: Ben sunt cunfes e asols e seignez:
signer.tr: They are well confessed and absolved and blessed:

songer.of: Sunjat qu'il eret al greignurs porz de Sizer,
songer.tr: He dreamt that he was at the great passes of Cize,
After this one he dreamed another vision:

sonner.of: N'i ad celoi ki mot sunt ne mot tint,
sonner.tr: There is none among them who speaks a word nor utters a word,

sonner.of: Par mi cel ost funt mil grailles suner;
sonner.tr: Throughout that host they have a thousand trumpets sounded;

sonner.of: En Sarraguce fait suner ses taburs;
sonner.tr: In Saragossa he has his drums sounded;

sonner.of: Sunent mil grailles por ço que plus bel seit:
sonner.tr: A thousand trumpets sound so that it may be more splendid:

sonner.of: «Mis parrastre est, ne voeill que mot en suns.»
sonner.tr: «He is my stepfather, I do not wish that you say a word of it.»

sonner.of: Cumpaign Rollant, kar sunez vostre corn:
sonner.tr: Companion Roland, do sound your horn:

sonner.of: - «Cumpainz Rollant l'olifan car sunez:
sonner.tr: - «Companion Roland, sound the oliphant:

sonner.of: - «Cumpainz Rollant, sunez vostre olifan:
sonner.tr: - «Companion Roland, sound your oliphant:

sonner.of: Vostre olifan, suner vos nel deignastes;
sonner.tr: Your olifant, you did not deign to sound it;

sonner.of: Vostre olifan ne deignastes suner,
sonner.tr: You did not deign to sound your oliphant,

sonner.of: Sunet sun gresle pur les soens ralier.
sonner.tr: He sounds his bugle to rally his men.

sonner.of: .VII. milie graisles i sunent la menee:
sonner.tr: Seven thousand trumpets sound the charge there:

sonner.of: Si fait suner ses cors e ses buisines,
sonner.tr: So he has his horns and his trumpets sounded,

sonner.of: Empeint le ben, par grant vertut le sunet.
sonner.tr: He grips it well, sounds it with great force.

sonner.of: Par grant dulor sunet sun olifan.
sonner.tr: With great anguish sounds his oliphant.

sonner.of: Unc nel sunast se ne fust (cu)cumbatant.»
sonner.tr: He would never sound it unless he were fighting.»

sonner.of: L'olifan sunet a dulor e a peine.
sonner.tr: He sounds the oliphant in sorrow and in pain.

sonner.of: Li empereres ad fait suner ses corns.
sonner.tr: The emperor has had his horns sounded.

sonner.of: Sunent cil graisle e derere e devant,
sonner.tr: Those trumpets sound, both in the rear and in the van,

sonner.of: Trait l'olifan, fieblement le sunat.
sonner.tr: He draws out the oliphant, blows it feebly.

sonner.of: Sunez voz graisles tant que en cest ost ad!»
sonner.tr: Sound your trumpets, all that there are in this host!»

sonner.of: Sunent li munt e respondent li val:
sonner.tr: The mountains resound and the valleys answer:

sonner.of: De cels de France oe(n)z suner les graisles!
sonner.tr: Hear the trumpets of those of France sounding!

sonner.of: Li empereres fait ses graisles suner,
sonner.tr: The emperor has his bugles sounded,

sonner.of: Ço dist li reis: «Sunez en vostre corn!» AOI.
sonner.tr: The king said: «Sound your horn!» AOI.

sonner.of: Gefreid d'Anjou ad sun greisle sunet.
sonner.tr: Geoffrey of Anjou has sounded his trumpet.

sonner.of: Sunent cil greisle e derere e devant;
sonner.tr: They sound their trumpets, behind and ahead;

sonner.of: Sunez voz graisles, que mi paien le sace[n]t!»
sonner.tr: Sound your trumpets, so that my pagans may know it!»

sonner.of: Par tute l'ost funt lur taburs suner,
sonner.tr: Throughout the host they have their drums sounded,

sonner.of: Cil est mult proz ki sunet l'olifant,
sonner.tr: He is very valiant who sounds the oliphant,

sonner.of: Granz sunt les oz u cez buisines sunent.
sonner.tr: Great are the hosts where these trumpets sound.

sonner.of: Li emperere i fait suner ses greisles,
sonner.tr: The emperor has his trumpets sounded,

sonner.of: Sunent cez greisles, les voiz en sunt mult cleres;
sonner.tr: Those trumpets sound; their voices are very clear;

sonner.of: Sunet la cler, que si paien l'oïrent;
sonner.tr: Sounds it loudly, so that his pagans heard it;

souffrir.tr: - «Sire,» said Ganelon, «it falls to me to endure it;

souffrir.of: Pur sun seignor deit hom susfrir destreiz
souffrir.tr: For his lord a man should suffer hardships

souffrir.of: Pur sun seignur deit hom susfrir granz mals
souffrir.tr: For his lord a man must suffer great hardships

souffrir.of: Nuveles vos di: mort vos estoet susfrir.
souffrir.tr: News I tell you: you must suffer death.

souffrir.of: Li Sarrazin nel poent susfrir tant:
souffrir.tr: The Saracens cannot endure it so long:

souffrir.of: Ço est merveille que Deus le soefret tant.
souffrir.tr: It is a marvel that God suffers him so long.

souffrir.of: Ceste bataille est mult fort a suffrir.
souffrir.tr: This battle is very hard to endure.

soupirer.of: Ne poet muer n'en plurt e ne suspirt.
soupirer.tr: He cannot keep from weeping and sighing.

sourdre.of: Li reis Marsilie od sa grant ost lor surt. AOI.
sourdre.tr: King Marsile with his great host surges upon them. AOI.

sourdre.of: Quant de paiens li surdent les enguardes.
sourdre.tr: When the pagans' scouts appear before him.

soutenir.of: N'en avrai ja ki sustienget m'onur;
soutenir.tr: I will never have anyone to uphold my honor;
I want to uphold all my kindred;

souvenir.of: De grant dulor li poüst suvenir!
souvenir.tr: Of great sorrow he might be reminded!

suivre.of: Vos le sivrez a la feste seint Michel:
suivre.tr: You will follow him there at the feast of Saint Michael:

suivre.of: Que jel sivrai od mil de mes fedeilz,
suivre.tr: Before I follow him with a thousand of my faithful,

suivre.of: La vos sivrat, ço dit mis avoez.»
suivre.tr: there he will follow you, so says my lord.»

suivre.of: Mis avoez la vos sivrat, ço dit;
suivre.tr: My lord will follow you there, so he says;

suivre.of: Il me sivrat ad Aís, a mun estage,
suivre.tr: He will follow me to Aix, to my residence,

suivre.of: Qu'il vos sivrat en France le regnet,
suivre.tr: Before he will follow you into France the realm,

suivre.of: Sun cumpaignun apres le vait sivant,
suivre.tr: His companion comes following after him,
Seventeen kings go following after him;

suivre.of: Sis filz le siut, ki mult ad grant le cors.
suivre.tr: His son follows him, who has a very large body.

survivre.of: Tut survesquiet e Virgilie e Omer,
survivre.tr: Who has outlived everyone, both Virgil and Homer,

tailler.of: Tient Durendal, ki ben trenchet e taillet,
tailler.tr: Holds Durendal, which cuts and slashes well,

taire.of: Franceis se taisent ne mais que Guenelun,
taire.tr: The French keep silent, all save Ganelon,

taire.of: Respunt li reis: «Ambdui vos en taisez!
taire.tr: The king answers: «Both of you, be silent about it!

taire.of: Franceis se taisent: as les vus aquisez.
taire.tr: The Franks fall silent: behold them quieted.

tancer.of: Tencent a lui, laidement le despersunent:
tancer.tr: They berate him, they vilify him foully:

teindre.of: En Rencesvals jo la teindrai vermeille.
teindre.tr: At Roncevaux I shall stain it crimson.

tendre.of: Li empereres tent (...) ses mains vers Deu,
tendre.tr: The emperor stretches out his hands toward God,

tendre.of: El grant verger fait li reis tendre un tref,
tendre.tr: In the great orchard the king has a tent pitched,

tendre.of: Li empereres li tent sun guant le destre;
tendre.tr: The emperor holds out to him his right glove;

tendre.of: Dunez li l'arc que vos avez tendut,
tendre.tr: Give him the bow that you have drawn,
Toward Spain they strive to make haste.

tendre.of: Tendit sa main, si ad pris l'olifan:
tendre.tr: Stretched out his hand, and has taken the oliphant:

tendre.of: Sun destre guant en ad vers Deu tendut:
tendre.tr: He has held out his right glove toward God:

tenir.of: Li reis Marsilie la tient, ki Deu nen amet,
tenir.tr: King Marsile holds it — he who does not love God,

tenir.of: A seint Michel tendrat mult halte feste.
tenir.tr: At Saint Michael's he will hold a very high feast.

tenir.of: La siet li reis, ki dulce france tient.
tenir.tr: There sits the king who holds sweet France.

tenir.of: Li empereres en tint sun chef enclin;
tenir.tr: The emperor kept his head bowed;

tenir.of: Chrestiens ert, de mei tendrat ses marches;
tenir.tr: He will be a Christian, will hold his marches from me;

tenir.of: Li empe[re]re en tint sun chef enbrunc,
tenir.tr: The emperor held his head bowed down,

tenir.of: E tute Espaigne tendrat par vostre dun,
tenir.tr: And will hold all Spain by your gift,

tenir.of: Puis recevrat la lei que nus tenum,
tenir.tr: Then will receive the faith that we hold,

tenir.of: Laissun les fols, as sages nus tenuns.» AOI.
tenir.tr: Let us leave the fools, let us hold to the wise.» AOI.

tenir.of: Al Sarrazin ki Sarraguce tient?»
tenir.tr: To the Saracen who holds Saragossa?»

tenir.of: L'estreu li tint sun uncle Guinemer.
tenir.tr: His uncle Guinemer held the stirrup for him.

tenir.of: E lui aidez e pur seignur le tenez.»
tenir.tr: And help him and hold him as your lord.»

tenir.of: En sa main tint une vermeille pume:
tenir.tr: In his hand he held a crimson apple:

tenir.of: «Tenez bel sire,» dist Rollant a sun uncle,
tenir.tr: «Take it, fair lord,» said Roland to his uncle,

tenir.of: La fut li reis ki tute Espaigne tint;
tenir.tr: There was the king who held all Spain;

tenir.of: Par le puig[n] tint le cunte Guenelun,
tenir.tr: By the fist he held the count Ganelon,

tenir.of: E d'Apollin, qui seintes leis tenuns!
tenir.tr: And by Apollo, whose holy laws we hold!

tenir.of: Un algier tint, ki d'or fut enpenet,
tenir.tr: He held a javelin, which was feathered with gold,

tenir.of: En sun puign destre par l'orie punt la tint.
tenir.tr: In his right fist he held it by the golden pommel.

tenir.of: Quar ço vos mandet Carles, ki France tient,
tenir.tr: For thus Charles, who rules France, commands you:

tenir.of: Lessez (la) folie, tenez vos al saveir.
tenir.tr: Leave aside folly, hold to wisdom.

tenir.of: «Tenez m'espee, meillur n'en at nuls hom;
tenir.tr: «Take my sword, no man has a better one;

tenir.of: «Tenez mun helme, unches meillor ne vi.
tenir.tr: «Take my helmet, never did I see a better one.

tenir.of: Marsilies tint Guen[elun] par l'espalle;
tenir.tr: Marsile took Ganelon by the shoulder;

tenir.of: Par cele lei que vos tenez plus salve,
tenir.tr: By the law that you hold most sacred,

tenir.of: Tenez les clefs de ceste citet large,
tenir.tr: Take the keys of this great city,

tenir.of: Que il ne voelent ne tenir ne guarder.
tenir.tr: Which they wish neither to hold nor to keep.

tenir.of: Si recevrat la lei que vos tenez,
tenir.tr: And he will receive the faith that you hold,

tenir.of: De vos tendrat Espaigne le regnet.»
tenir.tr: From you he will hold Spain the realm.»

tenir.of: Entre ses poinz teneit sa hanste fraisnine.
tenir.tr: Between his hands he held his ashen lance.

tenir.of: N'i perdrat Carles, li reis ki France tient,
tenir.tr: Charles, the king who holds France, shall lose nothing by it,

tenir.of: «Dunez mei l'arc, que vos tenez el poign.
tenir.tr: «Give me the bow that you hold in your fist.

tenir.of: Li empereres en tint sun chef enbrunc,
tenir.tr: The emperor held his head bowed,

tenir.of: Li nies Marsilies tient le guant en sun poign,
tenir.tr: Marsile's nephew holds the gauntlet in his fist,

tenir.of: Cil tient la tere entre[s]qu'as Cazmarine.
tenir.tr: He holds the land as far as Cazmarine.

tenir.of: «Seignurs barons, suef pas alez tenant!
tenir.tr: «Lord barons, go forward at a gentle pace!

tenir.of: Il tint la tere Datliun e Balbiun.
tenir.tr: He held the land of Dathan and Abiram.

tenir.of: «Ceste bataille ben la puum tenir,
tenir.tr: «This battle we can well sustain,

tenir.of: Tient Durendal, ki ben trenchet e taillet,
tenir.tr: Holds Durendal, which cuts and slashes well,

tenir.of: Tient Halteclere, sanglent en est l'acer,
tenir.tr: Grasps Halteclere, its steel is bloody,

tenir.of: Tient Durendal, qui plus valt que fin ór.
tenir.tr: He grasps Durendal, which is worth more than fine gold.

tenir.of: Ki tint Valeri e envers sur le Rosne.
tenir.tr: Who held Valence and the lands along the Rhône.

tenir.of: [L]i quens Rollant tint s'espee sanglente.
tenir.tr: Count Roland held his bloodied sword.

tenir.of: Del corn qu'il tient l'oiïe en est mult grant:
tenir.tr: Of the horn he holds the sound is very great:

tenir.of: Tient Durendal, cume vassal i fiert.
tenir.tr: He holds Durendal, and strikes like a brave warrior.

tenir.of: Ki tint Kartagene, Alfrere, Garmalie
tenir.tr: Who held Carthage, Alfrere, Garmalie

tenir.of: Tient Halteclere, dunt li acer fut bruns,
tenir.tr: He grips Halteclere, whose steel was burnished,

tenir.of: Paien l'entendent, nel tindrent mie en gab;
tenir.tr: The pagans hear it, they do not take it as a jest;

tenir.of: Ki tint la marche del val de Runers.
tenir.tr: Who held the march of the vale of Runers.

tenir.of: E pur prozdomes tenir e cunseiller,
tenir.tr: And for upholding worthy men and counselling them,

tenir.of: Pur lei tenir e pur humes atraire.
tenir.tr: For upholding the law and for drawing men to it.

tenir.of: Tient l'olifan, que unkes perdre ne volt,
tenir.tr: He holds the oliphant, which he never wished to lose,

tenir.of: Ne l'orrat hume, ne t'en tienget por fol.
tenir.tr: No man will hear of it who does not hold you a fool for it.

tenir.of: Que Carles tient, ki la barbe ad canue!
tenir.tr: Which Charles holds, he of the hoary beard!

tenir.of: Mult bon vassal vos ad lung tens tenue:
tenir.tr: A very good vassal has long held you:

tenir.of: E Engletere, que il teneit sa cambre;
tenir.tr: And England, which he held as his own chamber;

tenir.of: Que Carles tient, ki ad la barbe blanche.
tenir.tr: Which Charles holds, he whose beard is white.

tenir.of: Que Carles les tent, ki la barbe ad flurie.
tenir.tr: Which Charles holds, he whose beard has flowered white.

tenir.of: Desur sun braz teneit le chef enclin;
tenir.tr: Upon his arm he held his head bowed;

tenir.of: Tenent l'enchalz, tuit en sunt cumunel.
tenir.tr: They keep up the pursuit, all of them are in it together.

tenir.of: En dous chaeines si teneit un brohun.
tenir.tr: In two chains he held a bear.

tenir.of: E li message par les mantels se tindrent,
tenir.tr: And the messengers held on to each other by the mantles,

tenir.of: E quatre cuntes l'estreu li unt tenut.
tenir.tr: And four counts held the stirrup for him.

tenir.of: Ne pois a vos tenir lung parlement:
tenir.tr: I cannot hold a long conversation with you:

tenir.of: Dist a Franceis: «Segnu[r]s, le pas tenez;
tenir.tr: He said to the French: «Lords, hold the pace;

tenir.of: Par mains le tienent .III. de ses barons.
tenir.tr: Three of his barons hold him by the hands.

tenir.of: A grant dulur tendrai puis mun reialme:
tenir.tr: In great grief I will hold my kingdom thereafter:

tenir.of: Tient sun espiet, sin fait brandir la hanste,
tenir.tr: He holds his spear, and makes its shaft quiver,

tenir.of: L'estreu li tindrent Neimes e Jocerans;
tenir.tr: Naimes and Joceran held the stirrup for him;

tenir.of: Tient sun espiet, si l'apelet Maltet:
tenir.tr: He holds his spear, and he calls it Maltet:

tenir.of: L'estreu li tint Marcules d'Ultremer.
tenir.tr: Marcules of Overseas held his stirrup for him.

tenir.of: N'avrat vertut ques tienget cuntre nus.» AOI.
tenir.tr: He will not have the strength to stand against us.» AOI.

tenir.of: Cil tint la terre entresqu'en Val Sevree.
tenir.tr: He held the land as far as Val Sevree.

tenir.of: N'escut ne bronie ne pout sun colp tenir:
tenir.tr: Neither shield nor hauberk could withstand his blow:

tenir.of: Morz est li gluz ki en destreit vus teneit;
tenir.tr: Dead is the wretch who held you in distress;

tenir.of: Geifreid d'Anjou ki l'enseigne teneit.
tenir.tr: Geoffrey of Anjou, who held the standard.

tenir.of: Si vait ferir celui ki le dragun teneit,
tenir.tr: And goes to strike the one who held the dragon,

tenir.of: A mailz de fer e a cuignees qu'ils tindrent,
tenir.tr: With iron mallets and with axes that they held,

tenir.of: Il est mes filz e si tendrat mes marches.»
tenir.tr: He is my son, and he will hold my marches.»

tenir.of: Respundent Franc: «Ore en tendrum cunseill.»
tenir.tr: The Franks answer: «Now we shall hold counsel on it.»

tenir.of: Pur Pinabel se cuntienent plus quei.
tenir.tr: For Pinabel they keep themselves the quietest.

tenir.of: Par anceisurs dei jo tel plait tenir.
tenir.tr: By my ancestors I must hold such a case.

tenir.of: Respont Tierri: «Ja n'en tendrai cunseill.
tenir.tr: Thierry answers: «I will never take counsel in this.

tirer.of: Tiret sa barbe cum hom ki est iret;
tirer.tr: He pulls his beard like a man who is angry;

tirer.of: Ploret des oilz, sa blanche bar[b]e tiret.
tirer.tr: He weeps from his eyes, he pulls at his white beard.

tirer.of: Pluret des oilz, tiret sa barbe blance:
tirer.tr: Weeps from his eyes, pulls at his white beard:

tirer.of: Pluret des oilz, sa barbe blanche tiret.
tirer.tr: He weeps from his eyes, tugs at his white beard.

toucher.of: Sur un mulet od un bastun tuchant.
toucher.tr: On a mule, prodding it with a stick.

toucher.of: Deus le guarit, qu'el(l) cors ne l'ad tuchet.
toucher.tr: God protects him, for it did not touch his body.

tourner.of: Sur mei avez turnet fals jugement.
tourner.tr: you have turned a false judgment upon me.

tourner.of: Guardez de nos ne turnez le curage.
tourner.tr: Take care that you do not turn your heart away from us.

tourner.of: Cuntre le ciel vait la mure turnant,
tourner.tr: Toward the sky he goes turning the point,

tourner.of: L'une meitiet li turnet cuntreval;
tourner.tr: One half of it he turns downward;

tourner.of: Apres li dist: «Turnet estes a perdre!» AOI.
tourner.tr: Afterward he says to him: «You are doomed to perish!» AOI.

tourner.of: Ja cil d'Espaigne ne s'en deivent turner liez.
tourner.tr: Those of Spain shall not return from here rejoicing.

tourner.of: Ansdous les oilz en la teste li turnent,
tourner.tr: Both his eyes turn back in his head,

tourner.of: Turnat sa teste vers la paiene gent;
tourner.tr: He turned his head toward the pagan people;

tourner.of: Envers Espaigne en ad turnet sun vis.
tourner.tr: Toward Spain he has turned his face.

tourner.of: De cels d'Espaigne unt lur les dos turnez,
tourner.tr: Those of Spain have turned their backs,

tourner.of: Env(er)ers les funz s'en turnerent alquanz;
tourner.tr: Some turned toward the depths;

tourner.of: Par Sebre amunt tut lur naviries turnent.
tourner.tr: Up the Ebro they turn all their fleets.

tourner.of: Vers lur païs avreit sun chef turnet;
tourner.tr: He would have turned his head toward their country;

tourner.of: La meie honor est turnet en declin.»
tourner.tr: My honor has turned to decline.»

tourner.of: Turnez ses oilz, mult li sunt tenebros.
tourner.tr: His eyes are rolled back, very dark to him now.

tourner.of: Turnet su[n] vis vers le soleill levant,
tourner.tr: Turns his face toward the rising sun,

tourner.of: Envers Karlun la mure en ad turnee. AOI.
tourner.tr: He has turned its point toward Charles. AOI.

tourner.of: Passet li jurz, si turnet a la vespree.
tourner.tr: The day passes, and turns toward evening.

tourner.of: Quant l'ot Marsilie, vers sa pareit se turnet,
tourner.tr: When Marsile hears it, he turns toward his wall,

tourner.of: Les alves turnent, les seles cheent a tere.
tourner.tr: The saddle-bows turn, the saddles fall to the ground.

tourner.of: Puis sunt turnet Bavier e Aleman
tourner.tr: Then the Bavarians and Germans have turned away

tourner.of: Guenes est turnet a perdiciun grant;
tourner.tr: Ganelon is turned to great perdition;

trahir.of: Traït vos ad ki a guarder vos out.
trahir.tr: He who should have guarded you has betrayed you.

trahir.of: Cil l'at traït ki vos en roevet feindre.
trahir.tr: He who asks you to feign indifference has betrayed him.

trahir.of: Les .XII. pers ad traït por aveir.»
trahir.tr: The twelve peers he has betrayed for gain.»

trahir.of: Guenes est fels d'iço qu'il le traït;
trahir.tr: Ganelon is a villain in that he betrayed him;

trahir.of: Ki hume traïst, sei ocit e altroi. AOI.
trahir.tr: He who betrays a man kills himself and others. AOI.

trahir.of: Hom ki traïst altre, nen est dreiz qu'il s'en vant.
trahir.tr: A man who betrays another has no right to boast of it.

traire.of: Enceis qu'en seient. VII.C. espees traites.
traire.tr: Before seven hundred swords be drawn.

traire.of: Trait Durendal, sa bone espee nue,
traire.tr: He draws Durendal, his good naked sword,

traire.of: - «Ne la poi traire,» Oliver li respunt,
traire.tr: - «I could not draw it,» Oliver answers him,

traire.of: Danz Oliver trait ad sa bone espee,
traire.tr: Lord Oliver has drawn his good sword,

traire.of: Il trait Almace, s'espee de acer brun,
traire.tr: He draws Almace, his sword of burnished steel,
He draws out the oliphant, blows it feebly.

traire.of: Dist l'un a l'altre: «Ça vus traiez ami!
traire.tr: One says to another: «Come this way, friends!

traire.of: D'un arcbaleste ne poet traire un quarrel,
traire.tr: Farther than a crossbow can shoot a bolt,

traire.of: Trait ses chevels, si se cleimet caitive,
traire.tr: Tears at her hair and declares herself wretched,

traire.of: Trait ses crignels, pleines ses mains amsdous,
traire.tr: He pulls his hair, both hands full of it,

traire.of: Granz est e forz e trait as anceisurs.
traire.tr: He is tall and strong and takes after his forebears.

traire.of: Plus de cent milie espees i unt traites.
traire.tr: More than a hundred thousand swords they have drawn.

traire.of: Trait ad l'espee, le punt est de cristal,
traire.tr: He has drawn his sword, whose pommel is of crystal,

traire.of: Mult vassalment unt traites les espees.
traire.tr: Very valiantly they have drawn their swords.

traire.of: Li emperere devant sei l'ad fait traire. AOI.
traire.tr: The emperor has had him dragged before him. AOI.

trancher.of: De noz ostages ferat tre[n]cher les testes;
trancher.tr: He will have the heads of our hostages cut off;

trancher.of: Tanz colps ad pris de bons espiez trenchanz,
trancher.tr: So many blows has he taken from good sharp spears,

trancher.of: La destre oreille al premer uer trenchat,
trancher.tr: It tore off the right ear of the first beast,

trancher.of: Jo l'ocirai a mun espiet trenchant.
trancher.tr: I will kill him with my sharp spear.

trancher.of: Trenchet le piz, si li briset les os,
trancher.tr: Slashes his chest, and breaks his bones,

trancher.of: Trenchet li le coer, le firie e le pulmun,
trancher.tr: He cuts through his heart, his liver, and his lung,

trancher.of: Que tut li trenchet le vermeill e le blanc;
trancher.tr: So that he cuts clean through the red and the white;

trancher.of: Trenchet la cors e la cheveleüre,
trancher.tr: He cuts through the scalp and the hair,

trancher.of: Si li trenchat les oilz e la faiture,
trancher.tr: And cut through the eyes and the face,

trancher.of: Trenchet l'eschine, hunc n'i out quis [joi]nture,
trancher.tr: He cuts through the spine, never seeking a joint there,

trancher.of: Tient Durendal, ki ben trenchet e taillet,
trancher.tr: Holds Durendal, which cuts and slashes well,

trancher.of: Trenchet le cors e [la] bronie safree,
trancher.tr: Cleaves the body and the gilded mail-coat,

trancher.of: E al ceval a l'eschine trenchee;
trancher.tr: And cut through the horse's spine;

trancher.of: Le cors li trenchet tres l'un costet qu'a l'altre,
trancher.tr: He cleaves his body from one side to the other,

trancher.of: Escababi i ad le chef trenchet;
trancher.tr: He has cut off the head of Escababi;

trancher.of: Trenchet la teste e la bronie e le cors,
trancher.tr: He slices through the head and the hauberk and the body,

trancher.of: Tut li trenchat le vermeill e l'azur;
trancher.tr: He cuts clean through the vermilion and the azure;

trancher.of: Trenchet le nes e la buche e les denz,
trancher.tr: Cuts through the nose and the mouth and the teeth,

trancher.of: Tren[chen]t cez poinz, cez costez, cez eschines,
trancher.tr: They cut through these fists, these flanks, these spines,

trancher.of: Faldrun de Pui i ad par mi trenchet,
trancher.tr: He has cut Faldrun of Pui clean through the middle,

trancher.of: Trenchet li ad li quens le destre poign.
trancher.tr: the count has cut off his right fist.

trancher.of: Trenchet la teste d'ici qu'as denz menuz,
trancher.tr: He cleaves the head down to the fine teeth,

trancher.of: Trenchet cez hanstes e cez escuz buclers,
trancher.tr: He slices through those lances and those bossed shields,

trancher.of: Li quens Rollant li trenchat ier le destre poign.
trancher.tr: Count Roland cut off his right hand yesterday.

trancher.of: Si li trenchat li quens Rollant, li riches.
trancher.tr: For Count Roland, the mighty, cut it off for him.

trancher.of: Si vunt ferir de lur espiez trenchanz. AOI.
trancher.tr: So they go to strike with their sharp spears. AOI.

trancher.of: Succurez le a voz espiez trenchant!»
trancher.tr: Help him with your sharp spears!»

trancher.of: Al brant d'acer l'en trenchet .V. des laz,
trancher.tr: With the steel blade he cuts five of its laces away,

trancher.of: Trenchet la coife entresque a la char,
trancher.tr: He cuts the coif down to the flesh,

trancher.of: Trenchent les quirs e cez fuz ki sunt dubles;
trancher.tr: They cut the leathers and the wooden boards that are double;

trancher.of: [T]renchet la teste pur la cervele espandre
trancher.tr: Cuts the head so as to spill the brains

transmettre.of: Que li tramist li reis de Suatilie;
transmettre.tr: Which the king of Suatilie had sent to him;

transmettre.of: «Li reis Marsilie m'ad tramis ses messages;
transmettre.tr: «King Marsile has sent me his messengers;

transmettre.of: Dous de voz cuntes al paien tramesistes,
transmettre.tr: Two of your counts you sent to the pagan,

transmettre.of: Se lui lessez, n'i trametrez plus saive.»
transmettre.tr: If you leave him aside, you will not send a wiser one.»

transmettre.of: Si la tramist li amiralz de Primes.
transmettre.tr: The emir of Primes sent it to me thus.

transmettre.of: Si li tramist li amiralz Galafes.
transmettre.tr: And the emir Galafe sent it on to him.

transmettre.of: Dist al paien: «Deus tut mal te tramette!
transmettre.tr: He said to the pagan: «May God send you every evil!

travailler.of: Lui e altrui travaillent, e cunfundent.»
travailler.tr: They torment him and others, and bring ruin.»

travailler.of: Par tantes teres ad sun cors traveillet,
travailler.tr: Through so many lands he has worn out his body,

traverser.tr: They pass ten gates, they cross four bridges,

tressaillir.of: Fait sun eslais, si tressalt un fosset,
tressaillir.tr: Makes his dash and leaps over a ditch,

troubler.of: Tant ad seinet (ki) li oil li sunt trublet;
troubler.tr: He has bled so much that his eyes are clouded;

trousser.of: D'or e d'argent .IIII. cenz muls trussez,
trousser.tr: four hundred mules loaded with gold and silver,

trousser.of: Franc desherbergent, funt lur sumers trosser:
trousser.tr: The Franks break camp, have their pack-horses loaded:

trousser.of: Par tel air l'at estrussee e brandie,
trousser.tr: With such force he wrenched and brandished it,

trousser.of: De sul le fer fust uns mulez trusset.
trousser.tr: The iron alone would be a mule's load.

trouver.of: Se en rereguarde troevet le cors Rollant,
trouver.tr: If in the rearguard he finds Roland's person,

trouver.of: Qu'en rereguarde trover le poüsum.»
trouver.tr: That we may find him in the rearguard.»

trouver.of: Sel pois trover a port ne a passage,
trouver.tr: If I can find him at pass or defile,

trouver.of: Si li truvez ki tres bien li aiut!»
trouver.tr: And find him someone who may aid him well!»

trouver.of: Se truis Rollant, ne lerrai que nel mat!»
trouver.tr: If I find Roland, I will not fail to bring him down!»

trouver.of: Se truis Rollant, de mort serat finet,
trouver.tr: If I find Roland, he will be finished by death,

trouver.of: Se trois Rollant, de mort li duins fiance.
trouver.tr: If I find Roland, I pledge him to death.

trouver.of: Se trois Rollant, n'en porterat la teste,
trouver.tr: If I find Roland, he will not carry away his head,

trouver.of: Se trois Rollant li proz enmi ma veie,
trouver.tr: If I find Roland the brave in my path,

trouver.of: Truverunt nos e morz e detrenchez,
trouver.tr: They will find us both dead and cut to pieces,

trouver.of: Cuntre un des noz en truverat morz .XV.,
trouver.tr: For one of ours he will find fifteen of them dead,

trouver.of: Tels .IIII. cenz i troevet entur lui:
trouver.tr: He finds four hundred of them around him:

trouver.of: Iloec truvat Gerin e Gerer sun cumpaignun.
trouver.tr: There he found Gerin and Gerer his companion.

trouver.of: E si truvat Berenger e Attun;
trouver.tr: And he found Berenger and Atto;

trouver.of: Iloec truvat Anseïs e Sansun,
trouver.tr: There he found Anseïs and Samson,

trouver.of: Truvat Gerard le veill de Russillun.
trouver.tr: He found Gerard the old, of Roussillon.

trouver.of: Sun cumpaignun ad truvet, Oliver:
trouver.tr: He has found his companion, Oliver:

trouver.of: Se jo truis ó, mult grant bataille i ert;
trouver.tr: If I find [them] there, a very great battle will be fought;

trouver.of: Plus pres d'ici purrez truver les Francs.
trouver.tr: Nearer here you can find the Franks.

trouver.of: Dist Baligant: «Que avez vos truvet?
trouver.tr: Baligant said: «What have you found?

trouver.of: Des morz qu'il troevet cumencet a plurer.
trouver.tr: At the dead he finds there he begins to weep.

trouver.of: Pur mun nev[ol]d que vuldreie truver.
trouver.tr: To find my nephew, whom I would wish to find.

trouver.of: De tantes herbes el pre truvat les flors,
trouver.tr: Of so many herbs he found the flowers in the meadow,

trouver.of: Tuz lur amis qu'il i unt morz truvet,
trouver.tr: All their friends whom they found dead there,

trouver.of: S'il troevent oí, bataille quident rendre.
trouver.tr: If they find them today, they expect to give battle.

trouver.of: S'il troevent oí, bataille i ert mult grant. AOI.
trouver.tr: If they find them today, there will be a very great battle. AOI.

trouver.of: Par sun orgoill li ad un num truvet:
trouver.tr: Out of his pride he has found a name for it:

trouver.of: Quant Carles veit que morte l'ad truvee,
trouver.tr: When Charles sees that he has found her dead,

trouver.of: Truvee li unt le num de Juliane.
trouver.tr: They have found for her the name of Juliana.

trébucher.of: Cheent li rei, a tere se turbecherent,
trébucher.tr: The kings fall, tumble to the ground,

trépasser.of: Ne trespassast ses hume[s] e ses pers;
trépasser.tr: Without having gone beyond his men and his peers;

user.of: Il est mult vielz, si ad sun tens uset;
user.tr: He is very old, and has worn out his time;

vaincre.of: Li reis Marsilie est de guere vencud:
vaincre.tr: King Marsile is defeated in war:

vaincre.of: Ses citez arses e ses humes vencuz;
vaincre.tr: Burned his cities and vanquished his men;

vaincre.of: Tanz riches reis morz e vencuz en champ:
vaincre.tr: So many rich kings dead and vanquished in the field:

vaincre.of: Il ne sevent, liquels d'els la veintrat.
vaincre.tr: They do not know which of the two will win it.

vaincre.of: Faites batailles e vencues en champ!
vaincre.tr: Fought battles and won them in the field!

vaincre.of: El camp estez, que ne seium vencuz!
vaincre.tr: Hold the field, that we be not vanquished!»

vaincre.of: Ferez i, Francs, kar tres ben les veincrum!»
vaincre.tr: Strike, Franks, for we shall surely defeat them!»

vaincre.of: Par tel glutun n'ert bataille oi vencue.»
vaincre.tr: By such a villain a battle will not be won today.»

vaincre.of: Respunt Rollant: «Vencut est le culvert.
vaincre.tr: Roland answers: «The villain is vanquished.

vaincre.of: «Ferez paien, car tres ben les veintrum!»
vaincre.tr: «Strike, pagans, for we shall vanquish them right well!»

vaincre.of: Mort sunt si hume, sis unt paiens (...) vencut;
vaincre.tr: His men are dead, and the pagans have defeated them;

vaincre.of: E dist un mot: «Ne sui mie vencut!
vaincre.tr: And says one word: «I am not defeated!

vaincre.of: Ja n'ert vencut pur nul hume carnel.
vaincre.tr: He will never be defeated by any mortal man.

vaincre.of: Pur orgoillos veincre e esmaier,
vaincre.tr: For overcoming the proud and dismaying them,

vaincre.of: E pur glutun veincre e esmaier,
vaincre.tr: And for overcoming the wicked and dismaying them,

vaincre.of: E dist un mot: «Vencut est li nies Carles!
vaincre.tr: And says a word: «Charles's nephew is conquered!

vaincre.of: Tantes batailles en camp en ai vencues.
vaincre.tr: So many battles in the field I have won with you,

vaincre.of: Mais ço ne set liquels veint ne quels nun.
vaincre.tr: But he cannot tell which one wins and which does not.

vaincre.of: Mais Deus ne volt qu'il seit mort ne vencut.
vaincre.tr: But God does not wish him to be dead or conquered.

vaincre.of: E! gentilz reis, ja sunt vencuz noz humes,
vaincre.tr: Oh! noble king, our men are already conquered,

vaincre.of: E Carles ad sa bataille vencue.
vaincre.tr: And Charles has won his battle.

vaincre.of: A icest colp est li esturs vencut.
vaincre.tr: With this blow the combat is won.

vaincre.of: Quant Tierris ad vencue sa bataille,
vaincre.tr: When Thierry has won his battle,

valoir.of: Jamais n'ert hume ki encuntre lui vaille.» AOI.
valoir.tr: Never will there be a man who can match himself against him.» AOI.

valoir.of: Melz en valt l'or que ne funt cinc cenz livres:
valoir.tr: their gold is worth more than five hundred pounds:

valoir.of: Eles valent mielz que tut l'aveir de Rume,
valoir.tr: They are worth more than all the wealth of Rome,

valoir.of: Plus valt Mahum que seint Perre de Rume!
valoir.tr: Muhammad is worth more than Saint Peter of Rome!

valoir.of: Sis bons escuz un dener ne li valt:
valoir.tr: His good shield is not worth a denier to him:

valoir.of: Fers e acers i deit aveir valor.
valoir.tr: Iron and steel ought to be of worth here.

valoir.of: Enpres sun colp ne quid que un dener vaillet,
valoir.tr: After his blow I think it is not worth a denier,

valoir.of: Tient Durendal, qui plus valt que fin ór.
valoir.tr: He grasps Durendal, which is worth more than fine gold.

valoir.of: Fuïr s'en voel, mais ne li valt nient:
valoir.tr: He wishes to flee from it, but it avails him nothing:

valoir.of: Mielz valt mesure que ne fait estultie.
valoir.tr: Moderation is worth more than recklessness.

valoir.of: De ço qui calt? car ne lur valt nient.
valoir.tr: But what use is it? It avails them nothing.
Or otherwise he is not worth four deniers;

valoir.of: Tutes lor leis un dener ne lur valt.
valoir.tr: All their laws are not worth a penny to them.

valoir.of: Li capelers un dener ne li valt;
valoir.tr: The cap is not worth a penny to him;

vanter.of: N'en vanteras el regne dunt tu fus
vanter.tr: Will you boast, in the realm from which you came,

vanter.of: Si se vant(t)[er]ent mi vaillant chevaler
Hom ki traïst altre, nen est dreiz qu'il s'en vant.
vanter.tr: A man who betrays another has no right to boast of it.

vendre.of: Qu'en Sarraguce sa maisnee alat vendre;
vendre.tr: When he went to Saragossa to sell his household;

vendre.of: Tel as ocis que mult cher te quid vendre!»
vendre.tr: You have killed one such that I think I will sell him to you very dear!»

vendre.of: Einz que il moergent, se vendrunt mult cher.
vendre.tr: Before they die, they will sell themselves very dear.

vendre.of: Mais tut seit fel cher ne se vende primes!
vendre.tr: But cursed be whoever does not sell himself dearly first!

vendre.of: Sempres murrai, mais cher me sui vendut!»
vendre.tr: Soon I shall die, but I have sold myself dear!»

venger.of: Si vengez cels que li fels fist ocire!» AOI.
venger.tr: And avenge those whom the villain had killed!» AOI.

venger.of: Li emperere nos devreit ben venger.
venger.tr: The emperor ought well to avenge us.

venger.of: Respont li quens: «Deus le me doinst venger!»
venger.tr: The count replies: «May God grant me to avenge him!»

venger.of: Venget li reis, si nus purrat venger;
venger.tr: Let the king come, for he will be able to avenge us;

venger.of: Jamais n'iert home plus se voeillet venger.
venger.tr: Never will a man be more eager to take revenge.

venger.of: Li nostre deu, vengez nos de Carlun.
venger.tr: O our gods, avenge us on Charles!

venger.of: Kar de vos sul ai ben venget les noz.»
venger.tr: For through you alone I have well avenged our men.»

venger.of: De lui venger ja mais ne li ert lez.
venger.tr: Never will it be pleasant for him to avenge himself.

venger.of: Carles repairet, ki ben nus vengerat.»
venger.tr: Charles is coming back, who will avenge us well.»

venger.of: Venger te poez de la gent criminel.»
venger.tr: You can avenge yourself on the criminal people.»

venger.of: Li reis Marsilie enqui serat venget:
venger.tr: King Marsile will be avenged here:

venger.of: Que mun nevold pois[se] venger Rollant!»
venger.tr: That I may avenge my nephew Roland!»

venger.of: Vengez voz fi[l]z, voz freres e voz heirs,
venger.tr: Avenge your sons, your brothers, and your heirs,

venger.of: S'or n'i ferez pur venger vostre hunte.»
venger.tr: If you do not strike now to avenge your shame.»

venger.of: Ço dist li reis: «Seignurs, vengez voz doels,
venger.tr: The king said: «Lords, avenge your sorrows,

venger.of: Venget m'en sui, mais n'i ad traïsun.»
venger.tr: I have avenged myself, but there is no treason in it.»

venir.of: En cest païs nos est venuz cunfundre.
venir.tr: Has come into this land to destroy us.

venir.of: Vendrat li jurz, si passerat li termes,
venir.tr: The day will come, and so the term will pass,

venir.of: Vindrent a Charles ki France ad en baillie:
venir.tr: They came to Charles, who has France in his keeping:

venir.of: La noit demurent tresque vint al jur cler.
venir.tr: The night they remain until the bright day came.

venir.of: Ensembl' od els li quens Rollant i vint,
venir.tr: Together with them Count Roland came there,

venir.of: Guenes i vint, ki la traïsun fist.
venir.tr: Guenes came there, who committed the treason.

venir.of: En piez se drecet, si li vint cuntredire.
venir.tr: Rises to his feet, and came to contradict him.

venir.of: Set anz [ad] pleins, que en Espaigne venimes;
venir.tr: Seven full years it is, since we came into Spain;

venir.of: En piez se drecet, si vint devant Carlun,
venir.tr: He rises to his feet, and came before Charles,

venir.of: Apres iço i est Neimes venud;
venir.tr: After this, Naimes came forward;

venir.of: Ço dist li reis: «Guenes venez avant. AOI.
venir.tr: The king said: «Ganelon, come forward. AOI.

venir.of: Vint i ses nies, out vestue sa brunie,
venir.tr: His nephew came, had donned his hauberk,

venir.of: Blancandrins vint devant l'empereür;
venir.tr: Blancandrin came before the emperor;

venir.of: En Sarraguce vus vendrat aseger;
venir.tr: He will come to besiege you in Saragossa;

venir.of: E Blancandrins i vint, al canud peil,
venir.tr: And Blancandrin came there, with the hoary hair,

venir.of: Puis si cumencet a venir ses tresors. AOI.
venir.tr: Then he begins to bring forth his treasures. AOI.

venir.of: A tant i vint uns paiens, Valdabruns:
venir.tr: Thereupon came a pagan, Valdabrun:

venir.of: Apres i vint un paien, Climorins.
venir.tr: After him came a pagan, Climorins.

venir.of: A tant i vint la reine Bramimunde.
venir.tr: Then came the queen Bramimonde.

venir.of: Venuz en est a la citet de Galne.
venir.tr: He has come to the city of Galne.

venir.of: Guenes li quens est venuz as herberges. AOI.
venir.tr: Ganelon the count has come to the encampment. AOI.

venir.of: Guenes i vint, li fels, li parjurez.
venir.tr: Ganelon came there, the felon, the perjurer.

venir.of: Devers Ardene vit venir uns leuparz,
venir.tr: From toward the Ardennes he saw a leopard coming,

venir.of: Que vint a Carles le galops e les salz,
venir.tr: Which came to Charles at a gallop and by leaps,

venir.of: Anpres iço i est Neimes venud:
venir.tr: After this Naimes came forward:

venir.of: Cuntre lui vient sis cumpainz Oliver;
venir.tr: Toward him comes his companion Oliver;

venir.of: Vint i Gerins e li proz quens Gerers,
venir.tr: There came Gerin and the valiant count Gerier,

venir.of: E vint i Otes, si i vint Berengers,
venir.tr: And there came Oton, and there came Berengier,

venir.of: E vint i Astors e Anseïs li veillz;
venir.tr: And there came Astor and Anseïs the old;

venir.of: Vint i Gerart de Rossillon li fiers;
venir.tr: There came Gerart of Roussillon the proud;

venir.of: Venuz i est li riches dux Gaifiers.
venir.tr: The mighty duke Gaifier has come there too.

venir.of: Puis que il venent a la Tere Majur,
venir.tr: When they come to the Great Land,

venir.of: Li nies Marsilie, il est venuz avant,
venir.tr: The nephew of Marsile, he has come forward,

venir.of: Ço dist Marsilie: «Seignurs, venez avant!
venir.tr: Marsile said this: «Lords, come forward!

venir.of: Venez i, reis, sil verrez veirement:
venir.tr: Come there, king, and you will truly see it:

venir.of: Curant i vint Margariz de Sibilie;
venir.tr: Margariz of Seville came running there;

venir.of: Vint en la presse, sur les altres s'escriet
venir.tr: He came into the throng, above the others he cries out

venir.of: Si veit venir cele gent paienur,
venir.tr: And sees the pagan host coming,

venir.of: «Devers Espaigne vei venir tel bruur,
venir.tr: «From the direction of Spain I see such a tumult coming,

venir.of: Vint as Franceis, tut lur ad acuntet.
venir.tr: Came to the French, told them everything.

venir.of: Felun paien mar i vindrent as porz:
venir.tr: Ill-fated pagans, in an evil hour they came to the passes:

venir.of: Melz voeill murir que huntage me venget.
venir.tr: I would rather die than that shame befall me.

venir.of: Marsilie vient par mi une valee
venir.tr: Marsile comes through the middle of a valley

venir.of: D'Affrike i ad un Affrican venut,
venir.tr: From Africa there has come an African,

venir.of: Ki quel cumpert, venuz en sunt ensemble.
venir.tr: Whoever pays for it, they have come together.

venir.of: Sem(e) creïsez, venuz i fust mi sire;
venir.tr: Had you trusted me, my lord would have come here;

venir.of: Vint tresqu'a els, sis prist a castier:
venir.tr: Came right up to them, and began to rebuke them:

venir.of: Venget li reis, si nus purrat venger;
venir.tr: Let the king come, for he will be able to avenge us;

venir.of: Josque il vengent el camp cumunement:
venir.tr: Until they reach the field all together:

venir.of: Quant en cest camp vendrat Carles, mi sire,
venir.tr: When Charles, my lord, comes onto this field,

venir.of: Le cheval brochet, si vient poignant vers lui. AOI.
venir.tr: He spurs his horse and comes riding toward him. AOI.

venir.of: Mais saveir volt se Charles i vendrat:
venir.tr: But he wants to know whether Charles will come:

venir.of: Se Carles vient, de nus i avrat perte.
venir.tr: If Charles comes, we shall suffer loss from it.

venir.of: Li quens Rollant, quant il les veit venir,
venir.tr: Count Roland, when he sees them coming,

venir.of: A l'arcevesque en est venuz a tut,
venir.tr: And has come with them all to the archbishop,

venir.of: Si cum il poet a l'arcevesques en vent,
venir.tr: As best he can he comes with him to the archbishop,

venir.of: Ensembl'od els sent Gabriel i vint.
venir.tr: Together with them Saint Gabriel came there.

venir.of: Devers un gualt uns granz leons li vint,
venir.tr: From a wood a great lion came toward him,

venir.of: Apres icel li vien[t] un altre avisiun,
venir.tr: After that one there comes to him another vision,

venir.of: Devers Ardene veeit venir .XXX. urs,
venir.tr: From toward the Ardennes he saw thirty bears come,

venir.of: De pa(i)smeisuns en est venuz Marsilies:
venir.tr: Marsile has come back from his swoons:

venir.of: E cum il vienent en Espaigne la tere,
venir.tr: And when they come to Spain, the land,

venir.of: Issent de mer, venent as ewes dulces,
venir.tr: They leave the sea, they come to the fresh waters,

venir.of: A icel jur venent a Sarraguce. AOI.
venir.tr: On that day they come to Saragossa. AOI.

venir.of: Cuntre Franceis li sui venut aider.
venir.tr: That I have come to help him against the Franks.

venir.of: E a mei venget pur reconoistre sun feu.
venir.tr: And let him come to me to acknowledge his fief.

venir.of: Sur nus est venue male confusiun.
venir.tr: A wicked confusion has come upon us.

venir.of: Mun seignur dites qu'il me vienge veeir.
venir.tr: Tell my lord to come and see me.

venir.of: Fuiant s'en vint, qu'il n'i pout mes ester.
venir.tr: He came away fleeing, for he could stay there no longer.

venir.of: E Bramidonie vient curant cuntre lui;
venir.tr: And Bramimonde comes running toward him;

venir.of: Sus en la chambre ad doel en sunt venut. AOI.
venir.tr: Up in the chamber, in grief, they have come. AOI.

venir.of: Muntet el ceval, vient a sa gent puignant.
venir.tr: Mounts the horse, comes to his people at a gallop.

venir.of: «Venez paien, car ja s'en fuient Frant!» AOI.
venir.tr: «Come, pagans, for the Franks are already fleeing!» AOI.

venir.of: En Rencesvals en est Carles venuz.
venir.tr: Charles has come to Roncesvals.

venir.of: Carles li reis se vint de pasmeisuns;
venir.tr: Charles the king came round from his swoons;

venir.of: Cum en Espaigne venis [a] mal seignur!
venir.tr: How you came to Spain to an unlucky lord!

venir.of: De plusurs regnes vendrunt li hume estrange;
venir.tr: Men from many foreign kingdoms will come;

venir.of: Vendrunt li hume, demanderunt noveles;
venir.tr: The men will come and will ask for news;

venir.of: Einz que jo vienge as maistres porz de Sirie,
venir.tr: Before I come to the main passes of Syria,

venir.of: Venir s'en volt li emperere Carles,
venir.tr: Emperor Charles wants to be on his way,

venir.of: De cels devant i vindrent dui messages,
venir.tr: From those in front two messengers came,

venir.of: Si Arrabiz de venir ne se repentent,
venir.tr: If the Arabs do not repent of coming,

venir.of: Si Arrabiz de venir ne demurent,
venir.tr: If the Arabs do not delay in coming,

venir.of: N'i ad Franceis, si a lui vient juster,
venir.tr: There is no Frank who, if he comes to joust with him,

venir.of: De Val Fuit sun venuz en traver.
venir.tr: They have come from Val Fuit across the land.

venir.of: «Venez, paien, kar jo(n) irai en l'estree.»
venir.tr: «Come, pagans, for I shall go ahead on the way.»

venir.of: Ki errer voelt, a mei venir s'en alt!»
venir.tr: Whoever wishes to ride, let him come to me!»

venir.of: A icest mot paien venent avant,
venir.tr: At this word the pagans come forward,

venir.of: «Ferez, paien: por el venud n'i estes!
venir.tr: «Strike, pagans: you have not come here for anything else!

venir.of: Carles de France i vint, kil succurat. AOI.
venir.tr: Charles of France came there, and rescued him. AOI.

venir.of: Dist l'amiraill: «Jangleu, venez avant!
venir.tr: The emir said: «Jangleu, come forward!

venir.of: Ven mei servir d'ici qu'en Oriente!»
venir.tr: Come serve me from here as far as the East!»

venir.of: A icest mot venuz i est dux Neimes:
venir.tr: At this word Duke Naimes has come up:

venir.of: Prent la citet, od sa gent i est venue;
venir.tr: He takes the city, has come in with his people;

venir.of: Vint a Burdeles la citet de...
venir.tr: He came to Bordeaux, the city of...

venir.of: E vient a Ais, al meillor sied de France;
venir.tr: And comes to Aix, the best seat of France;

venir.of: Muntet el palais, est venut en la sale.
venir.tr: He goes up into the palace, has come into the hall.

venir.of: As li Alde venue, une bele damisele.
venir.tr: Behold Alde come, a fair maiden.

venir.of: Par mun saveir vinc jo a guarisun.
venir.tr: By my own wit I came to safety.

venir.of: Devant lu rei est venuz Pinabel,
venir.tr: Before the king Pinabel has come,

venir.of: Venuz i est li emperere Carles,
venir.tr: Emperor Charles has come there,

venir.of: Vienent ad Ais, descendent en la place.
venir.tr: They come to Aix, they dismount in the square.

venir.of: Pur Guenelun erent a plait venuz,
venir.tr: They had come to the trial for Ganelon,

venir.of: Seint Gabriel de part Deu li vint dire:
venir.tr: Saint Gabriel on God's behalf came to tell him:

verser.of: Rumpent cez cengles e cez seles verserent,
verser.tr: They break the girths and overturned the saddles,

violer.of: Les castels pris, (. . .) les citez violees.
violer.tr: taken the castles, (. . .) violated the cities.
And violated the temple of Solomon,

violer.of: E mes citez fraites e violees.
violer.tr: And broken and violated my cities.

vivre.of: Ne l'amerai a trestut mun vivant,
vivre.tr: I shall not love him all the days of my life,

vivre.of: Tant ad erret nen est dreiz que plus vivet.
vivre.tr: He has gone so far that it is not right that he live longer.

vivre.of: - «Ço n'iert,» dist Guenes: «tant cum vivet sis niés:
vivre.tr: - «That will not be,» said Ganelon, «as long as his nephew lives:

vivre.of: - «Ço n'iert,» dist Guenes, «tant cum vivet Rollant:
vivre.tr: - «That will not be,» said Ganelon, «so long as Roland lives:

vivre.of: Soürs est Carlles, ne (cre) crent hume vivant.» AOI.
vivre.tr: Charles is secure, he fears no living man.» AOI.

vivre.of: «Que ço seit dit de nul hume vivant,
vivre.tr: «That it be said by any living man,

vivre.of: Ultre cest jurn ne serum plus vivant;
vivre.tr: Beyond this day we shall be alive no longer;

vivre.of: E or sai ben n'avons guaires a vivre;
vivre.tr: And now I know well we have not much longer to live;

vivre.of: Quant tu es mor[t], dulur est que jo vif!»
vivre.tr: Since you are dead, it is grief that I live!»

vivre.of: Jo oi al corner que guaires ne vivrat.
vivre.tr: I hear by the blowing that he will not live long.

vivre.of: Se R[ollant] vit, nostre guere renovelet,
vivre.tr: If Roland lives, our war is renewed,

vivre.of: Si grant dol ai que ne voldreie vivre,
vivre.tr: I have such great grief that I would not wish to live,

vivre.of: Se jo vif alques, mult grant prod i avreiz.»
vivre.tr: If I live a while, you will gain great profit from it.»

vivre.of: Apres Rollant que jo vive remaigne!»
vivre.tr: That I remain alive after Roland!»

vivre.of: Vivre le laisez, car mult est gentilz hoem.
vivre.tr: Let him live, for he is a very noble man.

vivre.of: Respundent Franc: «Ja mar en vivrat uns!»
vivre.tr: The Franks answer: «Never shall a single one live!»

voir.of: L'ost des Franceis verrez sempres desfere.
voir.tr: You will soon see the host of the Franks disband.

voir.of: Ja einz ne verrat passer cest premer meis,
voir.tr: He will not see this first month pass

voir.of: Par ceste barbe que veez [blancheier],
voir.tr: By this beard that you see growing white,

voir.of: Sin vois vedeir alques de sun semblant.»
voir.tr: And go see something of his disposition.»

voir.of: Quant ço veit Guenes que ore s'en rit Rollant,
voir.tr: When Ganelon sees that Roland now laughs about it,

voir.of: Dreiz emperere, veiz me ci en present,
voir.tr: Rightful emperor, here you see me present,

voir.of: Gua[r]dez le ben, ja nel verrai des oilz.»
voir.tr: Guard him well, for I shall never see him again with my eyes.»

voir.of: La veïsez tant chevaler plorer,
voir.tr: There you would have seen so many knights weep,

voir.of: Quant le vit Guenes, mist la main a l'espee,
voir.tr: When Ganelon saw it, he put his hand to his sword,

voir.of: Guardet al bref, vit la raisun escrite:
voir.tr: He looks at the letter, saw the writing set down there:

voir.of: N'est hom kil veit e conuistre le set
voir.tr: There is no man who sees him and comes to know him

voir.of: «Jo ai tel gent, plus bele ne verreiz;
voir.tr: «I have such troops, you will never see finer;

voir.of: Carlles verrat sun grant orguill cadeir;
voir.tr: Charles will see his great pride fall;

voir.of: «Tenez mun helme, unches meillor ne vi.
voir.tr: «Take my helmet, never did I see a better one.

voir.of: Kar a mes oilz vi .IIII.C. milie armez,
voir.tr: For with my own eyes I saw four hundred thousand armed men,

voir.of: La sunt neiez, jamais nes en verrez;
voir.tr: There they were drowned, never will you see them again;

voir.of: Ja ne verrez cest premer meis passet
voir.tr: Never will you see this first month pass

voir.of: Devers Ardene vit venir uns leuparz,
voir.tr: From toward the Ardennes he saw a leopard coming,

voir.of: «Veez les porz e les destreiz passages:
voir.tr: «You see the passes and the narrow defiles:

voir.of: Virent Guascuigne, la tere lur seignur.
voir.tr: They saw Gascony, the land of their lord.

voir.of: De cels de France virent les gunfanuns.
voir.tr: Of those of France they saw the banners.

voir.of: Veez m'espee, ki est e bone e lunge:
voir.tr: See my sword, which is both good and long:

voir.of: Venez i, reis, sil verrez veirement:
voir.tr: Come there, king, and you will truly see it:

voir.of: Cele nel veit vers lui ne s'esclargisset;
voir.tr: None sees him but she brightens toward him;

voir.of: Quant ele le veit, ne poet muer ne riet;
voir.tr: When she sees him, she cannot help but smile;

voir.of: Veez m'espee, ki d'or est enheldie:
voir.tr: Behold my sword, which is hilted with gold:

voir.of: Si veit venir cele gent paienur,
voir.tr: And sees the pagan host coming,

voir.of: «Devers Espaigne vei venir tel bruur,
voir.tr: «From the direction of Spain I see such a tumult coming,

voir.of: Or veit il ben d'Espaigne le regnet
voir.tr: Now he sees clearly the realm of Spain

voir.of: Dist Oliver: «Jo ai paiens veüz:
voir.tr: Oliver said: «I have seen the pagans:

voir.of: Unc mais nuls hom en tere n'en vit plus.
voir.tr: never before did any man on earth see more of them.

voir.of: Tut en verrez le brant ensanglentet.
voir.tr: You will see its blade all bloodied because of it.

voir.of: De Durendal verrez l'acer sanglent.
voir.tr: You will see the bloody steel of Durendal.

voir.of: Jo ai veüt les Sarrazins d'Espaigne,
voir.tr: I have seen the Saracens of Spain,

voir.of: Dist Oliver: «Rollant, veez en alques!
voir.tr: Said Oliver: «Roland, look over there a bit!

voir.of: Veeir poez, dolente est la rereguarde;
voir.tr: You can see, the rearguard is to be pitied;

voir.of: Quant Rollant veit que la bataille serat,
voir.tr: When Roland sees that the battle will take place,

voir.of: Kar a voz oilz veez les Sarrazins.
voir.tr: For with your own eyes you see the Saracens.

voir.of: Asez ad doel quant vit mort sun nevold,
voir.tr: He has great grief when he sees his nephew dead,

voir.of: Guardet a tere, veit gesir le glutun,
voir.tr: He looks to the ground, sees the wretch lying there,

voir.of: Guardet arere, veit le glutun gesir,
voir.tr: He looks behind, sees the wretch lying there,

voir.of: Ki lui veïst l'un geter mort su[r] l'altre,
voir.tr: Whoever had seen him throw one dead upon another,

voir.of: Hume nel veit,ki mult ne s espaent.
voir.tr: No man sees it who is not greatly terrified.

voir.of: Unches mais hom tel ne vit ajustee.
voir.tr: Never did any man see such a one joined.

voir.of: Marsilies veit de sa gent le martirie,
voir.tr: Marsile sees the slaughter of his people,

voir.of: Unches nuls hom nel vit juer ne rire.
voir.tr: Never did any man see him play or laugh.

voir.of: Cum il le vit, a ferir le desiret.
voir.tr: As soon as he saw him, he longed to strike him.

voir.of: Franceis veient que paiens i ad tant,
voir.tr: The French see that there are so many pagans there,

voir.of: Li quens Rollant, quant il veit Sansun mort,
voir.tr: Count Roland, when he sees Samson dead,

voir.of: Enceis nel vit, sil recunut veirement
voir.tr: Never before had he seen him, yet he recognized him truly

voir.of: La veïssez si grant dulor de gent,
voir.tr: There you would have seen such great suffering of people,

voir.of: Ki puis veïst Rollant e Oliver
voir.tr: Whoever then might have seen Roland and Oliver

voir.of: Li quens Rollant des soens i veit grant perte; AOI.
voir.tr: Count Roland sees great loss among his own men; AOI.

voir.of: Tanz bons vassals veez gesir par tere!
voir.tr: So many good vassals you see lying upon the ground!

voir.of: Se puis veeir ma gente sorur Alde,
voir.tr: If I can see my fair sister Alde again,

voir.of: Vostre proecce, Rollant, mar la ve[ï]mes!
voir.tr: Your prowess, Roland, in an evil hour did we see it!

voir.of: «Se veïssum Rollant einz qu'il fust mortz,
voir.tr: «If only we might see Roland before he is dead,

voir.of: De cels de France i veit tanz morz gesir!
voir.tr: of those of France he sees so many lying dead!

voir.of: Meillors vassals de vos unkes ne vi.
voir.tr: Better vassals than you I never saw.

voir.of: Barons Franceis, pur mei vos vei murir:
voir.tr: French barons, for my sake I see you die:

voir.of: De Sarrazins verrat tel discipline,
voir.tr: He will see such slaughter of Saracens,

voir.of: Quan Rollant veit la contredite gent
voir.tr: When Roland sees the accursed people,

voir.of: Quant paien virent que Franceis i out poi,
voir.tr: When the pagans saw that the French were few there,

voir.of: Ne a muiler ne a dame qu'aies veüd,
voir.tr: But neither to wife nor to lady whom you have seen

voir.of: Ki lui veïst Sarrazins desmembrer,
voir.tr: Whoever had seen him dismember the Saracens,

voir.of: Ne loinz ne pres (es) ne poet vedeir si cler
voir.tr: Neither far nor near can he see clearly enough

voir.of: Jo ne vos vei, veied vus Damnedeu!
voir.tr: I do not see you, may the Lord God see you!

voir.of: Or veit Rollant que mort est sun ami,
voir.tr: Now Roland sees that his friend is dead,

voir.of: Li quens Rollant, quant il les veit venir,
voir.tr: Count Roland, when he sees them coming,

voir.of: Ja ne verrai le riche empereuür!»
voir.tr: I shall never again see the mighty emperor!»

voir.of: Li quens Rollant, quant il veit mort ses pers,
voir.tr: Count Roland, when he sees his peers dead,

voir.of: Li arcevesques quant vit pasmer Rollant,
voir.tr: The archbishop, when he saw Roland swoon,

voir.of: La veit gesir le nobilie barun,
voir.tr: There he sees lying the noble baron,

voir.of: Li quens Rollant veit l'ar[ce]vesque a tere:
voir.tr: Count Roland sees the archbishop on the ground:

voir.of: Defors sun cors veit gesir la buele;
voir.tr: Outside his body he sees the bowels lie;

voir.of: Quant il ço vit que n'en pout mie freindre,
voir.tr: When he saw that he could not break it at all,

voir.of: Quant veit li quens que ne la freindrat mie,
voir.tr: When the count sees that he will not break it,

voir.of: «Veez avant de dous liwes de nus,
voir.tr: «Look ahead, two leagues from us,

voir.of: Ve[d]e[i]r puez les granz chemins puldrus,
voir.tr: You can see the great dusty roads,

voir.of: Quant veit li reis le vespres decliner,
voir.tr: When the king sees the evening decline,

voir.of: Quant Carles veit que tuit sunt mort paiens,
voir.tr: When Charles sees that all the pagans are dead,

voir.of: Veit les tuneires e les venz e les giels,
voir.tr: Sees the thunders and the winds and the frosts,

voir.of: En grant dulor i veit ses chevalers.
voir.tr: In great anguish he sees his knights there.

voir.of: Devers Ardene veeit venir .XXX. urs,
voir.tr: From toward the Ardennes he saw thirty bears come,

voir.of: La vit li reis si merveillus estur;
voir.tr: There the king saw so astonishing a combat;

voir.of: Ja veez vos que a mort sui destreit,
voir.tr: You see now that I am hard pressed to death,

voir.of: Mun seignur dites qu'il me vienge veeir.
voir.tr: Tell my lord to come and see me.

voir.of: Li reis Marsilie, cum il veit Baligant,
voir.tr: King Marsile, when he sees Baligant,

voir.of: Si vunt ve[d]eir le merveillus damage
voir.tr: And go to see the terrible damage

voir.of: Sur l'erbe verte veit gesir sun nevuld;
voir.tr: He sees his nephew lying on the green grass;

voir.of: Guardet a la tere, veit sun nevold gesir.
voir.tr: He looks at the ground, sees his nephew lying there.

voir.of: Unques nuls hom tel chevaler ne vit
voir.tr: Never did any man see such a knight

voir.of: Guardet a tere, veit gesir sun nev[u]ld:
voir.tr: He looks at the ground, sees his nephew lying there:

voir.of: Veiz Baligant, ki apres tei chevalchet:
voir.tr: See Baligant, who rides after you:

voir.of: Encoi verrum se tu as vasselage.« AOI.
voir.tr: Today we shall see whether you have valor.»

voir.of: Fait sun eslais, veant cent mil humes, AOI.
voir.tr: He makes his charge in sight of a hundred thousand men, AOI.

voir.of: Quant Carles veit si beles cuntenances,
voir.tr: When Charles sees such fine bearing,

voir.of: «Veüd avum li orguillus reis Carles.
voir.tr: «We have seen the proud King Charles.

voir.of: Mult me merveill se ja verrum Carlun.»
voir.tr: I very much wonder whether we shall ever see Charles.»

voir.of: A itel ore unches puis ne la vit,
voir.tr: At such an hour that he never saw it afterwards,

voir.of: «Veez l'orgoil de France la loee!
voir.tr: «Look at the pride of France the praised!

voir.of: Unkes nuls hom ne vit tel ajustee.»
voir.tr: Never did any man see such a gathering.»

voir.of: Carles li magnes, cum il vit l'amiraill,
voir.tr: Charles the Great, when he sees the emir,

voir.of: Veez paien: felun sunt e cuart,
voir.tr: Look at the pagans: they are wicked and cowardly,

voir.of: Veez mun fils, Carlun le vait querant,
voir.tr: See my son, he goes seeking Charles,

voir.of: La veïsez la tere si junchee:
voir.tr: There you would see the earth so strewn:

voir.of: Bataille veit cil ki entr'els volt estre. AOI.
voir.tr: He sees battle who wishes to be among them. AOI.

voir.of: Quant Naimun veit nafret devant sei,
voir.tr: When he sees Naimes wounded before him,

voir.of: Ki puis veist li chevaler d'Arabe,
voir.tr: Whoever might then see the knights of Arabia,

voir.of: Ki dunc veïst cez escuz si malmis,
voir.tr: Whoever then might see those shields so battered,

voir.of: Cez chevalers ki dunc veïst caïr
voir.tr: Whoever then might see those knights fall,

voir.of: Unc ne vi gent ki si fust cumbatant.
voir.tr: I never saw a people so warlike.

voir.of: Quant de Franceis les escheles vit rumpre,
voir.tr: When he saw the battalions of the Franks breaking,

voir.of: «Veez paien cum ocient voz humes!
voir.tr: «See how the pagans are killing your men!

voir.of: Baligant veit sun gunfanun cadeir
voir.tr: Baligant sees his gonfalon fall

voir.of: Kar hoi matin vos vi plurer des oilz.»
voir.tr: For this morning I saw you weeping from your eyes.»

voir.of: Quant ele vit Arrabiz si cunfundre,
voir.tr: When she saw the Arabs so confounded,

voir.of: Li pelerin le veient ki la vunt.
voir.tr: The pilgrims who go there see it.

voir.of: Quant Carles veit que morte l'ad truvee,
voir.tr: When Charles sees that he has found her dead,

voir.of: E mun nevold, que ja mais ne verreiz,
voir.tr: And my nephew, whom you will never see again,

voir.of: Veit cels de France e tuz les jugeürs,
voir.tr: He sees those of France and all the judges,

voir.of: Quant Guenes veit que ses granz plaiz cumencet,
voir.tr: When Ganelon sees that his great trial begins,

voir.of: Ja por murir n'en ert veüd gerun,
voir.tr: Not by his dying will any gain of him be seen,

voir.of: Quant Carles veit que tuz li sunt faillid,
voir.tr: When Charles sees that all have failed him,

voir.of: Ci vei Tierri, ki jugement ad fait.
voir.tr: Here I see Thierry, who has pronounced judgment.

voir.of: Quant veit Tierri qu'or en ert la bataille,
voir.tr: When Thierry sees that the battle is now to be,

voir.of: Ço veit Tierris, que el vis est ferut:
voir.tr: Thierry sees this, that he is struck in the face:

voler.of: Qu'envers le cel en volent les escicles.
voler.tr: That toward the sky the splinters fly.

voler.of: Plus est isnels que n'est oisel ki volet;
voler.tr: Swifter is it than a bird that flies;

voler.of: Cuntre le ciel en volet li fous tuz clers.
voler.tr: Toward the sky the fire flies up, all bright.

vouloir.of: S'en volt ostages, e vos l'en enveiez,
vouloir.tr: If he wants hostages, then send them to him,

vouloir.of: Teres e fiéz tant cum vos en vuldrez.»
vouloir.tr: Lands and fiefs as much as you will want of them.»

vouloir.of: S'il voelt ostages, il en avrat par veir.»
vouloir.tr: If he wants hostages, he shall have them indeed.»

vouloir.of: De sun aveir vos voelt asez duner,
vouloir.tr: of his wealth he wishes to give you plenty,

vouloir.of: - «Voet par hostages,» ço dist li Sarrazins,
vouloir.tr: - «By hostages,» said the Saracen,

vouloir.of: La vuldrat il chrestiens devenir.»
vouloir.tr: There he will wish to become a Christian.»

vouloir.of: Par cels de France voelt il del tut errer. AOI.
vouloir.tr: Through those of France he wishes to act in everything. AOI.

vouloir.of: De sun aveir me voelt duner grant masse,
vouloir.tr: From his wealth he wishes to give me a great quantity,

vouloir.of: U par ostage vos (en) voelt faire soürs;
vouloir.tr: Or by hostages he wishes to give you assurance;

vouloir.of: Se li reis voelt, jo i puis aler ben.»
vouloir.tr: If the king wills it, I can well go there.»

vouloir.of: Si li reis voelt, prez sui por vus le face.» AOI.
vouloir.tr: If the king wishes, I am ready to do it for you.» AOI.

vouloir.of: Ademplir voeill vostre comandement.» AOI.
vouloir.tr: I will fulfill your command.» AOI.

vouloir.of: Mais li quens Guenes iloec ne volsist estre:
vouloir.tr: But Count Ganelon would not wish to be there:

vouloir.of: Ki tute gent voelt faire recreant,
vouloir.tr: He who wants to make every people cry for mercy,

vouloir.of: Pur les nuveles qu'il vuldreient oïr.
vouloir.tr: Because of the news they would wish to hear.

vouloir.of: Demi Espaigne vos voelt en fiu duner.
vouloir.tr: He wishes to give you half of Spain in fief.

vouloir.of: Se cest acorde ne vulez otrier,
vouloir.tr: If you will not grant this accord,

vouloir.of: Ferir l'en volt, se n'en fust desturnet. AOI.
vouloir.tr: He wished to strike him with it, had he not been prevented. AOI.

vouloir.of: Mais de s'espee ne volt mie guerpir;
vouloir.tr: But he would by no means give up his sword;

vouloir.of: Si ceste acorde ne volez otrier,
vouloir.tr: If you will not grant this accord,

vouloir.of: Se de mun cors voeil aquiter la vie,
vouloir.tr: If I wish to ransom the life of my body,

vouloir.of: En talant ai que mult vos voeill amer,
vouloir.tr: I have the desire that I much want to love you,

vouloir.of: De Carlemagne vos voeill oïr parler.
vouloir.tr: I want to hear you speak of Charlemagne.

vouloir.of: Meilz voelt murir que guerpir sun barnet.»
vouloir.tr: He would rather die than abandon his noble company.»

vouloir.of: De mun aveir vos voeill dunner grant masse:
vouloir.tr: Of my wealth I will give you a great quantity:

vouloir.of: Que il ne voelent ne tenir ne guarder.
vouloir.tr: Which they wish neither to hold nor to keep.

vouloir.of: Se Mahumet me voelt estre guarant,
vouloir.tr: If Muhammad is willing to be my protector,

vouloir.of: Pur tut l'or Deu ne volt estre cuard [...]
vouloir.tr: For all God's gold he would not be a coward [...]

vouloir.of: De chrestiens voelt faire male vode.
vouloir.tr: Of Christians he wishes to make an evil massacre.

vouloir.of: «Mis parrastre est, ne voeill que mot en suns.»
vouloir.tr: «He is my stepfather, I do not wish that you say a word of it.»

vouloir.of: Melz voeill murir que huntage me venget.
vouloir.tr: I would rather die than that shame befall me.

vouloir.of: Ne traïsun unkes amer ne volt.
vouloir.tr: Nor did he ever wish to love treason.

vouloir.of: Suz ciel n'at hume que [tant] voeillet haïr;
vouloir.tr: Under heaven there is no man he would so wish to hate;

vouloir.of: Voillet o nun, tut i laisset sun tens.
vouloir.tr: Willing or not, each leaves his life there.

vouloir.of: Fuïr s'en voel, mais ne li valt nient:
vouloir.tr: He wishes to flee from it, but it avails him nothing:

vouloir.of: Voelent u nun, si guerpissent le camp.
vouloir.tr: Willing or not, they abandon the field.

vouloir.of: «Sire cumpaign, sel volez otrier,
vouloir.tr: «Lord companion, if you will grant it,

vouloir.of: Mielz voeill murir que hunte nus seit retraite.» AOI.
vouloir.tr: I would rather die than that shame be reported of us.» AOI.

vouloir.of: Jamais n'iert home plus se voeillet venger.
vouloir.tr: Never will a man be more eager to take revenge.

vouloir.of: L'enseigne Carle n'i volt mie ublier:
vouloir.tr: Charles's battle-cry he does not wish to forget:

vouloir.of: Voeillet (illi) o nun, desuz cez vals s'en fuit,
vouloir.tr: Whether he will or not, he flees down below these valleys,

vouloir.of: Li uns ne volt l'altre nient laisser.
vouloir.tr: Not one of them is willing to abandon the other.

vouloir.of: Mais saveir volt se Charles i vendrat:
vouloir.tr: But he wants to know whether Charles will come:

vouloir.of: Ki estre i voelt isnelement chevalzt!
vouloir.tr: Whoever wants to be there, ride swiftly!

vouloir.of: Voellet o nun, remes i est a piet.
vouloir.tr: Whether he will or not, he is left there on foot.

vouloir.of: Joes voell aler querre e entercer,
vouloir.tr: I want to go seek them out and gather them,

vouloir.of: Voeillet o nun, a tere chet pasmet.
vouloir.tr: Whether he will or no, he falls to the ground in a swoon.

vouloir.of: Aler i volt, sin durrat a Rollant.
vouloir.tr: He wants to go there, and will give some to Roland.

vouloir.of: Tient l'olifan, que unkes perdre ne volt,
vouloir.tr: He holds the oliphant, which he never wished to lose,

vouloir.of: Mielz voeill murir qu'entre paiens remaigne.
vouloir.tr: I would rather die than have it remain among pagans.

vouloir.of: Pur ço l'at fait que il voelt veirement
vouloir.tr: He has done this because he truly wants

vouloir.of: Mais lui meïsme ne volt mettre en ubli,
vouloir.tr: But he will not put himself into oblivion either,

vouloir.of: Josque Deus voeil[l]e que en cest camp revengum.»
vouloir.tr: Until God wishes that we come back to this field.»

vouloir.of: Icele noit ne se volt il desarmer,
vouloir.tr: That night he does not wish to disarm,

vouloir.of: Ki herbe voelt, il la prent en gisant.
vouloir.tr: Whoever wants grass takes it lying down.

vouloir.of: Urs e leuparz les voelent puis manger,
vouloir.tr: Bears and leopards then want to devour them,

vouloir.of: Aler i volt, mais il ad desturber.
vouloir.tr: He wants to go there, but he is hindered.

vouloir.of: A Charlemagne se vuldrat acorder.
vouloir.tr: And will wish to come to terms with Charlemagne.

vouloir.of: Gent paienor ne voelent cesser unkes:
vouloir.tr: The pagan people never wish to rest:

vouloir.of: En France dulce le voeil aler querant.
vouloir.tr: Into sweet France I mean to go seeking him.

vouloir.of: Meilz voel murir que ja fuiet de camp;
vouloir.tr: He would rather die than ever flee from the field;

vouloir.of: Quite li cleim, se il la voelt aveir,
vouloir.tr: I declare it free to him, if he wishes to have it,

vouloir.of: Si s'en vuolt en dulce France aler.
vouloir.tr: He wanted to go away to sweet France.

vouloir.of: Se vos volez, li repaires ert grefs.»
vouloir.tr: That, if you wish, their return will be hard.»

vouloir.of: Pur mun nev[ol]d que vuldreie truver.
vouloir.tr: To find my nephew, whom I would wish to find.

vouloir.of: Si grant doel ai que jo ne vuldreie estre!»
vouloir.tr: I have such great grief that I would not wish to be!»

vouloir.of: Si grant dol ai que ne voldreie vivre,
vouloir.tr: I have such great grief that I would not wish to live,

vouloir.of: Venir s'en volt li emperere Carles,
vouloir.tr: Emperor Charles wants to be on his way,

vouloir.of: Li amiralz ne se voelt demurer:
vouloir.tr: The emir does not wish to delay:

vouloir.of: Voeillet o nun, n'i perdet sun edet.
vouloir.tr: Whether he wishes it or not, does not lose his years there.

vouloir.of: Ço est une gent ki unches ben ne volt. AOI.
vouloir.tr: It is a people that never wished any good. AOI.

vouloir.of: «Ki par noz Deus voelt aveir guarison,
vouloir.tr: «Whoever wants to have healing through our gods,

vouloir.of: Mais des meillors voeill jo retenir treis:
vouloir.tr: But I want to keep three of the best:

vouloir.of: Ki errer voelt, a mei venir s'en alt!»
vouloir.tr: Whoever wishes to ride, let him come to me!»

vouloir.of: Bataille veit cil ki entr'els volt estre. AOI.
vouloir.tr: He sees battle who wishes to be among them. AOI.

vouloir.of: Cument qu'il seit, ne s'i voelt celer mie.
vouloir.tr: Whatever may happen, he does not wish to hide at all.

vouloir.of: Deven mes hom, en fedeltet voeill rendre;
vouloir.tr: Become my man, I wish you to pay homage;

vouloir.of: Mais Deus ne volt qu'il seit mort ne vencut.
vouloir.tr: But God does not wish him to be dead or conquered.

vouloir.of: Paien s'en turnent, ne volt Deus qu'il i remainent.
vouloir.tr: The pagans go away; God does not wish them to stay there.

vouloir.of: Paien s'en fuient, cum Damnesdeus le volt.
vouloir.tr: The pagans flee, as the Lord God wills.

vouloir.of: Li reis creit en Deu, faire voelt sun servise;
vouloir.tr: The king believes in God, wishes to do his service;

vouloir.of: S'or i ad cel qui Carles cuntredie voillet,
vouloir.tr: If there is anyone there who wishes to oppose Charles,

vouloir.of: Ço voelt li reis par amur cunvertisset.
vouloir.tr: That is the king's wish, that she be converted through love.

vouloir.of: Entresqu'a Ais ne volt prendre sujurn.
vouloir.tr: As far as Aix he does not want to take any rest.

vouloir.of: Se or ad parent ki m'en voeille desmentir,
vouloir.tr: If now he has a kinsman who wishes to give me the lie on it,

vouloir.of: Mun jugement voel sempres guarantir.»
vouloir.tr: I will at once warrant my judgment.»

vouloir.of: Sustenir voeill trestut mun parentet;
vouloir.tr: I want to uphold all my kindred;

vouloir.of: Mielz voeill murir que il me seit reprovet.»
vouloir.tr: I would rather die than have it reproached to me.»

vouloir.of: Creire voelt Deu, chrestientet demandet.
vouloir.tr: She wishes to believe in God, she asks for Christianity.

vouloir.of: Li emperere n'i volsist aler mie:
vouloir.tr: The emperor would not at all wish to go:

vêtir.of: Vint i ses nies, out vestue sa brunie,
vêtir.tr: His nephew came, had donned his hauberk,

vêtir.of: Halbercs vestuz e tres bien fermeez
vêtir.tr: hauberks donned and very well fastened,

vêtir.of: Helmes laciez e blancs osbercs vestuz
vêtir.tr: helmets laced on and white hauberks donned.

vêtir.of: Si ad vestut sun blanc osberc sasfret,
vêtir.tr: And so he has put on his white hauberk, saffron-bright,
Swiftly he has put on his hauberk,

vêtir.of: Helmes laciez e vestues lor bronies;
vêtir.tr: Helmets laced and their hauberks put on;

vêtir.of: Osbercs vestuz e lur brunies dubleines,
vêtir.tr: Hauberks put on and their double mail-coats,

vêtir.of: Vest une bronie dunt li pan sunt sasfret,
vêtir.tr: He puts on a hauberk whose skirts are set with gold,

vêtir.of: Ne il n'en fut ne vestut ne saisit.
vêtir.tr: And was never invested with it nor given possession of it.

vêtir.of: Meillor vassal de lui ne vestit bronie.
vêtir.tr: No better vassal than he ever put on a hauberk.

vêtir.of: Vestent osberc blancs e forz e legers,
vêtir.tr: They put on hauberks, white and strong and light,

ébaudir.of: A icest mot si s'esbaldissent Franc,
ébaudir.tr: At this word the Franks take heart,

échapper.of: Se uns escapet, morz ies e cunfunduz.»
échapper.tr: If one escapes, you are dead and ruined.»

éclaircir.of: Cele nel veit vers lui ne s'esclargisset;
éclaircir.tr: None sees him but she brightens toward him;

éclaircir.of: Esclargiz est li vespres e li jurz.
éclaircir.tr: The evening and the day grow bright.

éclaircir.of: Si esclargiez voz talenz e voz coers,
éclaircir.tr: And clear your minds and your hearts,

éclaircir.of: «E! Deus,» dist Carles, «le dreit en esclargiez!»
éclaircir.tr: «Ah! God,» says Charles, «make the right clear!»

éclaircir.of: E esclargiez est la sue grant ire,
éclaircir.tr: And his great anger is cleared,

éclairer.of: Que jo n'esclair ceste meie grant ire.»
éclairer.tr: To relieve this great wrath of mine.»

éclairer.of: Par main en l'albe, si cum li jurz esclairet,
éclairer.tr: At morning, in the dawn, as the day grows bright,

éclairer.of: Tut li païs en reluist e esclairet.
éclairer.tr: The whole country shines and is lit by it.

éclairer.of: E l'olifan, ki tres(tu)tuz les esclairet.
éclairer.tr: And the oliphant, which rings out above them all.

éclisser.of: La hanste briset e esclicet josqu'as poinz.
éclisser.tr: His lance breaks and splinters all the way to his fists.

écouter.of: Messe e matines ad li reis escultet.
écouter.tr: Mass and matins the king has heard.

écouter.of: Vos le doüssez esculter e oïr.»
écouter.tr: You ought to have listened to him and heard him out.»

écouter.of: Messe e matines ad li reis escultet.
écouter.tr: Mass and matins has the king heard.

écouter.of: Naimes li duc l'oïd, si l'escultent li Franc.
écouter.tr: Naimes the duke heard it, and the Franks listen to it.
The emperor stood still and listened:

écrier.of: Devant Marsilie cil s'escriet mult halt:
écrier.tr: Before Marsile he cries out very loudly:

écrier.of: Devant Marsilie cil en est escriet:
écrier.tr: Before Marsile this man cries out:

écrier.of: Devant Marsilie s'escriet en la presse,
écrier.tr: Before Marsile he cries out in the throng,

écrier.of: Vint en la presse, sur les altres s'escriet
écrier.tr: He came into the throng, above the others he cries out

écrier.of: Franceis escriet, Oliver apelat:
écrier.tr: He calls out to the French, he addressed Oliver:

écrier.of: A icest mot sunt Franceis escriet.
écrier.tr: At this word the Franks cried out.

écrier.of: E se s'escriet l'enseigne paienor;
écrier.tr: And cries out the pagan war-cry;

écrier.of: - «Munjoie!» escriet, ço est l'enseigne Carlun. AOI.
écrier.tr: - «Monjoie!» he cries, that is Charles's war-cry. AOI.

écrier.of: - «Munjoie!» escriet por le camp retenir.
écrier.tr: - «Munjoie!» he cries out, to hold the field.

écrier.of: - «Munjoie!» escriet, ço est l'enseigne Carle. AOI.
écrier.tr: - «Munjoie!» he cries, that is Charles's battle-cry. AOI.

écrier.of: De tutes parz est «Munjo[i]e» escriee. AOI.
écrier.tr: On all sides «Munjoie» is cried. AOI.

écrier.of: Apres escriet: «Cist sunt bon a (o)[c]unfundre!
écrier.tr: Then he cries out: «These are good to destroy!

écrier.of: A voiz escriet: «Ferez i, chevaler!» AOI.
écrier.tr: In a loud voice he cries out: «Strike here, knights!» AOI.

écrier.of: Paien escrient: «Aíe nos, Mahum!
écrier.tr: The pagans cry out: «Help us, Mahomet!

écrier.of: Puis escrient l'enseigne paenime.
écrier.tr: Then they shout the pagan battle cry.

écrier.of: Apres escriet Rollant qu'il li aiut. AOI.
écrier.tr: Afterward he cries out to Roland to help him. AOI.

écrier.of: «Munjoie!» escriet e haltement e cler.
écrier.tr: «Munjoie!» he cries out both loudly and clearly.

écrier.of: Grant est la noise de «Munjoie!» escrier.
écrier.tr: Great is the noise of the shouting of «Munjoie!»

écrier.of: Carles escriet: «U estes vos, bels nies?
